In manuscript no. 100 (Tafsir), they are undotted.]] that Maksalmina, Mahsalmina, Yamlikha, Marutunus, Kasatunus, Yabur, Yakrunus, Yatbiyunus and Qalush were young men who had fled from their king Daqyanus, the tyrant, for fear that he would tempt them away from their religion. They entered this cave, and when their whereabouts were reported, he ordered that the cave be sealed up against them with stones. We have written down their situation and the account of their news, so that whoever comes after them may know of it, should they be discovered.

When they had read it, they were astonished and praised God, who had shown them a sign of the Resurrection among them. Then they raised their voices in praise and glorification of God. Then they entered upon the young men in the cave and found them sitting in its midst, their faces radiant, their clothes not worn out. Ariyus and his companions fell prostrate and praised God, who had shown them one of His signs. Then they spoke to one another, and the young men informed them about what they had suffered from their king Daqyanus, that tyrant from whom they had fled.

Then Ariyus and his companions sent a messenger to their righteous king Tidhusiyus, saying: "Hasten, perhaps you will look upon one of the signs of God, which God has placed in your kingdom and made a sign for the worlds, to be a light and a radiance for them, and a confirmation of the Resurrection. So come quickly to young men whom God has raised up, though He had caused them to die more than three hundred years ago." When the news reached King Tidhusiyus, he rose from the seat on which he had been sitting, his mind and reason returned to him, his anxiety left him, and he turned back to God, the Mighty and Majestic, and said: "O God, I praise You, Lord of the heavens and the earth. I worship You, I praise You, and I glorify You. You have been gracious to me and shown me mercy by Your mercy, and You have not extinguished the light which You placed for my forefathers and for the righteous servant, King Qastantinus." When the people of the city were informed, they rode out to him and went with him until they came to the city of Afsus. The people of the city met them, and they went with him until they climbed toward the cave and came to it. When the young men saw Tidhusiyus, they rejoiced at him and fell prostrate on their faces. Tidhusiyus stood before them, then embraced them and wept, while they sat before him on the ground, glorifying God and praising Him. And he said: "By God, I can liken you to nothing but the disciples when they saw the Messiah." And he said: "May God relieve you, as if you were those who are called and then gathered from the graves." Then the young men said to Tidhusiyus: "We bid you farewell. Peace be upon you and the mercy of God. May God protect you and protect your kingdom in peace. We seek refuge for you in God from the evil of the jinn and of men."

[[The passage from his saying "Then he ordered a food of khalar and nashil..." up to here is omitted from this report in ʿAra'is al-Majalis of the exegete al-Tha'labi, p. 427: "Al-khalar: a grain eaten as food, said to be the chickpea. Al-nashil: milk in the hour it is milked." The passage appears, from what is evident, to be part of the speech of the Companions of the Cave.]] "Then he ordered a food of khalar and nashil, for the worst thing that enters a person's belly is that he should know nothing, except a dignity if he is honoured by it, or a humiliation if he is humiliated by it."

While the king was standing, they returned to their resting places, lay down, and God took their souls by His command. The king approached them, placed his garments over them, and ordered that a coffin of gold be made for each man among them. When evening came and he slept, they came to him in a dream and said: "We were not created from gold or silver, but we were created from dust, and to dust we shall return. So leave us as we were in the cave, on the dust, until God raises us from it." Then the king ordered a coffin of teak, and they were placed in it. God veiled them with awe when they left from among them, so no one could approach them. The king ordered that their cave be made a mosque in which to pray, and he made for them a great festival, and ordered that people come to it every year. This is the account of the Companions of the Cave.

◆ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: God raised them up — meaning the young men, the Companions of the Cave — when a Muslim king had come to rule over them, meaning over the people of their city. God had caused hunger to afflict the young men. Then one of them said: ﴿How long have you remained?﴾ They said: ﴿We have remained a day or part of a day.﴾ He said: They referred the knowledge of that to God. ﴿Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with this silver of yours to the city﴾, and they had with them silver coins struck in the reign of the king of their time, ﴿and let him bring you a provision from it﴾, meaning food, ﴿and let him not alert anyone to you.﴾ So one of them went out and saw the landmarks had changed until he reached the city. People greeted him, and he did not recognise any of them, so he went out while they did not recognise him, until he came to the food seller and bought food from him. The food seller said: "Give me your silver." So he brought out the silver to him. He said: "From where do you have this silver?" He said: "This is our silver and the silver of the people of our land." He said: "Impossible! This silver was struck by so-and-so, son of so-and-so, three hundred and nine years ago. You have found a treasure, and I shall not leave you until I bring you before the king." So he brought him before the king, and the king was a Muslim, and his companions were Muslims. He rejoiced and was delighted, revealed his affair to them, and informed them of the news of his companions. Then they sent for the tablet in the treasury, brought it, and it agreed with what had been described of their affair. The polytheists said: "We have a better claim to them, these are the sons of our fathers." The Muslims said: "We have a better claim to them; they are Muslims from among us." So they went with him to the cave. When they reached the mouth of the cave he said: "Let me enter upon my companions first, so that I may bring them good news, for if they see you with me they will terrify them." He entered and gave them good news, and God took their souls. He said: God blinded them to their place, so they could not find it. The polytheists said: "We shall build a structure over them, for they are the sons of our fathers, and we shall worship God in it." The Muslims said: "We have a better claim to them; they are of us. We shall build a mosque over them in which to pray and worship God."

The most correct opinion, in my view, concerning this is the statement of the one who said: God, exalted is He, raised them from their sleep so that they might question one another among themselves, as we have explained before, because God, mighty is His remembrance, informed His servants of this in His Book. God caused the people whom He caused to find them to find them, so that it would be confirmed to them, by God's raising these young men from their sleep after its long duration, in the same form they had been on the day they slept, their hair not whitened over the passing of days and nights, nor did they grow old over the course of ages and times, that God has power to raise whom He caused to die in this world from his grave to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection. For God, mighty is His remembrance, has informed us of this, saying: ﴿And thus We caused them to be found, so that they would know that the promise of God is true and that the Hour is not in doubt.﴾

The reciters differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿so send one of you with this silver of yours﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina, and some of the Iraqis, recited ﴿بِوَرِقِكُمْ﴾ (biwariqikum) with a fatha on the waw and a kasra on the ra and the qaf. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra recited ﴿بَورْقِكُمْ﴾ (bawriqikum) with a sukun on the ra and a kasra on the qaf. Some of the Meccans recited it with a kasra on the ra and the qaf assimilated into the kaf. All these readings have the same meaning, though their wording differs, and they are well-known dialects of the speech of the Arabs. However, the original form is with a fatha on the waw and a kasra on the ra and the qaf, because it is al-warq (the silver), and whatever else differs from it has entered upon it the desire for lightening. There is also another dialect, al-warq (وَرْق), just as they say kabid (كَبِد) for kabd (كَبْد) for the liver. When this is the original, recitation with it is more pleasing to me, without the other two being rejected as to their soundness. We have mentioned the report that the one who was sent with the silver to the city was named Yamlikha.

Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri related to me, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Muqatil: ﴿so send one of you with this silver of yours﴾: his name was Yamlikh.

As for His words: ﴿let him see which of them has the best food﴾, the people of ta'wil (exegesis, the interpretation of meaning) differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is, let him see which of the people of the city has more food.

Mention of those who said this:
◆ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Husayn, from Ikrima, concerning ﴿which of them is purer in food﴾: more.
◆ And al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Husayn, from Ikrima, the like of it, except that he said: ﴿أيُّهُ أكْثَرُ﴾ (ayyuhu aktharu).

Others said: rather, its meaning is: which of them is more lawful as food.

Mention of those who said this:
◆ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿which of them is purer in food﴾: more lawful.
◆ al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: which of them is better as food.

Mention of those who said this:
◆ al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Mu'ammar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His words: ﴿purer in food﴾: better in food.

The most correct opinion in my view, concerning this, is the statement of the one who said: the meaning of that is: more lawful and purer. This is because there is no sense in choosing the one with more food to buy from, unless it means that when he has more food, the better of it is more likely to be found with him. And if the one sent is required to buy from the seller of the better food, then he has been commanded to buy what is good, whether what the buyer has of that is little or much. Those who understood the interpretation of "purer" as "more" did so because they found the Arabs say: the wealth of so-and-so has zaka (زكا), meaning it has increased, and as the poet said:

"Our tribes are seven, and you are three,
and the seven are purer (azka) and better than three."

[[The verse is by al-Qital al-Kilabi. Sibawayh cited it in (al-Kitab 2: 181), and it is among the witnesses of Abu Ubayda in (Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 237, 397). In the second place he said: "ayyuha azka ta'aman" means "more." He said: "Our tribes are seven..." (the verse). In the first place he said: he mentioned "thalatha" (three) by taking it to mean "a clan," then made it feminine, because he took it to mean a tribe. I say: The grammarians permit both masculine and feminine for numerals when the counted noun is not mentioned, and this is evidence for that. In (Lisan al-Arab: zaka), al-zaka' (with mad) means growth and increase; zaka yazku zaka'an and zakwan.]]

in the sense of "more." Even so, lawful good food, however little, is more than unlawful wicked food, however much. It has been said that His words: ﴿let him see which of them﴾ are linked to the pronoun of the city, and what is meant is its people, for the sense of the speech is: let him see which of its people has purer food, since the hearer knows what is intended by the speech. It may also be that by His words ﴿which of them is purer in food﴾ they meant: which of them is more lawful, because they had left their people, who were idol worshippers, and so they did not consider it permissible to eat their slaughter.

* *

As for His words: ﴿let him bring you a provision from it﴾:
He says: let him bring you food from it, a sustenance on which you may live and which you may eat.
As:
◆ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr: ﴿let him bring you a provision from it﴾: food.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and let him be discreet﴾:
He says: let him be gentle in what he buys, in his route, and in his entering the city. ﴿and let him not alert anyone to you﴾: He says: let him not let anyone among the people know of you.

As for His words: ﴿for if they discover you, they will stone you﴾: by this they mean Daqyanus and his companions. They said: if Daqyanus and his companions discover you, and learn your whereabouts, they will stone you, meaning, they will abuse you with words.
As:
◆ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words: ﴿for if they discover you, they will stone you﴾: he said: they will revile you with words, and harm you.

* *

As for His words: ﴿or return you to their religion﴾:
He says: or they will send you back to their religion, so that you become unbelievers by worshipping idols.
﴿and then you will never succeed⁠—ever﴾: He says: you will never attain success, which is lasting survival and eternity in the Gardens. Then: that is, if you return to their religion forever, for the days of your lives.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 18, verse 21:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We caused them to be found, that they might know that the promise of Allah is true and that the Hour, there is no doubt about it. When they disputed among themselves over their affair, and said, "Construct over them a building; their Lord knows best about them." Those who prevailed in their affair said, "We will surely take over them a place of worship."﴾

He, dhikruhu, says: Just as We raised them after their long sleep, in the same state they were in the hour they slept, so that they might question one another and thereby increase in insight into the great authority of Allah, and in knowledge of Allah's excellent defence of His friends. ﴿And thus We caused them to be found﴾ means: thus We made the other group aware of them, the people who had been in doubt about Allah's power to revive the dead and in disbelief about the re-creation of His creatures' bodies, in the state they were in the day He took them, after decay, so that they would know that the promise of Allah is true, and be certain that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And thus We caused them to be found﴾, he said: We made them aware of them, so that whoever denied this account would know that the promise of Allah is true, and that the Hour, there is no doubt about it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿When they disputed among themselves over their affair﴾

It means: those who came upon the youths. He, exalted is He, says: Thus We made these people who differed about the establishment of the Hour and Allah's reviving of the dead after their death, from the people of Tadhusis, come upon them, when they disputed among themselves over their affair, regarding what Allah would do with those whom He had annihilated of His servants, when He had worn them away in their graves after their death, whether He would re-create them or not. And as for His words: "they said, 'Construct over them a building'," it means: those whom We made to come upon the companions of the cave said, "Construct over them a building." ﴿Their Lord knows best about them﴾ means: the Lord of the youths knows best about the youths and their state. As for His words: ﴿Those who prevailed in their affair said﴾, He, majestic is His praise, says: the people who prevailed over the affair of the companions of the cave said, ﴿We will surely take over them a place of worship.﴾

There has been disagreement about the speakers of this statement: were they the Muslim group, or were they the disbelievers? We have mentioned some of that earlier, and we will mention, God willing, what has not yet passed of it.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Those who prevailed in their affair said, "We will surely take over them a place of worship."﴾ He said: he meant their enemy.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Allah blinded those who came upon the companions of the cave in their place, so they were not guided. The polytheists said, "We will build over them a building, for they are the sons of our fathers, and we will worship Allah in it." And the Muslims said, "Rather, we have more right to them; they are of us. We will build over them a mosque in which we will pray and worship Allah."

Interpretation of the words of the Most High: ﴿They will say, "They were three, the fourth of them their dog," and they will say, "They were five, the sixth of them their dog," guessing at the unseen. And they will say, "They were seven, and the eighth of them their dog." Say, "My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few." So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument, and do not consult any of them about them. (22) And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," (23)﴾

The Most High says: Some of those who dispute about the matter of the youths of the Cave will say, "They were three, the fourth of them their dog," and some of them will say, "They were five, the sixth of them their dog," ﴿guessing at the unseen﴾: that is, casting (qadhfan) by conjecture (bi-al-zann) without certain knowledge, as the poet said:

"And I make the truth an unseen thing, cast (murajjaman)"

[This is the second half of a line whose speaker I have not been able to identify. It is evidence that the meaning of rajm is: speaking by conjecture without certain knowledge. Abu 'Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an (1: 398): "'Rajman bil-ghayb': rajm is what you are not certain of. He said: a 'murajjam' opinion: one does not know whether it is true or false." Zuhayr said: "And war is nothing but what you have seen and tasted, and it is not, concerning it, a murajjam (conjectural) report." (And in Lisan al-'Arab, under r-j-m:) rajm is speaking by conjecture and guesswork.]

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: ﴿They will say, "They were three, the fourth of them their dog," and they will say, "They were five, the sixth of them their dog," guessing at the unseen﴾: that is, casting (qadhfan) at the unseen.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: ﴿guessing at the unseen﴾, he said: casting by conjecture.

* *

And his words: ﴿and they will say, "They were seven, and the eighth of them their dog."﴾

That is: and some of them will say, "They were seven, and the eighth of them their dog."

﴿Say, "My Lord knows best their number."﴾ The Mighty and Majestic says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to those who utter these statements about the number of the youths of the Cave, guessing at the unseen: ﴿My Lord knows best their number; none knows them﴾, that is: none knows their number ﴿except a few﴾ of His creation.

As:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿none knows them except a few﴾, he said: a few of the people.

Others said: rather, by "the few" he meant the People of the Book.

Those who said so:

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿none knows them except a few﴾, he said: he means the People of the Book. Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "I am among those whom God excepted," and he would say: "Their number is seven."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Isra'il told us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿none knows them except a few﴾, he said: "I am among the few; they were seven."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: it was related to us that Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "I am among those few whom God excepted; they were seven, and the eighth of them their dog."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Their number is seven, and the eighth of them is their dog, and I am among those whom God excepted."

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: ﴿none knows them except a few﴾, he said: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "I am among the few; they were seven, and the eighth of them their dog."

* *

And his words: ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾

The Mighty and Majestic says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: So do not argue, O Muhammad: that is, do not dispute with the People of the Book concerning them, meaning concerning the number of the People of the Cave. The number has been omitted, being sufficient with the mention of them, since the hearers know what is meant.

Ahl al-ta'wil said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿So do not argue concerning them﴾: do not argue about their number.

* *

And his words: ﴿except with an outward argument﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the "outward argument" that God excepted and permitted to His Prophet ﷺ. Some of them said: it is what God recounted in His Book, which he was permitted to recite to them, and he should not argue with them by anything other than that.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾: that is, let what I have recounted to you suffice; do not argue about them.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾: that is, except with what we have made manifest to you of their affair.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding his words ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾: that is, what we have recounted to you of their affair suffices you.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So do not argue concerning them﴾, he said: what we have recounted to you of their affair suffices you.

- It was related from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding his words ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾: that is, what we have recounted to you suffices you.

Others said: the outward argument is that he says, "It is not as you say," and similar speech.

Those who said so:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding his words ﴿except with an outward argument﴾: that he says to them, "It is not as you say; you do not know their number. If they say such and such, then say, 'It is not so,' for they do not know their number." And he recited "They will say, 'They were three, the fourth of them their dog'" until he reached ﴿guessing at the unseen﴾.

* *

And his words: ﴿and do not consult any of them about them﴾

The Most High says: and do not seek a ruling (istift'a) concerning the number of the youths of the Cave from any of them, meaning from the People of the Book, because they do not know their number; they only speak about them by guesswork, not by certain speech.

Ahl al-ta'wil said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Isa told us, from Sufyan, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words ﴿and do not consult any of them about them﴾, he said: they are the People of the Book.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and do not consult any of them about them﴾: from the Jews.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and do not consult any of them﴾: from the Jews. He said: and do not ask the Jews about the affair of the People of the Cave, except what I have already informed you of their affair.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and do not consult any of them about them﴾: from the People of the Book. We used to narrate that they were the sons of al-Rukna [[al-Rukna: thus with the short vowel, and perhaps its original form is al-Ruknā with the long vowel, plural of rakin, meaning a man who is dignified and steady, or strong through his clan and its numbers.]], and al-Rukna were the kings of Rome. God granted them Islam, so they set themselves apart in their religion and withdrew from their people until they reached the Cave, and God struck upon their ears, and they remained a long age until their nation perished and a Muslim nation came after them, and their king was a Muslim.

Interpretation of the words of the Most High: ﴿They will say, "They were three, the fourth of them their dog," and they will say, "They were five, the sixth of them their dog," guessing at the unseen. And they will say, "They were seven, and the eighth of them their dog." Say, "My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few." So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument, and do not consult any of them about them. (22) And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," (23)﴾

The Most High says: Some of those who dispute about the matter of the youths of the Cave will say, "They were three, the fourth of them their dog," and some of them will say, "They were five, the sixth of them their dog," ﴿guessing at the unseen﴾: that is, casting (qadhfan) by conjecture (bi-al-zann) without certain knowledge, as the poet said:

"And I make the truth an unseen thing, cast (murajjaman)"

[This is the second half of a line whose speaker I have not been able to identify. It is evidence that the meaning of rajm is: speaking by conjecture without certain knowledge. Abu 'Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an (1: 398): "'Rajman bil-ghayb': rajm is what you are not certain of. He said: a 'murajjam' opinion: one does not know whether it is true or false." Zuhayr said: "And war is nothing but what you have seen and tasted, and it is not, concerning it, a murajjam (conjectural) report." (And in Lisan al-'Arab, under r-j-m:) rajm is speaking by conjecture and guesswork.]

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: ﴿They will say, "They were three, the fourth of them their dog," and they will say, "They were five, the sixth of them their dog," guessing at the unseen﴾: that is, casting (qadhfan) at the unseen.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: ﴿guessing at the unseen﴾, he said: casting by conjecture.

* *

And his words: ﴿and they will say, "They were seven, and the eighth of them their dog."﴾

That is: and some of them will say, "They were seven, and the eighth of them their dog."

﴿Say, "My Lord knows best their number."﴾ The Mighty and Majestic says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to those who utter these statements about the number of the youths of the Cave, guessing at the unseen: ﴿My Lord knows best their number; none knows them﴾, that is: none knows their number ﴿except a few﴾ of His creation.

As:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿none knows them except a few﴾, he said: a few of the people.

Others said: rather, by "the few" he meant the People of the Book.

Those who said so:

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿none knows them except a few﴾, he said: he means the People of the Book. Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "I am among those whom God excepted," and he would say: "Their number is seven."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Isra'il told us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿none knows them except a few﴾, he said: "I am among the few; they were seven."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: it was related to us that Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "I am among those few whom God excepted; they were seven, and the eighth of them their dog."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Their number is seven, and the eighth of them is their dog, and I am among those whom God excepted."

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: ﴿none knows them except a few﴾, he said: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "I am among the few; they were seven, and the eighth of them their dog."

* *

And his words: ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾

The Mighty and Majestic says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: So do not argue, O Muhammad: that is, do not dispute with the People of the Book concerning them, meaning concerning the number of the People of the Cave. The number has been omitted, being sufficient with the mention of them, since the hearers know what is meant.

Ahl al-ta'wil said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿So do not argue concerning them﴾: do not argue about their number.

* *

And his words: ﴿except with an outward argument﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the "outward argument" that God excepted and permitted to His Prophet ﷺ. Some of them said: it is what God recounted in His Book, which he was permitted to recite to them, and he should not argue with them by anything other than that.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾: that is, let what I have recounted to you suffice; do not argue about them.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾: that is, except with what we have made manifest to you of their affair.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding his words ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾: that is, what we have recounted to you of their affair suffices you.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So do not argue concerning them﴾, he said: what we have recounted to you of their affair suffices you.

- It was related from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding his words ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾: that is, what we have recounted to you suffices you.

Others said: the outward argument is that he says, "It is not as you say," and similar speech.

Those who said so:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding his words ﴿except with an outward argument﴾: that he says to them, "It is not as you say; you do not know their number. If they say such and such, then say, 'It is not so,' for they do not know their number." And he recited "They will say, 'They were three, the fourth of them their dog'" until he reached ﴿guessing at the unseen﴾.

* *

And his words: ﴿and do not consult any of them about them﴾

The Most High says: and do not seek a ruling (istift'a) concerning the number of the youths of the Cave from any of them, meaning from the People of the Book, because they do not know their number; they only speak about them by guesswork, not by certain speech.

Ahl al-ta'wil said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Isa told us, from Sufyan, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words ﴿and do not consult any of them about them﴾, he said: they are the People of the Book.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and do not consult any of them about them﴾: from the Jews.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and do not consult any of them﴾: from the Jews. He said: and do not ask the Jews about the affair of the People of the Cave, except what I have already informed you of their affair.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and do not consult any of them about them﴾: from the People of the Book. We used to narrate that they were the sons of al-Rukna [[al-Rukna: thus with the short vowel, and perhaps its original form is al-Ruknā with the long vowel, plural of rakin, meaning a man who is dignified and steady, or strong through his clan and its numbers.]], and al-Rukna were the kings of Rome. God granted them Islam, so they set themselves apart in their religion and withdrew from their people until they reached the Cave, and God struck upon their ears, and they remained a long age until their nation perished and a Muslim nation came after them, and their king was a Muslim.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 24:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except [by adding] "If Allah wills." And remember your Lord when you forget and say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right guidance."﴾

This is a discipline from Allah, mighty is His remembrance, to His Prophet ﷺ, whom He charged not to affirm with certainty concerning any matter that may occur that it will certainly come to pass, unless he attaches it to the will of Allah, because nothing happens except by the will of Allah.

It was said to him this, as we have been informed, because he had promised those who asked him about the three questions we have mentioned earlier (one of which was the question about the youths of the Cave) that he would answer them the next day, and he did not add the exception. Revelation was therefore withheld from him, it is said, for fifteen [nights] because of that, until its delay grieved him. Then Allah sent down to him the answer to them, and informed His Prophet of the reason revelation had been withheld from him, and taught him what he should adopt in his promises and in his reports of matters that will occur, of which no revelation from Allah has come to him. So He said: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow"﴾ O Muhammad, as you said to those who asked you about the matter of the People of the Cave, and the questions they asked you, "I will tell you about them tomorrow," ﴿except [by adding] "If Allah wills."﴾ The meaning of the statement is: except that you say with it, "If Allah wills," so the verb "say" is omitted, being sufficiently indicated by what is mentioned, since the context points to it. Some of the scholars of Arabic said that it is permissible that the meaning of His saying ﴿except [by adding] "If Allah wills"﴾ is an exception from the saying, not from the act, as if its meaning for him were: "Do not say a saying except that Allah wills that saying." But this is a far-fetched meaning from the apparent sense of the revelation, and it contradicts the interpretation of the commentators.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾

The commentators differed about its meaning. Some of them said: "And make the exception in your oath when you recall that you forgot it at the time of the oath."

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Harun al-Harbi narrated to us, saying: Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the man who swears: he said, "Let him make the exception, even after a year." And he would say, "And remember your Lord when you forget," in that regard. It was said to al-A'mash, "Did you hear it from Mujahid?" He said, "Laith ibn Abi Sulaym related it to me, [who] thinks it is the saying of al-Kisa'i [[The phrase "yura dhahaba al-Kisa'i hadha" is written thus in the fifteenth volume of manuscript no. 100, folio 411, and the expression is obscure; there may be a distortion in it.]]."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, concerning His saying: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow" except [by adding] "If Allah wills." And remember your Lord when you forget﴾: the exception, then when you remember, make the exception.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, concerning His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾, he said: "It has reached me that al-Hasan said: when he recalls that he did not say, 'If Allah wills,' let him say, 'If Allah wills.'"

Others said: its meaning is: "And remember your Lord when you disobey."

Those who said this:

Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from Ikrimah, concerning the saying of Allah: (And remember your Lord when you forget): he said, "Remember your Lord when you disobey."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from Ikrimah, the like of it.

The more correct of the two sayings concerning this, is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: "And remember your Lord when you abandon remembering Him," because one of the meanings of forgetting (nisyan) in the speech of the Arabs is abandoning (tark), and we have already explained this earlier.

If someone says: Is it permissible for a man to make the exception in his oath when the meaning of the statement is what you mentioned, after a period of time from the state of his swearing? It is said: Rather, the correct view is that he makes the exception even after breaking his oath, so he says, "If Allah wills," so that by his saying that he exits from what Allah obligated him in this regard through this verse, and the sin is removed from him by his leaving what he was commanded to say in this regard. As for the expiation (kaffarah), it is not removed from him in any case, unless his exception was attached to his oath.

If he says: What is the basis of the view of the one who said to him, "Let him make the exception even after a year," and the one who said, "even after a month," and the one who said, "as long as he is in his sitting"? It is said: Their meaning in this is close to our meaning, that it is permissible for him, even after ten years, and that by his exception and his saying "If Allah wills" after some time from the state of his swearing, the sin that would have been binding on him had he not said it is removed from him. As for the expiation, it is binding on him by breaking the oath in every case, unless his exception was attached to the oath. This is because we do not know of any speaker among those who said the exception may be made after a time who claims that it removes the expiation from him if he breaks the oath. In this there is the clearest evidence for the soundness of what we have said, and that the meaning of the saying in it is close to our meaning.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right guidance."﴾

Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet ﷺ: Say, "Perhaps Allah will guide me and set me on a straighter course than what I promised you and informed you would happen, if He wills."

It has been said: this is something the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to say when he forgot to make the exception in his statement, concerning a future matter, with his saying "If Allah wills," when he remembers.

Those who said this: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad, a man from the people of Kufa who used to interpret the Qur'an, and Yahya ibn Abbad used to sit with him, he said: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow" except [by adding] "If Allah wills." And remember your Lord when you forget, and say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right guidance."﴾ He said: And when a person forgets to say, "If Allah wills," his repentance from that, or its expiation, is that he says: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right guidance.﴾

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted's, Words: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾ (25) ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How clearly He sees and hears! They have no protector other than Him, and He does not make anyone a partner in His command."﴾ (26)

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾. Some of them said: this is a report from Allah, dhikruh, about the People of the Book, that they say this, and they cited as evidence for the soundness of their view His words ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾. They said: if that were a report from Allah about the exact duration of their stay in the cave, then His words ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾ would have no understandable sense, whereas Allah has informed His creation of the extent and measure of their stay in it.

Mention of those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾: "This is the statement of the People of the Book, so Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth"﴾."

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾, he said: "In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿And they said: 'They remained…'﴾ (meaning that he said: the people said), do you not see that He said: ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾."

- 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Damrah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Mutar al-Warraq, regarding the words of Allah ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years﴾, he said: "It is only something the Jews said, so Allah refuted them and said: ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾."

Others said: rather, that is a report from Allah about the exact measure of their stay in their cave.

Mention of those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾, he said: "The number of how long they remained."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it, and he added to it ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾, he said: "And nine years."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, the like of it.

- Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: al-Ajlah narrated to me, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, who said: "This verse was revealed, ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred﴾, and they said: 'Days or months or years?' So Allah revealed: ﴿three hundred years and added nine﴾."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾, he said: "Between two mountains."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The most correct of these views, in our judgement, is that it be said as Allah, exalted is His mention, said: the People of the Cave remained in their cave in slumber until Allah raised them, so that they might question one another, and until those who discovered them found them, three hundred years and nine years. This is because Allah informed of this in His Book. As for what was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, that he recited (﴿And they said: "They remained…"﴾), and the view of whoever said that it is the statement of the People of the Book, Allah has refuted that from them. Its meaning, Allah willing, is that the People of the Book said, as was reported in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that the youths, from the time they entered the cave until our day, were three hundred years and nine years. So Allah refuted that from them and informed His Prophet that this was the measure of their stay in the cave from the time they took refuge in it until He raised them so that they might question one another. Then His majesty, mention be exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad: "Allah knows best how long they remained" after He took their souls, from the time He raised them from their sleep until this day of yours; none knows that except Allah and whomever Allah has informed of it.

If someone says: what indicates that it is so? It is said: what indicates it is that He, majestic is His praise, began the report about the measure of their stay in their cave as a beginning, saying: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾, and did not place any indicator that this was a report from Him about the statement of a people who said it. It is not permissible to attribute His report about something to being a report about someone else without proof, for if that were permissible it would be permissible for all His reports, and if that were permissible for His reports, it would be permissible for the reports of others to be attributed to Him as His reports, and that is the reversal of established realities and what cannot be imagined to be sound.

If someone supposes that His words ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾ are evidence that His words ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾ are a report from Him about a people who said it, then that would have to be so only if it admitted no interpretation other than that. But since it admits of our interpretation, that its meaning is: "Say: Allah knows best how long they remained up to the day We sent down this sura," and other such meanings, it is not necessary that this be evidence that His words ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾ are a report from Allah about a people who said it. Since it is not evidence of that, and no report has come that His words ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾ are a report from Allah about a people who said it, nor has any proof been established for the soundness of that which must be accepted, what we have said is correct and what opposes it is invalid.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿three hundred years﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah and Basrah, and some of the Kufans, recited it ﴿thalātha mi'atin sinīna﴾ with tanwin on "mi'atin" (thalatha mi'atin), meaning: "and they remained in their cave, years three hundred." The majority of the readers of Kufah recited it ﴿thalātha mi'atin sinīna﴾ with the idafah of "thalatha mi'a" to "sinin," without tanwin.

The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recites ﴿thalātha mi'atin﴾ with tanwin and ﴿sinīna﴾, because the Arabs add "mi'a" (hundred) to what explains it only when its explanation comes in the singular form, as in their saying "thalatha mi'at dirham" (three hundred dirhams) and "'indī mi'at dinar" (I have a hundred dinars). That is because "mi'a" and "alf" (thousand) are large numbers, and the Arabs explain them only with what has the same meaning of large quantity, and the singular expresses the genus, whereas that is not for small numbers. Although the Arabs sometimes place a small plural in place of a large one, that is not the usual usage. But when its explanation comes in the plural form, it takes tanwin, so one says "'indī alfun darāhima" (I have a thousand dirhams) and "'indī mi'atun danānīr" (I have a hundred dinars), as I have described.

* *

His words ﴿To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾.

He, exalted is His mention, says: to Allah belongs the knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth; no knowledge of any part of it escapes Him, and nothing is hidden from Him. He says: so affirm to Him the knowledge of the measure of how long the youths stayed in the cave until this day of yours, for none knows that except the One who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and that is none but Allah, the One, the Subduer.

* *

His words ﴿How clearly He sees and hears!﴾

He says: "Clear of sight is Allah and of hearing," and that is by way of exaggeration in praise, as if it were said: how much He sees and how much He hears!

The meaning of the speech: how much Allah sees of every existing thing, and how much He hears of everything heard; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

As it was narrated:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿How clearly He sees and hears!﴾: "No one sees more than Allah or hears more, blessed and exalted!"

- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿How clearly He sees and hears! They have no protector other than Him, of any kind﴾: "He sees their deeds and hears that from them, All-Hearing, All-Seeing."

* *

His words ﴿They have no protector other than Him﴾

His majesty, mention be exalted, says: the creatures have no protector apart from their Lord who created them, who manages their affairs and their arrangement, and turns them in what they are turned.

﴿And He does not make anyone a partner in His command﴾: he says: Allah does not make anyone other than Himself a partner in His judgement and decree over His creation; rather, He alone is singular in judgement and decision concerning them, and in their management and disposal as He wills and loves.

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted's, Words: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾ (25) ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How clearly He sees and hears! They have no protector other than Him, and He does not make anyone a partner in His command."﴾ (26)

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾. Some of them said: this is a report from Allah, dhikruh, about the People of the Book, that they say this, and they cited as evidence for the soundness of their view His words ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾. They said: if that were a report from Allah about the exact duration of their stay in the cave, then His words ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾ would have no understandable sense, whereas Allah has informed His creation of the extent and measure of their stay in it.

Mention of those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾: "This is the statement of the People of the Book, so Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth"﴾."

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾, he said: "In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿And they said: 'They remained…'﴾ (meaning that he said: the people said), do you not see that He said: ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾."

- 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Damrah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Mutar al-Warraq, regarding the words of Allah ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years﴾, he said: "It is only something the Jews said, so Allah refuted them and said: ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾."

Others said: rather, that is a report from Allah about the exact measure of their stay in their cave.

Mention of those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾, he said: "The number of how long they remained."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it, and he added to it ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾, he said: "And nine years."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, the like of it.

- Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: al-Ajlah narrated to me, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, who said: "This verse was revealed, ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred﴾, and they said: 'Days or months or years?' So Allah revealed: ﴿three hundred years and added nine﴾."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾, he said: "Between two mountains."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The most correct of these views, in our judgement, is that it be said as Allah, exalted is His mention, said: the People of the Cave remained in their cave in slumber until Allah raised them, so that they might question one another, and until those who discovered them found them, three hundred years and nine years. This is because Allah informed of this in His Book. As for what was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, that he recited (﴿And they said: "They remained…"﴾), and the view of whoever said that it is the statement of the People of the Book, Allah has refuted that from them. Its meaning, Allah willing, is that the People of the Book said, as was reported in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that the youths, from the time they entered the cave until our day, were three hundred years and nine years. So Allah refuted that from them and informed His Prophet that this was the measure of their stay in the cave from the time they took refuge in it until He raised them so that they might question one another. Then His majesty, mention be exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad: "Allah knows best how long they remained" after He took their souls, from the time He raised them from their sleep until this day of yours; none knows that except Allah and whomever Allah has informed of it.

If someone says: what indicates that it is so? It is said: what indicates it is that He, majestic is His praise, began the report about the measure of their stay in their cave as a beginning, saying: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾, and did not place any indicator that this was a report from Him about the statement of a people who said it. It is not permissible to attribute His report about something to being a report about someone else without proof, for if that were permissible it would be permissible for all His reports, and if that were permissible for His reports, it would be permissible for the reports of others to be attributed to Him as His reports, and that is the reversal of established realities and what cannot be imagined to be sound.

If someone supposes that His words ﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained"﴾ are evidence that His words ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾ are a report from Him about a people who said it, then that would have to be so only if it admitted no interpretation other than that. But since it admits of our interpretation, that its meaning is: "Say: Allah knows best how long they remained up to the day We sent down this sura," and other such meanings, it is not necessary that this be evidence that His words ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾ are a report from Allah about a people who said it. Since it is not evidence of that, and no report has come that His words ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾ are a report from Allah about a people who said it, nor has any proof been established for the soundness of that which must be accepted, what we have said is correct and what opposes it is invalid.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿three hundred years﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah and Basrah, and some of the Kufans, recited it ﴿thalātha mi'atin sinīna﴾ with tanwin on "mi'atin" (thalatha mi'atin), meaning: "and they remained in their cave, years three hundred." The majority of the readers of Kufah recited it ﴿thalātha mi'atin sinīna﴾ with the idafah of "thalatha mi'a" to "sinin," without tanwin.

The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recites ﴿thalātha mi'atin﴾ with tanwin and ﴿sinīna﴾, because the Arabs add "mi'a" (hundred) to what explains it only when its explanation comes in the singular form, as in their saying "thalatha mi'at dirham" (three hundred dirhams) and "'indī mi'at dinar" (I have a hundred dinars). That is because "mi'a" and "alf" (thousand) are large numbers, and the Arabs explain them only with what has the same meaning of large quantity, and the singular expresses the genus, whereas that is not for small numbers. Although the Arabs sometimes place a small plural in place of a large one, that is not the usual usage. But when its explanation comes in the plural form, it takes tanwin, so one says "'indī alfun darāhima" (I have a thousand dirhams) and "'indī mi'atun danānīr" (I have a hundred dinars), as I have described.

* *

His words ﴿To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾.

He, exalted is His mention, says: to Allah belongs the knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth; no knowledge of any part of it escapes Him, and nothing is hidden from Him. He says: so affirm to Him the knowledge of the measure of how long the youths stayed in the cave until this day of yours, for none knows that except the One who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and that is none but Allah, the One, the Subduer.

* *

His words ﴿How clearly He sees and hears!﴾

He says: "Clear of sight is Allah and of hearing," and that is by way of exaggeration in praise, as if it were said: how much He sees and how much He hears!

The meaning of the speech: how much Allah sees of every existing thing, and how much He hears of everything heard; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

As it was narrated:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿How clearly He sees and hears!﴾: "No one sees more than Allah or hears more, blessed and exalted!"

- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿How clearly He sees and hears! They have no protector other than Him, of any kind﴾: "He sees their deeds and hears that from them, All-Hearing, All-Seeing."

* *

His words ﴿They have no protector other than Him﴾

His majesty, mention be exalted, says: the creatures have no protector apart from their Lord who created them, who manages their affairs and their arrangement, and turns them in what they are turned.

﴿And He does not make anyone a partner in His command﴾: he says: Allah does not make anyone other than Himself a partner in His judgement and decree over His creation; rather, He alone is singular in judgement and decision concerning them, and in their management and disposal as He wills and loves.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 27:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord; there is none who can alter His words, and you will not find other than Him any refuge (multahad)﴾ (18:27).

He, exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Follow, O Muhammad, what has been sent down to you of this Book of your Lord, and do not neglect its recitation, nor following what it contains of the commands and prohibitions of God, and acting upon its lawful and unlawful, lest you be among the ruined. That is because the destination of whoever opposes it and abandons following it on the Day of Resurrection is Hell. ﴿There is none who can alter His words﴾ means: there is none who can change what He has promised, through His words that He revealed to you, to the people of disobedience to Him and to those who act contrary to this Book which We revealed to you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and you will not find other than Him any refuge (multahad)﴾

It means: and if you, O Muhammad, do not recite what has been revealed to you of your Lord's Book, following it and taking it as your guide, then there will befall you the threat of God with which He threatened those who oppose His limits. You will not find, apart from God, a shelter (mawil) to turn to, nor a place of escape (ma'dal) to turn away from toward Him, because God's power encompasses you and all His creation, and none of them can flee from a matter He intends for them.

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿multahad﴾, although their wording in explaining it differs.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿multahad﴾, he said: a refuge (malja').

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿multahad﴾, he said: a refuge (malja').

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿and you will not find other than Him any refuge (multahad)﴾, he said: a shelter (mawil).

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿multahad﴾, he said: a refuge (malja') or a shelter (mawil).

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and you will not find other than Him any refuge (multahad)﴾: They will not find a place of refuge to take shelter in, nor will they find, apart from Him, a refuge or anyone to protect them. The multahad is only the mufta'al form from al-lahd (the niche), as one says of it: "I inclined (lahadtu) to such-and-such" when I leaned toward it. From this comes the word lahd for the niche in the grave, because it lies at one side of the grave, not in the cleft at its middle. And from it comes ilhad in religion, which is opposition through deviating from it and abandoning it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 28:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life. And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his own desire and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect.﴾ (28)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Keep yourself patient﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿with﴾ your companions ﴿who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾, by remembering Him with glorification, praise, declaration of His oneness, supplication, and righteous deeds, including the obligatory prayers and others, ﴿seeking His countenance﴾ by their actions, not seeking any gain of the worldly goods.

We have already mentioned the disagreement of those who differ over His words ﴿call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾ in the commentary on Surat al-An'am, and the correct view in that matter in our opinion has been sufficient, so there is no need to repeat it here. The readers (qurra') are agreed upon reciting it as ﴿bil-ghadati wal-'ashiyy﴾ (with al-ghadah and al-'ashiyy). It has been reported that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami used to recite it as ﴿bil-ghadwati wal-'ashiyy﴾ (with al-ghadwah). That reading is disliked among the scholars of Arabic, because ghadwah is definite (ma'rifah) and does not take the alif and lam, for the alif and lam only define what is not already definite; definite nouns are not defined by them. Moreover, ghadwah is not put into an annexation (idafah) construction, and the impossibility of its annexation is clear evidence that the alif and lam cannot enter upon it, since nouns that take the alif and lam are those that accept annexation. The Arabs say: "I came to you on the morning (ghadat) of Friday," and do not say "I came to you at the ghadwah of Friday." Our reading in this matter is what the readers in the major cities recite; we do not permit anything else, because they are agreed upon it, and for the grammatical reason we have explained.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and let not your eyes pass beyond them﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: Do not turn your eyes away from these people, whom I have commanded you, O Muhammad, to keep yourself patient with, toward others among the unbelievers, and do not go beyond them to them. The root is from their saying: "I passed beyond that" (ʿadawtu dhalika), meaning "I went beyond it," when one exceeds it.

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said. Those who said so:

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding His words ﴿and let not your eyes pass beyond them﴾: "Do not go beyond them to others."

- 'Ali related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to me, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and let not your eyes pass beyond them﴾, he said: "Do not go beyond them to others."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Keep yourself patient...﴾ to the end of the verse: The people said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We are ashamed to sit with so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so, so distance yourself from them, O Muhammad, and sit with the nobles of the Arabs." Then the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and let not your eyes pass beyond them﴾, and do not disdain them. He said: "They have commanded me to that." Then: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his own desire and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect.﴾

- al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Usamah ibn Zayd informed me, from Abu Hazim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that when this verse was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in some of his houses: ﴿Keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, he went out seeking them, and found a group remembering Allah, among them one with disheveled hair, one with dry skin, and one with a single garment. When he saw them, he sat with them and said: "All praise is due to Allah who has placed among my nation those whom I was commanded to keep myself patient with," and the two eyes were lifted by the action, and he did not pass beyond them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: Do not let your eyes turn away from these believers who call upon their Lord, toward the nobles of the polytheists, seeking through sitting with them honor and pride. This is because, as was mentioned, some people from among the great men of the polytheists came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and some of them said: Rather, [they were] from the great men of the Arab tribes who had no insight into Islam. They saw him sitting with Khabbab, Suhayb, and Bilal, and asked him to remove them from him when they attended. They said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was concerned, so Allah revealed to him: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾. Then he would stand when he wished to stand, and leave them seated. So Allah revealed to him: ﴿Keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾, the verse, ﴿and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾, meaning: desiring the company of those great nobles. The report about this was mentioned earlier in the commentary on Surat al-An'am.

- al-Husayn ibn 'Amr al-'Anqazi related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: Asbat ibn Nasr related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, who was the reciter of the Azd, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab, in a story he related from the Prophet ﷺ, in which he mentioned this statement interspersed within the report: ﴿and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾, he said: "Sitting with the nobles."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I was informed that 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn said to the Prophet ﷺ before he became Muslim: "The smell of Salman the Persian has harmed me; so make for us a gathering with you where they do not mix with us, and make for them a gathering where we do not mix with them." So the verse was revealed.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "All praise is due to Allah who has placed in my nation those whom I was commanded to keep myself patient with."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾: He desires the nobles of this world.

- Salih ibn Mismar narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik related to us, saying: Sulayman ibn 'Ata' related to us, from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle Abu Mushajji' ibn Rab'i, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: The "those whose hearts are to be reconciled" (al-mu'allafah qulubuhum) came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn, [[In the original: 'Uyaynah ibn Badr. The correct reading is Ibn Hisn; it is likely a slip of the pen, and he is mentioned correctly shortly after.]] and al-Aqra' ibn Habis and their kin, and they said: "O Prophet of Allah, if you were to sit at the front of the mosque and drive away from us these people, and the odours of their coarse woollen garments" - meaning Salman, Abu Dharr, and the poor Muslims, who had nothing but woollen garments - "we would sit with you, converse with you, and take from you." So Allah revealed: ﴿And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord; none can alter His words, and you will not find any refuge other than Him﴾, until He reached ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire﴾, threatening them with the Fire. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood, seeking them, until he found them at the back of the mosque remembering Allah, and he said: "All praise is due to Allah who did not cause me to die until He commanded me to keep myself patient with men of my nation; with you is my life and with you is my death."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his own desire﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: Do not obey, O Muhammad, the one whose heart We have occupied from among the unbelievers, who asked you to drive away from you the group who call upon their Lord morning and evening, away from Our remembrance, through disbelief and the dominance of wretchedness over him, and who follows his desire, abandoning following the command and prohibition of Allah, preferring the desire of his soul over obedience to his Lord. They were, as has been mentioned: 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn, al-Aqra' ibn Habis, and their kin.

- al-Husayn ibn 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi related to me, saying: my father related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance﴾, he said: "'Uyaynah and al-Aqra'."

As for His words: ﴿and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾, the people of interpretation differed in its explanation. Some of them said: its meaning is: and his affair was loss.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding Allah's words ﴿and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾, he said: "Lost." In Ibn 'Amr's report he said: "Lost," and al-Harith in his report said: "Loss."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "Loss."

Others said: its meaning is: and his affair was regret.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar related to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Rashid related to us, from Dawud, regarding [furutan]: he said: "Remorse."

Others said: its meaning is: destruction.

Those who said so:

- al-Husayn ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: my father related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab, regarding ﴿and his affair was furutan﴾, he said: "Destruction."

Others said: its meaning is: opposing the truth.

Those who said so:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿and his affair was furutan﴾, he said: "Opposing the truth, that is the furut."

The most correct of these views, in our judgment, is the view of those who said: its meaning is loss and destruction, from their saying: "Afrata fulan fi hadha al-amr ifrata": when he exceeded in it and went beyond its measure. Likewise His words ﴿and his affair was furutan﴾ mean: the affair of this one whose heart We made heedless of Our remembrance, in vanity and arrogance and contempt for the people of faith, was excess that exceeded its bounds, so he thereby lost the truth and perished.

And indeed, Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash related to us, saying: He was asked: How did 'Asim recite? He said: ﴿and his affair was furutan﴾. Abu Kurayb said: Abu Bakr said: 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn used to boast with the saying "I, I."

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 29:

Interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of the meaning) of His saying, ﴿And say: The truth is from your Lord; so whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve. Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose enclosure will surround them. And if they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place.﴾ (29)

Almighty God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to those whose hearts We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follow their desires: the truth, O people, is from your Lord. Guidance and misguidance are in His hand, and to Him belongs success and failure.
