- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Khallad ibn Ata, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: His name before he committed disobedience was Azazil, and he was one of the inhabitants of the earth, and he was among the angels most diligent in worship and most knowledgeable. That is what led him to arrogance, and he was from a tribe called the jinn.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, from Bishr ibn Ammarah, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Iblis was from a tribe among the tribes of the angels called the jinn, created from the scorching fire of the samum from among the angels. His name was al-Harith. He said: He was a treasurer of the treasurers of Paradise. He said: The angels were created from light other than this tribe. He said: The jinn mentioned in the Qur'an were created from smokeless fire (marij min nar), which is the flame of fire that appears at its edge when it blazes.

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Shaybān related to us, he said: Salam ibn Miskin related to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Iblis was the chief of the angels of the lowest heaven.

- Ibn Waki' related to us, he said: My father related to us, from al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿except Iblis, he was of the jinn﴾, he said: Iblis was one of the treasurers of Paradise, and he used to manage the affairs of the lowest heaven.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: Iblis was among the noblest of the angels and the most honourable in lineage. He was the treasurer over the gardens, and he had authority over the lowest heaven, and he had authority over the earth. And among what God had decreed was that he saw that he had, by that, a nobility and greatness over the people of heaven, so arrogance entered his heart, which no one knows but God. When the time of prostration came, when He commanded him to prostrate to Adam, God brought forth his arrogance at the time of prostration, so He cursed him and deferred him until the Day of Judgement. He said: Ibn Abbas said: As for His words ﴿He was of the jinn﴾, he was named "of the jinn" only because he was a treasurer over the gardens (jinan), just as one says of a man: Makki, Madani, Basri, Kufi. This is what Ibn Jurayj said.

Others said: They are a group of the angels, a tribe, and the name of their tribe was the jinn.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Salih, mawla of al-Tawama, and Shurayk ibn Abi Namir, one or both of them, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Among the angels there is a tribe of jinn, and Iblis was of them, and he used to govern what was between the heaven and the earth. Then he disobeyed, so God was wrathful with him and transformed him into a stoning devil (shaytan rajim), cursed by God, transformed. He said: When a man's sin is of pride, do not hope for him; when his sin is of disobedience, then hope for him. Adam's sin was of disobedience, and Iblis's sin was of pride.

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis, he was of the jinn﴾: a tribe of the angels called the jinn. Ibn Abbas said: Had he not been of the angels, he would not have been commanded to prostrate; and he was over the treasury of the lowest heaven. Qatadah used to say: He became jinn (i.e., hidden) from obedience to his Lord. Al-Hasan used to say: God compelled him to his lineage.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿except Iblis, he was of the jinn﴾, he said: He was of a tribe of the angels called the jinn.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: Iblis was never of the angels for even the blink of an eye, and he is the origin of the jinn, just as Adam, peace be upon him, is the origin of mankind.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say: Iblis was over the lowest heaven and over the earth and was a treasurer of the gardens.

- I was related from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿so they prostrated, except Iblis, he was of the jinn﴾: Ibn Abbas used to say: Iblis was among the noblest of the angels and the most honourable in lineage, and he was a treasurer over the gardens, and he had authority over the lowest heaven and authority over the earth. Among what his soul had embellished to him concerning God's decree was that he saw that he had by that a nobility over the people of heaven, so arrogance entered his heart, which no one knows but God. God brought forth that arrogance from him when He commanded him to prostrate to Adam, so he became proud and was among the disbelievers. That is His saying to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal﴾, meaning: what Iblis concealed within himself of arrogance.

* *

And His words: ﴿He was of the jinn﴾

Ibn Abbas used to say: God said ﴿He was of the jinn﴾ because he was a treasurer over the gardens, just as one says of a man: Makki, Madani, Basri, Kufi.

Others said: The name of Iblis's tribe was the jinn, and they are a group of the angels called the jinn, and therefore God, mighty and majestic, said ﴿He was of the jinn﴾, ascribing him to his tribe.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, concerning His words ﴿He was of the jinn﴾, he said: Of the gardeners (al-jannanin) who work in the gardens.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Abu Sa'id al-Yahmadi Isma'il ibn Ibrahim related to us, he said: Sawwar ibn al-Ja'd al-Yahmadi related to me, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, concerning His words ﴿of the jinn﴾, he said: Iblis was of the jinn whom the angels had expelled, and some of the angels seized him and took him to the heaven.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿except Iblis, he was of the jinn, and he departed from the command of his Lord﴾, he said: He was the treasurer of the gardens, so he was named after the gardens.

- Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn Bashir related to us, from Sufyan ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Iblis was one of the guardians of Paradise.

We have already explained the discussion on this matter earlier in this book of ours, and mentioned the differences of those who differed about it, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it in this place.

* *

And His words: ﴿so he departed from the command of his Lord﴾

He says: he went out from the command of his Lord, deviated from it and inclined away from it, as Ru'bah said:

They descend into Najd and the deep hollows, / deviating (fawasiqa) from their intended course, straying (jawa'ira).

By fawasiq he means camels that deviate from the straight path of Najd. Likewise, transgression (fisq) in religion is only deviation from the right course and inclining away from uprightness. It is related from the Arabs by report that: "The date-palm fruit departed (fasaqat) from its skin" when it came out of it, and "the mouse departed (fasaqat) from its hole" when it came out of it. A certain grammarian of Basra used to say: It was said ﴿so he departed from the command of his Lord﴾ because what is meant is: he departed from his returning the command of God, just as the Arabs say: "I overate from the food" meaning: I overate by what I ate. We have already explained this matter, and that its meaning is: he deviated and transgressed from the command of God and went out from it. Some learned people in the speech of the Arabs said: The meaning of fisq is expansion (al-ittisa'). They claimed that the Arabs say: "He was extravagant (fasaqa) in expenditure," meaning he expanded in it. He said: The wrongdoer is only called fasiq (transgressor) because of his expansion in what God has forbidden.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us ("ha"), and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words ﴿so he departed from the command of his Lord﴾, he said: In prostrating to Adam.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿so he departed from the command of his Lord﴾, he said: He disobeyed in prostrating to Adam.

* *

And His words: ﴿Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are an enemy to you?﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Will you, O children of Adam, befriend one who was arrogant toward your father and envied him, who denied My blessing upon him, who deceived him until he expelled him from Paradise and the delight of his life in it to the earth and the straitness of life there, and obey him and his descendants instead of God, despite their enmity toward you from of old and now, and abandon obedience to your Lord who blessed you and honoured you, by having His angels prostrate to your father, and settled him in His gardens, and gave you from the abundance of His favours what cannot be counted? And the descendants of Iblis are the devils who deceive the children of Adam.

As:

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me﴾, he said: His descendants are the devils, and he would count them: Zalnabur, the lord of the markets, who places his banner in every market between heaven and earth; Thubr, the lord of calamities; al-A'war, the lord of adultery; Masut, the lord of news, who brings it and casts it into the mouths of people, and they find no basis for it; and Dasim, who, when a man enters his house and does not greet and does not mention God, takes his eye to the goods until they are lifted, and when he eats and does not mention the name of God, eats with him.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, he said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us, he said: I heard al-A'mash say: When I enter a house and do not greet, I see a water-jug, and I say: Lift it, lift it, and I dispute with them; then I remember and say: Dasim, Dasim.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to me, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, he said: They are four: Thubr, Dasim, Zalnabur, and al-A'war, and Masut is one of them.

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me﴾ ... the verse, and they reproduce as the children of Adam reproduce, and they are an enemy to you.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are an enemy to you﴾: He is the father of the jinn just as Adam is the father of mankind.

And he said: God said to Iblis: I do not create for Adam any offspring except that I create for you the like of it, so there is no child of Adam except that he has a devil bound to him.

* *

And His words: ﴿Wretched is [that] exchange for the wrongdoers﴾

He, mighty is His remembrance, says: Wretched is the exchange for those who disbelieve in God, taking Iblis and his descendants as allies other than God, and they are an enemy to you, for whoever abandons taking God as ally by following His command and prohibition, and He is the one who blessed them and their father Adam before them, and bestowed upon them abundant favours that cannot be counted, is an exchange.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿Wretched is [that] exchange for the wrongdoers﴾: How wretched is what they substituted for the worship of their Lord when they obeyed Iblis.

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, and I would not take the misleaders as helpers.﴾ (18:51)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: I did not make Iblis and his offspring witness ﴿the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning, I did not bring them to be present at that, so that I might seek their help in creating them. ﴿Nor the creation of themselves﴾, meaning: nor did I make some of them witness the creation of others of them, so that I might seek help from one of them in creating another. Rather, I alone brought all of that into being, without any helper or supporter. He says: how, then, have they taken their enemy as allies besides Me, when they are creatures among creatures like themselves, and have abandoned worshipping Me, while I am the One who bestowed favour upon them and upon their forebears, and I am their Creator and the Creator of those whom they take as allies besides Me, alone in that, without any helper or supporter.

* *

And His words: ﴿and I would not take the misleaders as helpers (ʿaḍud)﴾

He says: I would not take as helpers and supporters one who does not guide to the truth but misleads, such that whoever follows him is led away from the straight path. This is from their saying: "So-and-so supports (yaʿḍudu) so-and-so," when he strengthens and aids him.

Some people of interpretation have said something similar to this.

Those who said so:

Basharr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿and I would not take the misleaders as helpers (ʿaḍudan)﴾: that is, helpers (aʿwanan).

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, the same. He only means by this that Iblis and his offspring mislead the children of Adam from the truth, and do not guide them to rectitude. It is also possible that by "the misleaders" he meant those who are followers in error and companions not upon guidance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 52–53:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And [mention] the Day He will say, "Call upon My partners, whom you claimed." So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a barrier of destruction (mawbiq).﴾ (18:52) and ﴿The criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall therein, and they will not find from it any means of escape.﴾ (18:53)

He, mighty is His mention, says: ﴿And the Day He will say﴾ — Allah, mighty is His mention, to those who associated with Him gods and equals — ﴿"Call upon My partners whom you claimed"﴾: He says to them, "Call upon those whom you used to claim were My partners in worship, that they may help you and protect you from Me." ﴿So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them﴾: He says, they sought their aid, but they did not give them aid. ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction (mawbiq).﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: And We will place between these polytheists and what they used to call upon besides Allah as partners, in the world on that day, enmity.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Buzayʿ narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: He placed between them enmity on the Day of Resurrection.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: enmity.

Others said: its meaning is: And We will make their act of that a place of ruin (mahlik) for them.

Those who said that:

- ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a place of ruin (mahlik).

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿mawbiq﴾ — he said: destruction.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾: the mawbiq is the destroyer, in which they destroy one another; it causes some of them to destroy others. And he recited: ﴿And We will appoint for their destruction an appointed time.﴾

- It was related to me from Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿mawbiq﴾ — he said: destruction.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from ʿArfajah, regarding His saying ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a place of ruin.

Others said: it is the name of a valley in Hell.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, from Abu Ayyub, from ʿAmr al-Bikali: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a deep valley by which is separated between the people of misguidance and the people of guidance, and the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — it was mentioned to us that ʿUmar al-Bikali related from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: It is a deep valley by which is divided, on the Day of Resurrection, between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, who said: Mujahid said, ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a valley in the Fire.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us ("ḥ"), and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a valley in Hell.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Dirham narrated to us, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a valley in Hell of pus and blood.

The most correct of these opinions in interpretation is the view that we mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbas and those who agreed with him regarding the interpretation of mawbiq as "destruction," because the Arabs say in their speech: "I have ruined (awbaqtu) so-and-so," meaning: I destroyed him. And from it is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿or He would destroy them for what they have earned﴾ — meaning: He would destroy them. And it is said of the one destroyed himself: "So-and-so has perished (waqa), so he perishes (yubiqu) with a perishing (wabaq)." The dialect of Banu ʿAmir is yabiq without a hamza. It is related from Tamim that they say yiyabiq. And it has been related that waqa yaqu wabuqan, as al-Kisa'i related. And some of the scholars of the Arabic language among the people of Basra used to say: al-mawbiq means "the promise," and he cited for his statement the verse of a poet:

"And he has passed by Sharawra and al-Sattar, leaving no … for him, and the two valleys with a mawbiq."

[The verse is in (al-Lisan: w-b-q). He said: waqa al-rajul yabiq waqan and wuqub... And al-Farra' said: He means: We made their connection in the world a mawbiq, that is, a destruction for them in the Hereafter. Ibn al-A'rabi said: mawbiq means a barrier, and every barrier between two things is a mawbiq. Abu ʿUbayda said: al-mawbiq is the promise, in His saying "and We placed between them a mawbiq," and he argued with the verse "and he has passed by Sharawra…", meaning: with a promise.]

He interprets it as "a promise." It is also permissible that the destruction which Allah, mighty is His praise, placed between these polytheists is the valley that was mentioned from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, and it is also permissible that it is the enmity that al-Hasan mentioned.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire﴾

He says: And the polytheists will witness the Fire on that day. ﴿And they will be certain that they are to fall therein﴾ — he says: they will know that they are going to enter it.

As it was narrated:

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they will be certain that they are to fall therein﴾ — he said: they will know.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed the disbeliever will see Hell and will think that it will fall upon him from a distance of forty years."

* *

His saying: ﴿And they will not find from it any means of escape﴾

He says: And they will not find, from the Fire that they saw, a way of deviation to which they might turn away from it. He says: they will not find any escape from falling into it, because Allah has decreed that upon them. And the use of al-maṣrif in the sense of al-maʿdil (means of turning aside) is the saying of Abu Kabir al-Hudhali:

"O Zuhayr, is there any escape from Shayba, or is there no eternity for one who spends and strives?"

[The verse is by Abu Kabir al-Hudhali, found in the second part of the Diwan of the Hudhaliyyin, Dar al-Kutub edition, p. 104, the opening of one of his odes. It is among the evidences of Abu ʿUbayda in (Majaz al-Qur'an, 1:407), who said, explaining His saying "and they will not find from it any means of escape": i.e., a way of deviation. And Abu Kabr al-Hudhali said: "O Zuhayr…" etc., the verse.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 52–53:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And [mention] the Day He will say, "Call upon My partners, whom you claimed." So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a barrier of destruction (mawbiq).﴾ (18:52) and ﴿The criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall therein, and they will not find from it any means of escape.﴾ (18:53)

He, mighty is His mention, says: ﴿And the Day He will say﴾ — Allah, mighty is His mention, to those who associated with Him gods and equals — ﴿"Call upon My partners whom you claimed"﴾: He says to them, "Call upon those whom you used to claim were My partners in worship, that they may help you and protect you from Me." ﴿So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them﴾: He says, they sought their aid, but they did not give them aid. ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction (mawbiq).﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: And We will place between these polytheists and what they used to call upon besides Allah as partners, in the world on that day, enmity.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Buzayʿ narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: He placed between them enmity on the Day of Resurrection.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: enmity.

Others said: its meaning is: And We will make their act of that a place of ruin (mahlik) for them.

Those who said that:

- ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a place of ruin (mahlik).

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿mawbiq﴾ — he said: destruction.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾: the mawbiq is the destroyer, in which they destroy one another; it causes some of them to destroy others. And he recited: ﴿And We will appoint for their destruction an appointed time.﴾

- It was related to me from Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿mawbiq﴾ — he said: destruction.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from ʿArfajah, regarding His saying ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a place of ruin.

Others said: it is the name of a valley in Hell.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, from Abu Ayyub, from ʿAmr al-Bikali: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a deep valley by which is separated between the people of misguidance and the people of guidance, and the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — it was mentioned to us that ʿUmar al-Bikali related from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: It is a deep valley by which is divided, on the Day of Resurrection, between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, who said: Mujahid said, ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a valley in the Fire.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us ("ḥ"), and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a valley in Hell.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Dirham narrated to us, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿And We will place between them a barrier of destruction﴾ — he said: a valley in Hell of pus and blood.

The most correct of these opinions in interpretation is the view that we mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbas and those who agreed with him regarding the interpretation of mawbiq as "destruction," because the Arabs say in their speech: "I have ruined (awbaqtu) so-and-so," meaning: I destroyed him. And from it is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿or He would destroy them for what they have earned﴾ — meaning: He would destroy them. And it is said of the one destroyed himself: "So-and-so has perished (waqa), so he perishes (yubiqu) with a perishing (wabaq)." The dialect of Banu ʿAmir is yabiq without a hamza. It is related from Tamim that they say yiyabiq. And it has been related that waqa yaqu wabuqan, as al-Kisa'i related. And some of the scholars of the Arabic language among the people of Basra used to say: al-mawbiq means "the promise," and he cited for his statement the verse of a poet:

"And he has passed by Sharawra and al-Sattar, leaving no … for him, and the two valleys with a mawbiq."

[The verse is in (al-Lisan: w-b-q). He said: waqa al-rajul yabiq waqan and wuqub... And al-Farra' said: He means: We made their connection in the world a mawbiq, that is, a destruction for them in the Hereafter. Ibn al-A'rabi said: mawbiq means a barrier, and every barrier between two things is a mawbiq. Abu ʿUbayda said: al-mawbiq is the promise, in His saying "and We placed between them a mawbiq," and he argued with the verse "and he has passed by Sharawra…", meaning: with a promise.]

He interprets it as "a promise." It is also permissible that the destruction which Allah, mighty is His praise, placed between these polytheists is the valley that was mentioned from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, and it is also permissible that it is the enmity that al-Hasan mentioned.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire﴾

He says: And the polytheists will witness the Fire on that day. ﴿And they will be certain that they are to fall therein﴾ — he says: they will know that they are going to enter it.

As it was narrated:

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they will be certain that they are to fall therein﴾ — he said: they will know.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed the disbeliever will see Hell and will think that it will fall upon him from a distance of forty years."

* *

His saying: ﴿And they will not find from it any means of escape﴾

He says: And they will not find, from the Fire that they saw, a way of deviation to which they might turn away from it. He says: they will not find any escape from falling into it, because Allah has decreed that upon them. And the use of al-maṣrif in the sense of al-maʿdil (means of turning aside) is the saying of Abu Kabir al-Hudhali:

"O Zuhayr, is there any escape from Shayba, or is there no eternity for one who spends and strives?"

[The verse is by Abu Kabir al-Hudhali, found in the second part of the Diwan of the Hudhaliyyin, Dar al-Kutub edition, p. 104, the opening of one of his odes. It is among the evidences of Abu ʿUbayda in (Majaz al-Qur'an, 1:407), who said, explaining His saying "and they will not find from it any means of escape": i.e., a way of deviation. And Abu Kabr al-Hudhali said: "O Zuhayr…" etc., the verse.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 54:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an for the people from every [kind of] example. But mankind is, most of anything, contentious.﴾ (18:54)

He, mighty is His remembrance, says: We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, and admonished them in it with every admonition, and argued against them in it with every argument, so that they might be reminded and turn back in repentance, and take heed and be admonished, and desist from the polytheism and worship of idols in which they persist. ﴿But mankind is, most of anything, contentious﴾ means: mankind is, most of anything, disputatious and quarrelsome, not turning to the truth, nor being restrained by admonition.

As narrated:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿But mankind is, most of anything, contentious﴾: "Al-jadal" is quarrelling, the quarrelling of the people with their prophets and their rejection of what they brought. And he recited: ﴿This is not but a human being like you; he eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink﴾ [23:33]. And he recited: ﴿He wants to make himself superior over you﴾ [23:24]. And he recited: ﴿Until you cause to descend upon us a book we can read﴾ [17:93]... the verse: ﴿And even if We had sent down to you a written book on paper﴾ [6:7]... the verse. And he recited: ﴿And if We opened for them a gate from the heaven and they continued to ascend therein﴾ [15:14], he said: "They would say: 'Our eyes have only been intoxicated; rather, we are a people bewitched'" [15:15].

The commentary on the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them, and from seeking forgiveness of their Lord, except that the way of the ancients should befall them, or that the punishment should come upon them face to face.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Nothing prevented these polytheists, O Muhammad, from believing in God when the guidance came to them, the clear proof of God, and they knew the truth of what you call them to and its reality, and from seeking forgiveness for their polytheism in which they persist, except the coming upon them of Our way (sunnah) with the like of them among the nations that denied their messengers before them, or their encountering of the punishment face to face (qubulan).

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: or the punishment comes upon them suddenly.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿or the punishment comes upon them face to face﴾, he said: "suddenly."

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Others said: its meaning is: or the punishment comes upon them openly, before their eyes (ʿiyanan).

Those who said this:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿or the punishment comes upon them face to face﴾: "qubulan" means in direct witnessing of that encounter.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this. A large group read (أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ الْعَذَابُ قُبُلا) with a damma on the qaf and the ba', meaning that there come upon them punishments of various kinds and forms, and they took qubul as the plural of qabil, just as qatil is pluralized as qutul and jadid as judud. Another group read: "أو يَأتِيَهُمُ العَذَابُ قِبَلا" with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba', meaning: or the punishment comes upon them face to face, from their saying: "kallamtuhu qibalan" (I spoke to him face to face). I have already explained this matter in Surat al-An'am in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

**Commentary on the Interpretation (ta'wil) of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bearers of good news and as warners, and those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood in order to refute the truth thereby, and they take My signs and what they were warned of as mockery﴾ (18:56)**

He, mighty is His remembrance, says: We send Our messengers only to give good news to the people of faith and belief in God, of the abundant reward in the Hereafter, and to warn the people of disbelief in Him and denial of Him of His great punishment and painful torment, so that they desist from associating partners with God and refrain from disbelief in Him and from His disobedience. ﴿And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood in order to refute the truth thereby﴾: that is, they argue against God's messenger and His book with falsehood, those who denied God and His messenger contend with falsehood. This was like their saying to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Tell us about the story of the youths who went off in the earliest times and whose affair is unknown, and about the man who reached the eastern and western parts of the earth, and about the Spirit," and other such things with which they used to dispute with him, seeking to overthrow him, to trouble him (ﷺ). So God told them: "We do not send Our messengers to you for argument and disputation. We send them only as bearers of good news to the people of faith, of Paradise, and as warners to the people of disbelief, of the Fire. Yet you dispute with them with falsehood, desiring thereby to nullify the truth that My messenger has brought you."

By His saying ﴿in order to refute the truth thereby﴾ He means: that they may nullify the truth with it, remove it, and dispel it. It is said of this verb: "dahada al-shay'" (the thing slipped away) when it departed and vanished. It is also said: "This is a place of dahd," meaning a slippery place where no sandal, hoof, or foot can hold firm. From this is the line of the poet:

*"You fell, and the Yashkuri escaped his caution, and he swerved as a camel swerves from the slippery ground."*

It is also narrated as "wa-nahha" (and he pushed away). And "adhdahtuhu" means: I made it depart and nullified it.

[[The verse is attributed to Tarafa in (Lisan al-Arab: dahd), in al-Taj, and in Asas al-Balaghah. It is not found in the poetry of the Six Poets (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili) or elsewhere. The author of Shu'ara' al-Nasraniyyah and the author of al-'Iqd al-Thamin, in the appendix to Tarafa's poetry, cite a fragment rhyming in "dad," beginning: "Abu Mundhir, my writing was a deception, and I did not give you my wealth willingly, nor my honour."

It is most likely that the verse fell out of this fragment, though it is common in books of literature and lexicography. It is one of the witnesses of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (1:408), where he said, regarding the verse ﴿to refute the truth thereby﴾: its sense is "to remove the truth thereby and make it depart." It is said: "a place of dahd" means a slippery place where no sandal, foot, or hoof holds. Tarafa said: "You fell, and... "

And in (Lisan al-Arab: dahd), the witness for dahd is Tarafa's verse: "You fell..." etc.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they take My signs and what they were warned of as mockery﴾:

He says: The disbelievers in God take His proofs, with which He argued against them, and His book that He sent down to them, and the warnings with which He warned them, as objects of mockery with which they make fun. They say: ﴿This is nothing but the fables of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening. Had we willed, we could have said the like of this﴾ (25:5 and 8:31).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 57:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have sent forth? Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if you invite them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever.﴾ (18:57)

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Who among mankind is more deserving of placing turning away and aversion where they do not belong than one who is reminded of His signs and proofs, whom He guides by them to the path of rectitude and leads by them to the way of salvation, yet he turns away from His signs and proofs, by which he could have reached deliverance from destruction. ﴿And forgets what his hands have sent forth﴾ means: and forgets the destructive sins he has committed in advance, so he does not repent and does not turn back.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿and forgets what his hands have sent forth﴾: that is, he forgets the sins that preceded.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We have placed over the hearts of those who turn away from the signs of God when they are reminded of them coverings, lest they understand it, since the meaning is that they should understand what they were reminded of. His words ﴿and in their ears deafness﴾ mean: in their ears a heaviness, lest they hear it. ﴿And if you invite them to guidance﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And if you, O Muhammad, invite these people who turn away from the signs of God when reminded of them to steadfastness upon the path of truth and belief in God, and in what you have brought them from your Lord, ﴿they will never be guided, ever﴾ means: they will never then remain steadfast upon the truth, and will never believe in what you call them to, because God has sealed their hearts, their hearing, and their sight.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 58:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord is the Forgiving, Possessor of mercy. If He were to seize them for what they have earned, He would hasten for them the punishment. But for them is an appointment, and they will not find from other than Him any refuge﴾ [18:58].

Exalted is He, speaking to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And your Lord, O Muhammad, is the Concealer of the sins of His servants by His pardon of them when they repent from them, ﴿Possessor of mercy. If He were to seize them for what they have earned﴾ — these who turn away from His signs when they are reminded of them — for what they have earned of sins and transgressions, ﴿He would hasten for them the punishment﴾ — but He, out of His mercy toward His creation, does not do that to them until their appointed term and their lifespans. ﴿But for them is an appointment﴾ — meaning: rather, for them there is an appointment, and that is the appointed time of the place of their punishment, which is the Day of Badr. ﴿And they will not find from other than Him any refuge﴾ — Exalted is He, speaking: These polytheists will not find, even if the punishment is not hastened for them in this world, apart from the appointment which I have made the appointed time for their punishment, any refuge to which they may take shelter, or any place of deliverance by which they may be saved; that is, they will not find any stronghold by which they can shield themselves from the punishment of God. It is said of it: "Wa'ala min kadha ila kadha, ya'ilu wa'lan wa'ulan wa'ulan, like wa'ulan (wu'ulan)," and from it is the saying of the poet:

"No, may your soul not find refuge (wa'alat); I left it to the Amiri men and it was not wounded"

[[The verse: one of the witnesses cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 187). He said: His saying, "lan yajidu min dunihi mawila": al-mawil is the place of deliverance, the refuge, and the meaning is the same. The Arabs say: "innahu la-yuwa'ilu ila mawdi'ihi," meaning: he goes to his place and his shelter. And a poet said: "La wa'alat nafsuka..." the verse. They mean: "la najat" (may it not be saved). In Lisan al-Arab (wa'ala) Abu al-Haytham said: it is said wa'ala ya'ilu wa'lan and wa'ala, wa'ala yuwa'ilu mu'alatan and wu'alan. Al-Layth said: al-ma'al and al-mawil: the refuge.]]

He says: "lā najat" (may it not be saved).

And the saying of al-A'sha:

"And I may steal from the master of the house his unawareness, though he may guard against me whatever he cannot escape (yi'ul)"

[[The verse is from the lamiyya of al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays (his Diwan with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 59). He said: khalasa al-shay' means he stole it and took it secretly. Ma yi'ul: what does not escape; the past tense is wa'ala, meaning he escaped. He says: he has taken every treasured thing whose owner guards it and protects it with his care, yet his caution does not save him from me. It is also one of the witnesses of Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (1: 408), like the previous witness, in explaining His saying: "lan yajidu min dunihi mawila." He said: al-A'sha said: "And I may steal..." the verse; that is, he does not escape.]]

And in accordance with what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us [ḥ], and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "mawila": he said: a place of safety.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- 'Ali related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "lan yajidu min dunihi mawila": he said: a refuge.

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, "lan yajidu min dunihi mawila": that is, they will not find from other than Him a protector or a refuge.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: "lan yajidu min dunihi mawila": he said: there is no refuge other than Him to which they may take shelter.

The exegesis of the words of the Most High: ﴿And those cities — We destroyed them when they did wrong, and We appointed for their destruction a set time﴾ (18:59)

The Most High says: "And those cities, of 'Ad, Thamud, and the People of the Thicket, We destroyed their inhabitants when they did wrong, by disbelieving in God and His signs." ﴿And We appointed for their destruction a set time﴾ means an appointed time and a term; when it arrived, the punishment came upon them and We destroyed them by it. The meaning is: likewise, We have appointed a set time for these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, who will never believe in you, and when that time comes, We will destroy them, following Our practice with their counterparts who passed away before them.

As follows:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us [ḥ]. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿for their destruction a set time﴾: he said, "A term."

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

The reciters (qurra', sing. qari') differed over the reading of His words ﴿لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ﴾ (limahlikihim). The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read it as "لِمُهْلَكِهِمْ" (limuhlikihim), with a damma on the mim and a fatha on the lam, interpreting it as a verbal noun (masdar) of "they destroyed them" (ahlakū ihlākan). 'Asim read it as "لِمَهْلَكِهِمْ" (limahlakihim), with a fatha on both the mim and the lam, interpreting it as a verbal noun of "they perished" (halakū halākan wa mahlakan).

In my view, the more correct of the two readings is the one that reads "لِمُهْلَكِهِمْ" with a damma on the mim and a fatha on the lam, because the authorities among the reciters agree upon it, and because of the evidence of His words ﴿And those cities — We destroyed them﴾, so that the verbal noun derives from "We destroyed" (ahlakna), since that verb occurred earlier. It has also been said that the pronoun refers back to "We destroyed them" (ahlaknāhum), since He had previously said ﴿And those cities﴾, because destruction only befell the people of the cities; so the speech returns to the meaning and is構 arranged accordingly rather than to the wording.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He said ﴿And those cities — We destroyed them when they did wrong﴾, meaning their inhabitants, just as He said ﴿and ask the town﴾ (12:82), and did not say "the towns" in form, but applied the wording to the people, and applied the wording of "the town" to them, up to His words ﴿in which we were﴾ (12:82). He said "We destroyed them" (ahlaknāhum) and did not say "We destroyed it" (ahlaknāhā), treating it according to the people, as one says "Tamim came" (jā'at Tamīm), attributing the verb to the Banu Tamim and not to Tamim himself. If one did otherwise, one would say "Tamim came" (jā'a Tamīm). This is not good in a case like this, because in such a position he intends other than Tamim, so he made it a noun; and when it is inflected (i'lāl), it cannot omit everything that precedes it in meaning, namely the feminine ta' of "jā'at" with "the Banu Tamim". He left the verb as it was, so that it would be known that something had been omitted before "Tamim".

Some of them said: It was permissible to say "those cities — We destroyed them" because the city stood in the place of the people, so it was permissible for the reference to return to the people once and to the city once. That is not permissible with Tamim, because the tribe is known by him, and Tamim is not the tribe; rather the tribe became known by him. If the tribe had been named after the man, the usage would follow him, as one says "I fell into Hud" (waqa'tu fi Hūd), meaning in the Surah of Hud, and Hud is not the name of the Surah; rather the Surah became known by him. If the Surah were named Hud, one would not inflect it, so one would say "I fell into Hud, O man" without inflection. Likewise, if the Banu Tamim had been named Tamim, one would say "This Tamim has come" (hādhihi Tamīm qad aqbalat). So the meaning of the speech is: "And those cities — We destroyed them when they did wrong, and We appointed for their destruction a set time."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 60:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Moses said to his young man, "I will not cease [travelling] until I reach the junction of the two seas, or I will continue for a long period."﴾

He, mighty is His remembrance, says to His Prophet ﷺ: Recall, O Muhammad, when Moses son of Imran said to his young man Yusha': ﴿I will not cease﴾, meaning: I will not stop travelling, ﴿until I reach the junction of the two seas﴾.

As related by:

Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿I will not cease﴾: "I will not stop." It was said that by His saying ﴿the junction of the two seas﴾ is meant the meeting of the Persian Sea and the Roman Sea. And al-Majma' (the junction) is a verbal noun from their saying: "jama'a yajma'u" (he gathered, gathers).

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr told us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿until I reach the junction of the two seas﴾: "The two seas are the Persian Sea and the Roman Sea; the Roman Sea is on the west side, and the Persian Sea is on the east side."

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿the junction of the two seas﴾: "The Persian Sea and the Roman Sea."

Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, ﴿the junction of the two seas﴾: "The Roman Sea and the Persian Sea, one of them toward the east and the other toward the west."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, he said: ﴿the junction of the two seas﴾. [[A blank in the original; in al-Durr (al-Suyuti) it is related from Ibn Abbas: "The explanation of 'the junction of the two seas' is: the meeting point of the two seas."]]

Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Yahya ibn al-Dirays related to us, he said: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, regarding His saying ﴿I will not cease until I reach the junction of the two seas﴾: "Tangier."

* *

As for His saying ﴿or I will continue for a long period﴾:

It means: or I will travel for a time and an age (dahr). It is singular, and its plural and its paucal forms are both "ahqab" (periods). The Arabs say: "I was with him for a period (huqbah) of time," and they plural it as "huqab."

Some scholars of the Arabic language interpreted His saying ﴿I will not cease﴾ as: "I will not depart" (la azulu), and they cited as evidence for that the verse of al-Farazdaq:

"They did not cease until their women swayed
in the valley of Dhi Qar, carrying the bags of perfumed (camel-loads)."

[[The verse is in the Diwan of al-Farazdaq (al-Sawi edition, p. 773), from an ode of nine verses in praise of Abdullah ibn Abd al-A'la al-Shaybani. The waw in "baraḥū" refers to the Banu Tamim, whose deeds on the day of Dhi Qar he boasts of. "Al-ayyab" is the plural of "ayba," a bag; "al-latha'im" is the plural of "latima," the camels on which grain and perfume alone are carried. The verse is evidence that some Arabic scholars interpret His saying "I will not cease" to mean "I will not stop."]]

He says: "They did not cease" (ma zalu).

Some scholars of the Arabic language mentioned that the huqb in the dialect of Qays means a year. As for the people of interpretation, they say about it what I shall mention: they differed concerning it. Some of them said: it is eighty years.

Mention of those who said this:

I was related from Hushaym, he said: Abu Bulj related to us, from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abdullah ibn Amr, he said: "The huqb is eighty years."

Others said: it is seventy years.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, ﴿or I will continue for a long period﴾: "Seventy autumns."

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Others said regarding this, in a manner close to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali told me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿or I will continue for a long period﴾: "A dahr (age)."

Ahmad ibn Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿huqban﴾: "The huqb: a time (zaman)."

Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿or I will continue for a long period﴾: "The huqb: a time (zaman)."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when they reached the meeting place of the two seas, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the sea, a tunnel⁠﴾ (18:61).

He, exalted is His remembrance, means: when Musa and his servant reached the meeting place of the two seas.

As related to me by Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Asim related to us, who said: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿meeting place between them⁠﴾, he said: between the two seas.

Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His words ﴿they forgot their fish⁠﴾:

By His words "forgot" he means: left behind.

As related to me by Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Asim related to us, who said: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿they forgot their fish⁠﴾, he said: they lost it.

Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: they lost it.

Some of the scholars of Arabic said: The fish was with Yusha', and it was he who forgot it, so the forgetting is attributed to both of them, as He said: ﴿From both of them come out pearls and coral⁠﴾, whereas they come out of the salt water and not the sweet. [This is the words of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (the Jami'a photocopy no. 24059, folio 189).]

In my view, it is permissible to say "they forgot" because both of them had taken provisions for their journey; so the carrying of one of them is attributed to both, since it was carried from both of them. It is like saying: the people left a certain place and carried with them such-and-such provisions, though only one of them carried it; but because that was by their opinion and command, it is attributed to all of them. Likewise, when the one who carried it forgot it at a place, it is said: the people forgot their provisions, attributing it to all through the forgetting of the one who carried it. So the speech applies to all while the action belongs to one. Thus it is with His words ﴿they forgot their fish⁠﴾, because God, mighty is His remembrance, addressed the Arabs in their own language and in what they commonly use in speech among themselves.

As for His words ﴿From both of them come out pearls and coral⁠﴾, the view on that is, in our opinion, contrary to what he said about it, and we shall clarify it, God willing, when we reach it.

As for His words ﴿it took its way into the sea, a tunnel⁠﴾, it means that the fish took its path, which it traveled in the sea, as a tunnel.

As related to us by Al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿it took its way into the sea, a tunnel⁠﴾, he said: the fish took. By "sarab" is meant the course and the way; "yasrab" fihi means he goes in it and travels it.

Then the scholars differed concerning the manner in which it took its way into the sea as a tunnel. Some of them said: its path along which it traveled became like a burrow.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His words ﴿a tunnel⁠﴾, he said: its trace was as if it were a burrow.

Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salama related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, when mentioning the story of that: "No water has parted since people existed other than this: the place where the fish stood remained, [[As in the original; the Durr has it as: "other than a water-place in which the fish had entered..." etc. In Tafsir Ibn Kathir: "other than the course of the place of the fish", etc.]]

so it opened like a window until Musa returned to it, and he saw its course, and said: 'That is what we were seeking.'"

Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Ibn Atiyya related to us, who said: Amr ibn Thabit related to us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "it took its way into the sea, a tunnel," he said: He came and saw the trace of its wings in the mud when it entered the water. Ibn Abbas said: ﴿it took its way into the sea, a tunnel⁠﴾ and he made a gesture with his hand. [[In al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Tafsir, from the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr): and he made a gesture with between his two thumbs and the two fingers beside them.]]

Others said: rather, its path in the sea became solid water.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: It made a tunnel from the depression [[Perhaps the intended meaning of "jarr" here is a hollow in the earth, as in Lisan al-Arab (jarr).]] until it reached the sea, then it traveled, and whenever it took a path in it, it became solid water.

Others said: rather, its path in the sea became stone.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The fish, whenever it touched any part of the sea, dried until it became a rock.

Others said: rather, it took its way as a tunnel on land toward the water, until it reached it, not in the sea.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿it took its way into the sea, a tunnel⁠﴾, he said: The fish was gathered in the open ground after its death, when God revived it. Ibn Zayd said: Abu Shuja informed me that he saw it, saying: I was brought it, and it was a half of a fish with one eye, and another half with nothing in it.

The correct statement on this is to say as God, mighty and majestic, said: "And the fish took its way into the sea, a tunnel." It is possible that the tunnel was by a parting of the earth, and it is possible that it was by the freezing of the water, and it is possible that it was by its turning into stone.

The soundest of the sayings on it is what has been reported as a narration from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that we mentioned from Ubayy from him.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So when they had passed beyond it, he said to his servant, "Bring us our morning meal. We have certainly suffered weariness from this journey of ours."﴾

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿When they had passed beyond it﴾ — Musa and his servant, the meeting place of the two seas — ﴿he said﴾ — Musa — ﴿to his servant﴾ — Yusha' (Joshua) — ﴿"Bring us our morning meal"﴾ — meaning: bring us our food and give it to us. He said "ātinā ghadā'anā" (bring us our morning meal), just as one says "atā al-ghadā'" and "ataytuhu" (I brought it), like "dhahaba" and "adhhabtuhu" (he went and I took it away). ﴿"We have certainly suffered weariness from this journey of ours"﴾ — meaning: we have certainly encountered fatigue and exhaustion from this journey of ours. This was said by Musa, as has been reported, after he had passed the rock, when hunger came upon him so that he would remember the fish and return to the place he was seeking.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He (ta'wil, meaning interpretation):** ﴿He said, "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it. And it took its way into the sea in an amazing manner."﴾ (18:63)

His words, exalted is He, mean: The youth of Musa said to Musa when he said to him, "Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed met with fatigue from this journey of ours" (18:62): "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish there." ﴿And none caused me to forget it except Satan﴾ means: none caused me to forget the fish except Satan. ﴿That I should mention it﴾: "an" (that) here is in the accusative position (naṣb), in apposition to "the fish" (al-hut), because the meaning of the sentence is: "None caused me to forget that I should mention the fish except Satan." The subject (the fish) came first in the verb, and then the phrase ﴿that I should mention it﴾ was repeated in apposition to it. It has been mentioned that this reading appears in the codex of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): "And none caused me to forget it, that I should mention it, except Satan."

Bishr related to me this, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid related to me, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Ma'qil relating from his father that the rock where Musa took refuge is the rock beyond the River of the Wolf (in ʿArāʾis al-Majālis by al-Tha'labi the exegete, Halabi edition, p. 218: "beyond the River of the Olive Oil") on the road. ﴿And it took its way into the sea in an amazing manner﴾: he was amazed by it.

As for others:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu ʿĀsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿in the sea, amazingly﴾: He said: Musa was amazed at the trace of the fish in the sea and its winding passages in which it disappeared, and he found al-Khidr there.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Al-Hasan related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿And it took its way into the sea in an amazing manner﴾: When Musa found that the fish had taken its way into the sea amazingly, he was amazed at the tunnel the fish made.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿And it took its way into the sea in an amazing manner﴾: He said: By Allah, it was amazing, a fish from which people had been eating for ages. What is more amazing than a fish from which people ate for an age of the ages, and then it became alive and was gathered into the sea?

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The fish would not touch anything in the sea without it drying up until it became a rock, and the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was amazed at that.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn ʿAtiyyah related to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Thabit related to us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words, ﴿And it took its way into the sea in an amazing manner﴾: He said: It means the tunnel of the fish in the sea was amazing to Musa.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿He said, "That is what we were seeking." So they retraced their steps, following their own traces (qasasan) (18:64). They found a servant of Ours, whom We had granted mercy from Us and taught knowledge from Our presence (18:65)﴾

His exalted saying: ﴿He said﴾ Musa said to his young man, ﴿That﴾, meaning by it, your forgetting the fish, ﴿is what we were seeking﴾, meaning: what we were looking for and seeking. Musa had been told: "Your companion whom you seek is where the fish will leave you."

As related to us:
Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿That is what we were seeking﴾: Musa said, "That is when you informed me that I would find al-Khidr, where the fish would escape me."

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "where the fish would part from me."

* *

His saying: ﴿So they retraced their steps, following their own traces (qasasan)﴾
Meaning: they returned along the path they had traversed, going back on their heels, tracing the traces they had followed.

Similar to what we have said has been said by the people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., the scholars of exegesis).

Those who said this:
Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿qasasan﴾: He said: Musa and his young man followed the trace of the fish, and they split the sea, returning.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿So they retraced their steps, following their own traces﴾: He said: Musa and his young man followed the trace of the fish through the split in the sea, while Musa and his young man were returning, and Musa was marveling at the trace of the fish in the sea, and at its windings where it had vanished.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: They returned by the way they had come, ﴿retracing their steps﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said regarding His saying, ﴿That is what we were seeking; so they retraced their steps, following their own traces﴾: "That is, they followed their traces until they reached the entrance of the fish."

* *

His saying: ﴿And they found a servant of Ours, whom We had granted mercy from Us﴾
Meaning: We bestowed upon him mercy from Us, ﴿and taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾, meaning: We taught him knowledge from Us as well.

As related to us:
Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿knowledge from Our presence﴾: that is, knowledge from Us. The reason for the journey of Musa (ﷺ) and his young man, and his meeting this scholar whom God mentioned in this passage, was, as has been reported, that Musa was asked, "Is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you?" He said, "No." Or, his own soul suggested this to him, and God disliked that for him. So God wished to make him aware that among His servants on earth there is one more knowledgeable than he is, and that it was not for him to pass judgment on what he had no knowledge of, but rather he should have referred that matter to the One who knows.

Others said: Rather, the reason for this was that he asked God, exalted is His praise, to direct him to a scholar from whom he might gain knowledge beyond his own.

Those who said this:
Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Harun ibn Antarah, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Musa asked his Lord and said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You?" He said: "The one who remembers Me and does not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants is most just in judgment?" He said: "The one who judges by the truth and does not follow desire." He said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most knowledgeable?" He said: "The one who seeks the knowledge of people in addition to his own knowledge, perhaps he will hear a word that guides him to right guidance or turns him back from ruin." He said: "My Lord, is there anyone on earth?" [[Meaning more knowledgeable; take note.]] He said: "Yes." He said: "My Lord, who is he?" He said: "Al-Khidr." He said: "And where shall I seek him?" He said: "On the shore, by the rock where the fish will escape." So Musa set out seeking him, until what God mentioned happened, and Musa reached him at the rock. Each of them greeted the other, and Musa said to him: "I wish that you would let me accompany you." He said: "You will not be able to bear my company." He said: "Indeed." He said: "If you accompany me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you." So they set out, until when they boarded the ship, he tore it. He said: "Have you torn it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing." He said: "Did I not say that you would not be able to bear patience with me?" He said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair." So they set out until they met a boy, and he killed him. He said: "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul to be avenged? You have certainly done an abhorrent thing." ... up to His saying: ﴿you could have taken a wage for it﴾. He said: So Musa's words about the wall were for himself, seeking something of the world, and his words about the ship and the boy were for God. ﴿He said, "This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience."﴾ Then he informed him about what he had said concerning the ship, the boy, and the wall. He said: Then he traveled with him over the sea until he reached the confluence of the seas, and there is no place on earth with more water than it. He said: Your Lord sent the sparrow (khuttaf), and it began drinking from it with its beak. It was said to Musa, "How much do you think this sparrow has taken (ra'a) from this water?" He said, "How little it has taken!" It said, "O Musa, my knowledge and your knowledge, in comparison with the knowledge of God, are like what this sparrow has drawn from this water." Musa had been thinking to himself that no one was more knowledgeable than he, or he had said so; therefore he was commanded to go to al-Khidr. [[Ra'a: he struck or diminished.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Musa addressed the Children of Israel and said: "No one is more knowledgeable of God and of His command than I am." So God revealed to him that he should go to this man.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, that it was said to him: "The sign of your meeting him is that you will forget some of your provisions." So he set out with his young man Yusha' ibn Nun, and they took with them a salted fish. When they reached the place God willed, God returned the fish to life, and it slipped into the sea; the fish took its path as a tunnel in the sea, and it slipped into it. ﴿So when they had passed beyond, he said to his young man, "Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours."﴾ ... until ﴿and it took its way into the sea in a wondrous manner﴾. So Musa's taking of its way in the sea was a wonder, and he kept marveling at the slipping of the fish.

Al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Musa followed the trace of the fish, he came to a man lying asleep, covered with his garment. Musa greeted him, and the man uncovered his face and returned the greeting, and said: "Who are you?" He said: "Musa." He said: "The one of the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did you not have enough business with the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes, but I was commanded to come to you and accompany you." He said: "You will not be able to bear patience with me," as God related, ﴿until﴾ reaching, ﴿when they boarded the ship, he tore it﴾, Musa's companion ﴿said: "Have you torn it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾ meaning: abhorrent. ﴿He said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair." So they set out until they met a boy and he killed him. He said: "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul to be avenged?"﴾

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: "Nawf claims that al-Khidr was not the companion of Musa." He said: "The enemy of God lies. Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to us from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'Musa stood up among the Children of Israel to address them, and it was asked, "Which of the people is most knowledgeable?" He said, "I am." So God rebuked him because he did not refer knowledge back to Him. He said: "Yes, a servant of Mine is at the meeting place of the two seas." He said: "My Lord, how can I reach him?" It was said: "Take a fish and place it in a basket. Then say to your young man: when you lose this fish, inform me." So they set out walking along the shore of the sea until they came to a rock, and Musa slept. The fish stirred in the basket, came out, and fell into the sea. God held back the flow of water from it, so that it became like an arch, and it became a tunnel for the fish, and this was a wonder to them both. Then they set out. When the next day came, Musa said to his young man: "Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours." He said: Musa did not feel the fatigue until he had passed the place God had commanded him. He said: So he said, "Do you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it; and it took its way into the sea in a wondrous manner." He said: So he said, "That is what we were seeking," so they retraced their steps, following their own traces, qasasan.'" He said: "They traced their traces." He said: "They came to the rock, and there was a man sleeping, covered with his garment. Musa greeted him, and he said: 'How is there greeting in our land?' He said: 'I am Musa.' He said: 'Musa of the Children of Israel?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'O Musa, I am upon knowledge from the knowledge of God, which God taught me and you do not know; and you are upon knowledge from His knowledge, which He taught you and I do not know.' He said: 'I will follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, as guidance.' He said: 'If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you.' So they set out walking along the shore, and al-Khidr was recognized, and he was carried without a fare. A sparrow came and alighted on the edge of the boat and pecked, or pecked in the water. Al-Khidr said to Musa: 'My knowledge and your knowledge, in comparison with the knowledge of God, is no more than the amount this sparrow has pecked, or diminished, from the sea.'" Abu Ja'far al-Tabari was uncertain, and in his book it is "pecked." He said: "Then, while he was [doing this], Musa came upon him just as he was driving a stake or pulling out a plank from it. Musa said to him: 'We were carried without a fare, and you tear it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing.' He said: 'Did I not say that you would not be able to bear patience with me?' He said: 'Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot.' He said: 'The first was from Musa a forgetting.' He said: 'Then they went out and set off walking, and they saw a boy playing with other boys, and he seized his head and killed him. Musa said to him: "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul to be avenged? You have certainly done a dreadful thing." He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to bear patience with me?" He said: "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me as your companion; you have reached an excuse from my side." He said: So they set out until, when they came to the people of a village and asked its people for food, they did not find anyone to feed them or give them drink. They found in it a wall about to collapse, and he set it upright with his hand. He said: He wiped it with his hand. Musa said to him: "They did not host us, nor did they give us lodging. If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it." He said: "This is the parting between me and you." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I wish that he had been patient until he related to us their story."'"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 64–65 (part 2 of 2):
