⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Umarah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I sat with Ibn Abbas, and with him were a group of the People of the Book. Some of them said: "O Abu al-Abbas, Nawf al-Bikali, the son of Ka'b's wife, claims on the authority of Ka'b that Musa, the Prophet who sought the knowledge-possessor, is in fact Musa ibn Maysha." Sa'id said: Ibn Abbas said: "Does Nawf say this?" Sa'id said: I said to him, "Yes, I heard Nawf say that." He said: "Did you hear it yourself, O Sa'id?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Nawf has lied." Then Ibn Abbas said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Musa, the prophet of the Children of Israel, asked his Lord, saying: 'O Lord, if there is among Your servants one who is more knowledgeable than I, then guide me to him.' He said to him: 'Yes, among My servants there is one who is more knowledgeable than you.' Then He described his location to him and permitted him to meet him. Musa set out with his servant (fata), and with him was a fine fish. It had been said to him: 'When this fish comes back to life at a place, your companion is there, and you have attained your goal.' Musa set out with his servant, and with him was that fish, which they carried. He journeyed until the journey wearied him and he reached the rock and that water, the water of life; whoever drinks of it becomes immortal, and nothing dead that comes near it fails to come back to life. When they dismounted and the water touched the fish, it came back to life and took its path into the sea, a tunnel. So they set off. When they had passed the place where they had turned back, Musa said: 'Bring us our morning meal; indeed we have met with fatigue from this journey of ours.' The youth said, and mentioned: 'Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it but Satan, that I should mention it; and it took its path into the sea in a marvelous way.'" Ibn Abbas said: Musa climbed onto the rock when they reached it, and behold, there was a man wrapped in his garment. Musa greeted him, and the knowledge-possessor returned the greeting. Then he said to him: "What brought you here? Do you have a matter with your people?" Musa said to him: "I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance." ﴿He said: "Indeed you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ He was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, and he had been taught that. Musa said: "Yes." He said: ﴿"And how can you have patience with that which you do not encompass in knowledge?"﴾ That is: you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not encompassed from the knowledge of the unseen what I know. ﴿He said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any command."﴾ Even if you see what contradicts me. He said: ﴿"If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything"﴾ even if you disapprove of it, ﴿"until I myself mention it to you."﴾ They set off walking along the shore of the sea, seeking people, asking for someone to carry them, until a new, sturdy ship passed by them, and none of the ships that had passed them was finer, more beautiful, or sturdier than it. They asked its people to carry them, and they carried them. When they had settled in it and it had sailed with them and its people, he took out a chisel and a hammer, then went to one side of it and struck it with the chisel until he made a hole in it, then took a plank and fitted it over the hole, then sat on it mending it. Musa said to him, seeing a matter that appalled him: ﴿"Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾ ﴿He said: "Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ ﴿He said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot,"﴾ that is: what you left of your covenant, ﴿"and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair."﴾ Then they went out of the ship and walked on until they came to the people of a town, and behold, boys were playing outside it, and among the boys was a boy more handsome than them all, and none was more prosperous or more pleasing than him. He took him by the hand and took a stone, and struck his head with it until he crushed it and killed him. Musa saw a terrible matter that he could not bear: a small child who had committed no sin. ﴿He said: "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul to justify it?"﴾ that is: a small one without any soul. ﴿"Certainly you have done a dreadful thing."﴾ ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ ﴿He said: "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep company with me; you have indeed reached an excuse from my side."﴾ That is: you have made excuses regarding my affair. ﴿So they went on until, when they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, they refused to host them; and they found in it a wall about to collapse﴾, so he rebuilt it, then sat down to build it. Musa grew impatient at what he saw him doing of the burden of a task for which he had no patience, and said: ﴿"If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it."﴾ That is: we asked them for food and they did not feed us, we asked them for hospitality and they did not host us, then you sat down without any favor, and had you wished you could have been given a wage for your work. ﴿He said: "This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience. As for the ship, it belonged to needy people who work in the sea, so I wanted to damage it, for behind them was a king who seizes every ship by force";﴾ and in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "every good ship." I only damaged it so that I might turn him away from it, and it was saved when he saw the defect I had made in it. ﴿"As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would burden them with transgression and disbelief, so we wished that their Lord would replace him for them with one better than him in purity and nearer in compassion." "As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord willed that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord";﴾ that is: I did not do it of my own self. ﴿"That is the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience."﴾ Ibn Abbas used to say: "The treasure was nothing but knowledge."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Umarah, from his father, from Ikrimah, who said: It was said to Ibn Abbas: "We have not heard Musa's servant mention any narration," and Ibn Abbas, concerning what is mentioned of the narration of the servant, said: The servant drank from the water and became immortal. The knowledge-possessor took him, and fastened him to a ship, then sent him into the sea; indeed it churns with him until the Day of Resurrection. That was because it was not permitted for him to drink from it, yet he drank.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And when Musa said to his servant, "I will not cease until I reach the meeting place of the two seas, or I will continue for a long time"﴾. He said: When Musa and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When the dwelling became settled for them, Allah revealed to him: ﴿"And remind them of the days of Allah"﴾. So he addressed his people and recalled to them what Allah had given them of good and blessing, and reminded them when Allah saved them from the family of Pharaoh, and reminded them of the destruction of their enemy, and that Allah had made them successors on the earth. He said: "Allah spoke to your Prophet directly, and chose me for Himself, and sent down upon me love from Him, and Allah has given you of all that you asked for; your Prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah." He left out no blessing that Allah had bestowed upon them without mentioning it and making it known to them. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: "So it is, O Prophet of Allah; we have recognized what you say. Is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "No." So Allah sent Jibril to Musa, peace be upon them both, and he said: "Indeed Allah says: 'Do you know where I place My knowledge? Yes, on the shore of the sea there is a man more knowledgeable than you.'" Ibn Abbas said: "He is al-Khidr." Musa asked his Lord to show him him, and Allah revealed to him: "Go to the sea, for you will find on the shore of the sea a fish; take it and hand it to your servant, then keep to the shore of the sea. When you forget the fish and it is lost from you, there you will find the righteous servant you seek." When the journey of Musa, the Prophet of Allah, lengthened and he became weary in it, he asked his servant about the fish. His servant, who was his attendant, said to him: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it but Satan, that I should mention it."﴾ The servant said: "I saw the fish when it took its path into the sea as a tunnel." This amazed Musa, so he returned until he came to the rock, and found the fish splashing in the sea, and Musa followed the fish. Musa advanced his staff, parting the water with it, following the fish, and the fish did not touch anything of the sea without it drying up until it became a rock. The Prophet of Allah marveled at this until the fish brought him to an island among the islands of the sea, where he met al-Khidr and greeted him. Al-Khidr said: "And upon you be peace. How is there greeting in this land? Who are you?" He said: "I am Musa." Al-Khidr said to him: "Are you the Musa of the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes." He welcomed him and said: "What brought you?" He said: "I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance." ﴿He said: "Indeed you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ He said: "You cannot endure that." Musa said: ﴿"You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any command."﴾ He said: So he set off with him, and said to him: "Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its matter to you." That is His saying: ﴿"Until I myself mention it to you."﴾ They boarded the ship, desiring the land; al-Khidr stood up and made a hole in the ship. Musa said to him: ﴿"Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿But when they reached the meeting place of the two seas, they forgot their fish﴾. It is mentioned that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, when he had crossed the sea and Allah had saved him from the family of Pharaoh, gathered the Children of Israel and addressed them, saying: "You are the best of the people of the earth and the most knowledgeable. Allah has destroyed your enemy, has brought you across the sea, and has sent down the Torah to you." It was then said to him: "Here there is a man more knowledgeable than you." He said: So he and his servant Yusha' ibn Nun set off seeking him, and they took a salted fish in a basket with them, and it was said to them: "When you forget what you have with you, you will meet a knowledgeable man called al-Khidr." When they reached that place, Allah returned life to the fish, and it made a path for itself through the sea-channel until it reached the sea, then it went on, and wherever it went it turned the water into solid ground. He said: Musa and his servant went on, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So when they had passed beyond it, he said to his servant, "Bring us our morning meal; indeed we have met with fatigue from this journey of ours." He said, "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish..."﴾ ...then he recited up to His words: ﴿"and We taught him knowledge from Us"﴾. They met a knowledgeable man called al-Khidr. It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Al-Khidr was only called Khidr because he sat upon a white patch of land, and it suddenly became green beneath him."¹

⁕ Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to us, saying: al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn Abbas, that he disputed with al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari about the companion of Musa. Ibn Abbas said: "He is Khidr." Then Ubayy ibn Ka'b passed by them, and Ibn Abbas called him and said: "I and my companion here have disputed about the companion of Musa who sought the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention his affair?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'While Musa was among an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: "Do you know of anyone more knowledgeable than you?" Musa said: "No." So Allah revealed to Musa: "Yes, Our servant Khidr." Musa asked the way to meet him, so Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: "When you lose the fish, return, for you will meet him." Musa followed the trail of the fish in the sea, and Musa's servant said to him: "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish." Musa said: "That is what we were seeking." So they retraced their steps, following their traces, and they found Our servant Khidr, and what passed between them was what Allah related in His Book.'"

⁕ Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Numayri narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Yazid, who said: I heard al-Zuhri narrate, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud informed me, from Ibn Abbas, that he disputed with al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari about the companion of Musa, then he mentioned approximately the narration of al-Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿He said, "That is what we were seeking." So they retraced their steps, following their own traces (qasasan) (18:64). They found a servant of Ours, whom We had granted mercy from Us and taught knowledge from Our presence (18:65)﴾

His exalted saying: ﴿He said﴾ Musa said to his young man, ﴿That﴾, meaning by it, your forgetting the fish, ﴿is what we were seeking﴾, meaning: what we were looking for and seeking. Musa had been told: "Your companion whom you seek is where the fish will leave you."

As related to us:
Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿That is what we were seeking﴾: Musa said, "That is when you informed me that I would find al-Khidr, where the fish would escape me."

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "where the fish would part from me."

* *

His saying: ﴿So they retraced their steps, following their own traces (qasasan)﴾
Meaning: they returned along the path they had traversed, going back on their heels, tracing the traces they had followed.

Similar to what we have said has been said by the people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., the scholars of exegesis).

Those who said this:
Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿qasasan﴾: He said: Musa and his young man followed the trace of the fish, and they split the sea, returning.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿So they retraced their steps, following their own traces﴾: He said: Musa and his young man followed the trace of the fish through the split in the sea, while Musa and his young man were returning, and Musa was marveling at the trace of the fish in the sea, and at its windings where it had vanished.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: They returned by the way they had come, ﴿retracing their steps﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said regarding His saying, ﴿That is what we were seeking; so they retraced their steps, following their own traces﴾: "That is, they followed their traces until they reached the entrance of the fish."

* *

His saying: ﴿And they found a servant of Ours, whom We had granted mercy from Us﴾
Meaning: We bestowed upon him mercy from Us, ﴿and taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾, meaning: We taught him knowledge from Us as well.

As related to us:
Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿knowledge from Our presence﴾: that is, knowledge from Us. The reason for the journey of Musa (ﷺ) and his young man, and his meeting this scholar whom God mentioned in this passage, was, as has been reported, that Musa was asked, "Is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you?" He said, "No." Or, his own soul suggested this to him, and God disliked that for him. So God wished to make him aware that among His servants on earth there is one more knowledgeable than he is, and that it was not for him to pass judgment on what he had no knowledge of, but rather he should have referred that matter to the One who knows.

Others said: Rather, the reason for this was that he asked God, exalted is His praise, to direct him to a scholar from whom he might gain knowledge beyond his own.

Those who said this:
Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Harun ibn Antarah, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Musa asked his Lord and said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You?" He said: "The one who remembers Me and does not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants is most just in judgment?" He said: "The one who judges by the truth and does not follow desire." He said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most knowledgeable?" He said: "The one who seeks the knowledge of people in addition to his own knowledge, perhaps he will hear a word that guides him to right guidance or turns him back from ruin." He said: "My Lord, is there anyone on earth?" [[Meaning more knowledgeable; take note.]] He said: "Yes." He said: "My Lord, who is he?" He said: "Al-Khidr." He said: "And where shall I seek him?" He said: "On the shore, by the rock where the fish will escape." So Musa set out seeking him, until what God mentioned happened, and Musa reached him at the rock. Each of them greeted the other, and Musa said to him: "I wish that you would let me accompany you." He said: "You will not be able to bear my company." He said: "Indeed." He said: "If you accompany me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you." So they set out, until when they boarded the ship, he tore it. He said: "Have you torn it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing." He said: "Did I not say that you would not be able to bear patience with me?" He said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair." So they set out until they met a boy, and he killed him. He said: "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul to be avenged? You have certainly done an abhorrent thing." ... up to His saying: ﴿you could have taken a wage for it﴾. He said: So Musa's words about the wall were for himself, seeking something of the world, and his words about the ship and the boy were for God. ﴿He said, "This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience."﴾ Then he informed him about what he had said concerning the ship, the boy, and the wall. He said: Then he traveled with him over the sea until he reached the confluence of the seas, and there is no place on earth with more water than it. He said: Your Lord sent the sparrow (khuttaf), and it began drinking from it with its beak. It was said to Musa, "How much do you think this sparrow has taken (ra'a) from this water?" He said, "How little it has taken!" It said, "O Musa, my knowledge and your knowledge, in comparison with the knowledge of God, are like what this sparrow has drawn from this water." Musa had been thinking to himself that no one was more knowledgeable than he, or he had said so; therefore he was commanded to go to al-Khidr. [[Ra'a: he struck or diminished.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Musa addressed the Children of Israel and said: "No one is more knowledgeable of God and of His command than I am." So God revealed to him that he should go to this man.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, that it was said to him: "The sign of your meeting him is that you will forget some of your provisions." So he set out with his young man Yusha' ibn Nun, and they took with them a salted fish. When they reached the place God willed, God returned the fish to life, and it slipped into the sea; the fish took its path as a tunnel in the sea, and it slipped into it. ﴿So when they had passed beyond, he said to his young man, "Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours."﴾ ... until ﴿and it took its way into the sea in a wondrous manner﴾. So Musa's taking of its way in the sea was a wonder, and he kept marveling at the slipping of the fish.

Al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Musa followed the trace of the fish, he came to a man lying asleep, covered with his garment. Musa greeted him, and the man uncovered his face and returned the greeting, and said: "Who are you?" He said: "Musa." He said: "The one of the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did you not have enough business with the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes, but I was commanded to come to you and accompany you." He said: "You will not be able to bear patience with me," as God related, ﴿until﴾ reaching, ﴿when they boarded the ship, he tore it﴾, Musa's companion ﴿said: "Have you torn it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾ meaning: abhorrent. ﴿He said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair." So they set out until they met a boy and he killed him. He said: "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul to be avenged?"﴾

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: "Nawf claims that al-Khidr was not the companion of Musa." He said: "The enemy of God lies. Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to us from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'Musa stood up among the Children of Israel to address them, and it was asked, "Which of the people is most knowledgeable?" He said, "I am." So God rebuked him because he did not refer knowledge back to Him. He said: "Yes, a servant of Mine is at the meeting place of the two seas." He said: "My Lord, how can I reach him?" It was said: "Take a fish and place it in a basket. Then say to your young man: when you lose this fish, inform me." So they set out walking along the shore of the sea until they came to a rock, and Musa slept. The fish stirred in the basket, came out, and fell into the sea. God held back the flow of water from it, so that it became like an arch, and it became a tunnel for the fish, and this was a wonder to them both. Then they set out. When the next day came, Musa said to his young man: "Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours." He said: Musa did not feel the fatigue until he had passed the place God had commanded him. He said: So he said, "Do you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it; and it took its way into the sea in a wondrous manner." He said: So he said, "That is what we were seeking," so they retraced their steps, following their own traces, qasasan.'" He said: "They traced their traces." He said: "They came to the rock, and there was a man sleeping, covered with his garment. Musa greeted him, and he said: 'How is there greeting in our land?' He said: 'I am Musa.' He said: 'Musa of the Children of Israel?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'O Musa, I am upon knowledge from the knowledge of God, which God taught me and you do not know; and you are upon knowledge from His knowledge, which He taught you and I do not know.' He said: 'I will follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, as guidance.' He said: 'If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you.' So they set out walking along the shore, and al-Khidr was recognized, and he was carried without a fare. A sparrow came and alighted on the edge of the boat and pecked, or pecked in the water. Al-Khidr said to Musa: 'My knowledge and your knowledge, in comparison with the knowledge of God, is no more than the amount this sparrow has pecked, or diminished, from the sea.'" Abu Ja'far al-Tabari was uncertain, and in his book it is "pecked." He said: "Then, while he was [doing this], Musa came upon him just as he was driving a stake or pulling out a plank from it. Musa said to him: 'We were carried without a fare, and you tear it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing.' He said: 'Did I not say that you would not be able to bear patience with me?' He said: 'Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot.' He said: 'The first was from Musa a forgetting.' He said: 'Then they went out and set off walking, and they saw a boy playing with other boys, and he seized his head and killed him. Musa said to him: "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul to be avenged? You have certainly done a dreadful thing." He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to bear patience with me?" He said: "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me as your companion; you have reached an excuse from my side." He said: So they set out until, when they came to the people of a village and asked its people for food, they did not find anyone to feed them or give them drink. They found in it a wall about to collapse, and he set it upright with his hand. He said: He wiped it with his hand. Musa said to him: "They did not host us, nor did they give us lodging. If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it." He said: "This is the parting between me and you." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I wish that he had been patient until he related to us their story."'"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 64–65 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Umarah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I sat with Ibn Abbas, and with him were a group of the People of the Book. Some of them said: "O Abu al-Abbas, Nawf al-Bikali, the son of Ka'b's wife, claims on the authority of Ka'b that Musa, the Prophet who sought the knowledge-possessor, is in fact Musa ibn Maysha." Sa'id said: Ibn Abbas said: "Does Nawf say this?" Sa'id said: I said to him, "Yes, I heard Nawf say that." He said: "Did you hear it yourself, O Sa'id?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Nawf has lied." Then Ibn Abbas said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Musa, the prophet of the Children of Israel, asked his Lord, saying: 'O Lord, if there is among Your servants one who is more knowledgeable than I, then guide me to him.' He said to him: 'Yes, among My servants there is one who is more knowledgeable than you.' Then He described his location to him and permitted him to meet him. Musa set out with his servant (fata), and with him was a fine fish. It had been said to him: 'When this fish comes back to life at a place, your companion is there, and you have attained your goal.' Musa set out with his servant, and with him was that fish, which they carried. He journeyed until the journey wearied him and he reached the rock and that water, the water of life; whoever drinks of it becomes immortal, and nothing dead that comes near it fails to come back to life. When they dismounted and the water touched the fish, it came back to life and took its path into the sea, a tunnel. So they set off. When they had passed the place where they had turned back, Musa said: 'Bring us our morning meal; indeed we have met with fatigue from this journey of ours.' The youth said, and mentioned: 'Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it but Satan, that I should mention it; and it took its path into the sea in a marvelous way.'" Ibn Abbas said: Musa climbed onto the rock when they reached it, and behold, there was a man wrapped in his garment. Musa greeted him, and the knowledge-possessor returned the greeting. Then he said to him: "What brought you here? Do you have a matter with your people?" Musa said to him: "I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance." ﴿He said: "Indeed you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ He was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, and he had been taught that. Musa said: "Yes." He said: ﴿"And how can you have patience with that which you do not encompass in knowledge?"﴾ That is: you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not encompassed from the knowledge of the unseen what I know. ﴿He said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any command."﴾ Even if you see what contradicts me. He said: ﴿"If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything"﴾ even if you disapprove of it, ﴿"until I myself mention it to you."﴾ They set off walking along the shore of the sea, seeking people, asking for someone to carry them, until a new, sturdy ship passed by them, and none of the ships that had passed them was finer, more beautiful, or sturdier than it. They asked its people to carry them, and they carried them. When they had settled in it and it had sailed with them and its people, he took out a chisel and a hammer, then went to one side of it and struck it with the chisel until he made a hole in it, then took a plank and fitted it over the hole, then sat on it mending it. Musa said to him, seeing a matter that appalled him: ﴿"Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾ ﴿He said: "Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ ﴿He said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot,"﴾ that is: what you left of your covenant, ﴿"and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair."﴾ Then they went out of the ship and walked on until they came to the people of a town, and behold, boys were playing outside it, and among the boys was a boy more handsome than them all, and none was more prosperous or more pleasing than him. He took him by the hand and took a stone, and struck his head with it until he crushed it and killed him. Musa saw a terrible matter that he could not bear: a small child who had committed no sin. ﴿He said: "Have you killed a pure soul without a soul to justify it?"﴾ that is: a small one without any soul. ﴿"Certainly you have done a dreadful thing."﴾ ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ ﴿He said: "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep company with me; you have indeed reached an excuse from my side."﴾ That is: you have made excuses regarding my affair. ﴿So they went on until, when they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, they refused to host them; and they found in it a wall about to collapse﴾, so he rebuilt it, then sat down to build it. Musa grew impatient at what he saw him doing of the burden of a task for which he had no patience, and said: ﴿"If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it."﴾ That is: we asked them for food and they did not feed us, we asked them for hospitality and they did not host us, then you sat down without any favor, and had you wished you could have been given a wage for your work. ﴿He said: "This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience. As for the ship, it belonged to needy people who work in the sea, so I wanted to damage it, for behind them was a king who seizes every ship by force";﴾ and in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "every good ship." I only damaged it so that I might turn him away from it, and it was saved when he saw the defect I had made in it. ﴿"As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would burden them with transgression and disbelief, so we wished that their Lord would replace him for them with one better than him in purity and nearer in compassion." "As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord willed that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord";﴾ that is: I did not do it of my own self. ﴿"That is the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience."﴾ Ibn Abbas used to say: "The treasure was nothing but knowledge."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Umarah, from his father, from Ikrimah, who said: It was said to Ibn Abbas: "We have not heard Musa's servant mention any narration," and Ibn Abbas, concerning what is mentioned of the narration of the servant, said: The servant drank from the water and became immortal. The knowledge-possessor took him, and fastened him to a ship, then sent him into the sea; indeed it churns with him until the Day of Resurrection. That was because it was not permitted for him to drink from it, yet he drank.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And when Musa said to his servant, "I will not cease until I reach the meeting place of the two seas, or I will continue for a long time"﴾. He said: When Musa and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When the dwelling became settled for them, Allah revealed to him: ﴿"And remind them of the days of Allah"﴾. So he addressed his people and recalled to them what Allah had given them of good and blessing, and reminded them when Allah saved them from the family of Pharaoh, and reminded them of the destruction of their enemy, and that Allah had made them successors on the earth. He said: "Allah spoke to your Prophet directly, and chose me for Himself, and sent down upon me love from Him, and Allah has given you of all that you asked for; your Prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah." He left out no blessing that Allah had bestowed upon them without mentioning it and making it known to them. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: "So it is, O Prophet of Allah; we have recognized what you say. Is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "No." So Allah sent Jibril to Musa, peace be upon them both, and he said: "Indeed Allah says: 'Do you know where I place My knowledge? Yes, on the shore of the sea there is a man more knowledgeable than you.'" Ibn Abbas said: "He is al-Khidr." Musa asked his Lord to show him him, and Allah revealed to him: "Go to the sea, for you will find on the shore of the sea a fish; take it and hand it to your servant, then keep to the shore of the sea. When you forget the fish and it is lost from you, there you will find the righteous servant you seek." When the journey of Musa, the Prophet of Allah, lengthened and he became weary in it, he asked his servant about the fish. His servant, who was his attendant, said to him: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it but Satan, that I should mention it."﴾ The servant said: "I saw the fish when it took its path into the sea as a tunnel." This amazed Musa, so he returned until he came to the rock, and found the fish splashing in the sea, and Musa followed the fish. Musa advanced his staff, parting the water with it, following the fish, and the fish did not touch anything of the sea without it drying up until it became a rock. The Prophet of Allah marveled at this until the fish brought him to an island among the islands of the sea, where he met al-Khidr and greeted him. Al-Khidr said: "And upon you be peace. How is there greeting in this land? Who are you?" He said: "I am Musa." Al-Khidr said to him: "Are you the Musa of the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes." He welcomed him and said: "What brought you?" He said: "I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance." ﴿He said: "Indeed you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ He said: "You cannot endure that." Musa said: ﴿"You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any command."﴾ He said: So he set off with him, and said to him: "Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its matter to you." That is His saying: ﴿"Until I myself mention it to you."﴾ They boarded the ship, desiring the land; al-Khidr stood up and made a hole in the ship. Musa said to him: ﴿"Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿But when they reached the meeting place of the two seas, they forgot their fish﴾. It is mentioned that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, when he had crossed the sea and Allah had saved him from the family of Pharaoh, gathered the Children of Israel and addressed them, saying: "You are the best of the people of the earth and the most knowledgeable. Allah has destroyed your enemy, has brought you across the sea, and has sent down the Torah to you." It was then said to him: "Here there is a man more knowledgeable than you." He said: So he and his servant Yusha' ibn Nun set off seeking him, and they took a salted fish in a basket with them, and it was said to them: "When you forget what you have with you, you will meet a knowledgeable man called al-Khidr." When they reached that place, Allah returned life to the fish, and it made a path for itself through the sea-channel until it reached the sea, then it went on, and wherever it went it turned the water into solid ground. He said: Musa and his servant went on, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So when they had passed beyond it, he said to his servant, "Bring us our morning meal; indeed we have met with fatigue from this journey of ours." He said, "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish..."﴾ ...then he recited up to His words: ﴿"and We taught him knowledge from Us"﴾. They met a knowledgeable man called al-Khidr. It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Al-Khidr was only called Khidr because he sat upon a white patch of land, and it suddenly became green beneath him."¹

⁕ Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to us, saying: al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn Abbas, that he disputed with al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari about the companion of Musa. Ibn Abbas said: "He is Khidr." Then Ubayy ibn Ka'b passed by them, and Ibn Abbas called him and said: "I and my companion here have disputed about the companion of Musa who sought the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention his affair?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'While Musa was among an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: "Do you know of anyone more knowledgeable than you?" Musa said: "No." So Allah revealed to Musa: "Yes, Our servant Khidr." Musa asked the way to meet him, so Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: "When you lose the fish, return, for you will meet him." Musa followed the trail of the fish in the sea, and Musa's servant said to him: "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed I forgot the fish." Musa said: "That is what we were seeking." So they retraced their steps, following their traces, and they found Our servant Khidr, and what passed between them was what Allah related in His Book.'"

⁕ Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Numayri narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Yazid, who said: I heard al-Zuhri narrate, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud informed me, from Ibn Abbas, that he disputed with al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari about the companion of Musa, then he mentioned approximately the narration of al-Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 66–67:

The explanation of the words of His, the Exalted: ﴿Moses said to him, "May I follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, [that which is] right guidance?" (66) He said, "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ (67)

His Exalted remembrance says: Moses said to the scholar (al-'alim), ﴿May I follow you on condition that you teach me﴾ of the knowledge that God has taught you, that which is guidance toward the truth and a sign of the right path?

﴿He said, "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾

His Exalted remembrance says: The scholar said, "Indeed, you will not be able to endure patience with me, for I act according to the inner knowledge (batin 'ilm) that God has taught me, while you have knowledge only of the outward (zahir) matters. So you will not be patient with what you see of the actions, as we have mentioned from the report from Ibn 'Abbas earlier, that he was a man who acted upon the unseen and had knowledge of that."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how can you have patience over that which you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾ (68) ﴿He said, "You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ (69)

He, mighty is His remembrance, says, reporting the statement of the scholar (al-'alim) to Musa: "And how can you be patient, O Musa, over the actions you see from me, whose good aspects you have no knowledge of, and remain with me upon them? You judge the correctness of the one who is right and the error of the one who is wrong only by the outward appearance before you and by the extent of your knowledge. My actions occur without a clear proof visible to your eye as to their correctness, because they begin for causes that produce deferred rather than immediate outcomes, and you have no knowledge of what results from them, because it is unseen, and you cannot encompass the knowledge of the unseen with knowledge (khubr, meaning knowledge)." He said: ﴿You will find me, God willing, patient﴾ over what I see from you, even if it contradicts what I consider correct, ﴿and I will not disobey you in any matter﴾. He means: I will comply with what you command me, even if it does not agree with my desire.

* *

He, blessed and exalted is He, says: The scholar said to Musa: "If you follow me now, then do not ask me about anything I do that you find objectionable, for I have already informed you that I perform actions based on the unseen, which you cannot encompass in knowledge." ﴿Until I myself mention to you its explanation﴾ means: until I myself mention to you, from among the actions you see me performing that you find objectionable, what they are, and explain to you their matter, and begin telling you about them.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they set out, until when they boarded the ship, he made a hole in it. [Moses] said, "Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing."﴾ [18:71]

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Moses and the scholar set out, walking and seeking a ship to board. When they reached it and boarded it, the scholar made a hole in the ship. Moses said to him: "Have you made a hole in it after we have been swept out into the sea, ﴿to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing﴾" — meaning: you have done something great, and committed a deed that is reprehensible.

Qatadah narrated to us from Bishr, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿You have certainly done a terrible thing﴾: that is, a marvel. A people had boarded their ship and he made a hole in it when they were most in need of it. But he knew from that what the Prophet of God Moses did not know, from the knowledge of God that He had given him. And he had said to the Prophet of God Moses (peace be upon him): ﴿If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you.﴾

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, ﴿You have certainly done a terrible thing﴾: he says: "munkaran" (a reprehensible thing).

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa' narrated to us; all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿You have certainly done a terrible thing﴾, he said: "munkaran" (reprehensible).

Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it. And "al-imr" in the speech of the Arabs means: a calamity. From it is the saying of the rajiz (rajaz poet):

"The rivals have met from me a reprehensible thing... a great calamity, a grave matter."[[The line is cited by Abu Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (1:409), in explaining His saying "you have done a thing imran" as meaning a great, reprehensible calamity, and in another verse "shay'an idda" (a grievous thing). He cited: "qad baqiya al-aqran..." (the line). In Lisan al-Arab (under "imr"), al-Akhfash says: it is said "amira amruhu yamaru amran" meaning it became intense, and the noun is "al-imr" with a kasra on the hamza. The rajiz said: "qad laqiya..." (the line). It is also said: wonder. And amran imran: reprehensible. In the revealed text: "laqad ji'ta shay'an imra." Abu Ishaq said: meaning you have done a great reprehensible thing. It was said: al-imr with a kasra is a great and shameful matter. It was also said: a marvel. He said: "nukran" is less than "imran," because drowning those in the ship is more reprehensible than killing a single soul. Ibn Sayyid said: al-Kisa'i held that the meaning of "imra" is a calamitous, reprehensible, marvelous thing, derived from the saying of people "amar al-qawm" when they became numerous.]]

Some scholars of the Arabic language used to say: its root is "everything intense and abundant," and from it one says of a people: "they have amara" when they increased and their matter became intense. He said: its verbal noun is "al-amar," and the noun is "al-imr."

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿to drown its people﴾. Most of the readers of Madinah and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿li-tughriqa ahlaha﴾ with the "ta" in "litughriqa" and the "ahl" in the accusative, meaning: you, O man, drown the people of this ship by the hole you made in it. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited "liyaghraqa" (with the "ya") "ahluha" in the nominative, on the basis that the people are the ones who drown.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is to say: both are well-known and widely transmitted recitations among the regional readings, with agreeing meaning though their wording differs; so whichever one the reader recites is correct.

We say they agree in meaning because it is known that Moses's objection to the scholar's making a hole in the ship was only because he believed that such a deed would cause its people to drown if such an act were committed in it. No one is in doubt about this meaning, whether one recites with the "ta" and the accusative, or with the "ya" and the nominative.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 72–73:

The exposition of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ (72) ﴿He said: "Do not blame me for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair."﴾ (73)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿He said﴾, the scholar (al-'alim), to Musa when he said what he said: ﴿"Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ regarding what you see of my actions, for you see what you have not encompassed in knowledge. Musa said to him: ﴿"Do not blame me for what I forgot"﴾. The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: this statement from Musa, peace be upon him, to the scholar was a figurative remark (mu'aridah), not that he had forgotten his covenant, nor had he been given a prior admonition when he accompanied him, with his words: ﴿"If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you."﴾

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to me from Yahya ibn Ziyad, who said: Yahya ibn al-Muhallab narrated to me, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b al-Ansari, regarding His saying: ﴿"Do not blame me for what I forgot"﴾, he said: he did not forget, but these are figurative expressions of speech.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "Do not blame me for my abandoning your covenant," considering that the meaning of forgetting (nisyan) is leaving (tark).

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿"Do not blame me for what I forgot"﴾: that is, for what you abandoned of your covenant.

The correct view on this matter is to say: Musa asked his companion not to blame him for what he forgot of his covenant, concerning his questioning him about the manner and cause of what he did, not for what he asked about; and he was mindful of his covenant. This is consistent with what is authentically related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which explains this meaning in the report, namely:

Narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, who said: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, regarding ﴿"Do not blame me for what I forgot"﴾, he said: "The first [objection] from Musa was forgetfulness."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"And do not burden me with difficulty in my affair"﴾

He says: do not cover me with difficulty in my affair; meaning, do not make my affair constrained for me with you and my companionship with you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 72–73:

The exposition of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ (72) ﴿He said: "Do not blame me for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair."﴾ (73)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿He said﴾, the scholar (al-'alim), to Musa when he said what he said: ﴿"Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ regarding what you see of my actions, for you see what you have not encompassed in knowledge. Musa said to him: ﴿"Do not blame me for what I forgot"﴾. The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: this statement from Musa, peace be upon him, to the scholar was a figurative remark (mu'aridah), not that he had forgotten his covenant, nor had he been given a prior admonition when he accompanied him, with his words: ﴿"If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you."﴾

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to me from Yahya ibn Ziyad, who said: Yahya ibn al-Muhallab narrated to me, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b al-Ansari, regarding His saying: ﴿"Do not blame me for what I forgot"﴾, he said: he did not forget, but these are figurative expressions of speech.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "Do not blame me for my abandoning your covenant," considering that the meaning of forgetting (nisyan) is leaving (tark).

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿"Do not blame me for what I forgot"﴾: that is, for what you abandoned of your covenant.

The correct view on this matter is to say: Musa asked his companion not to blame him for what he forgot of his covenant, concerning his questioning him about the manner and cause of what he did, not for what he asked about; and he was mindful of his covenant. This is consistent with what is authentically related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which explains this meaning in the report, namely:

Narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, who said: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, regarding ﴿"Do not blame me for what I forgot"﴾, he said: "The first [objection] from Musa was forgetfulness."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"And do not burden me with difficulty in my affair"﴾

He says: do not cover me with difficulty in my affair; meaning, do not make my affair constrained for me with you and my companionship with you.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 74:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So they went on until, when they met a boy, he killed him. [Moses] said, "Have you killed a pure soul without [its having killed] another? You have certainly done a terrible thing."﴾

His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿So they went on until, when they met a boy, he killed him﴾ — the scholar (al-'Alim, al-Khidr) — then ﴿[Moses] said﴾ to him: ﴿"Have you killed a pure soul"﴾.

The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Basra read it as (aqatalta nafsan zakiyatan) ("أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا زَاكِيَةً"), and they said its meaning is: pure, one who has no sin, for she had never sinned due to her youth. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿nafsan zakiyyatan﴾ with the meaning: repentant, one whose sins have been forgiven.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Have you killed a pure soul?﴾ "The zakiyya is the repentant one."

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿"He said, 'Have you killed a pure soul?'"﴾ He said: "The zakiyya is the repentant one."

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us: "Aqatalta nafsan zakiyatan" — he said: al-Hasan said: "Repentant." Thus in the hadith of al-Hasan and Shahr, it is zakiyah.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿a pure soul﴾: "Repentant."

Mention of those who said its meaning is: the Muslim who has no sin: al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, he said: Ya'la ibn Muslim informed me that he heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: Khidr found boys playing, so he took a handsome boy, laid him down, and slaughtered him with a knife. He said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i, who said: the name of the boy whom Khidr killed was Jaysur. ﴿"Have you killed a pure soul?"﴾ He said: "A Muslim." He said: Ibn 'Abbas read it as ﴿zakiyya﴾, like your saying: zakiyya.

Some scholars of the Arabic language among the people of Kufa used to say: the meaning of zakiyya and zakiyya is one, like qasiya and qasiyya, and he would say: it is the one who has committed no wrong. That is the correct view in my opinion, because I have found no difference between them in anything of the speech of the Arabs.

Given that this is so, whichever of the two readings the reciter reads is correct, because they are two widely transmitted readings in the recitation of the regions, with one meaning.

* *

As for His words: ﴿without [its having killed] another﴾

He says: without retaliation for a soul she had killed, so that killing became due to her as retaliation (qawadan) for it. As for His words: ﴿You have certainly done a terrible thing (nukran)﴾, He says: you have certainly brought something objectionable, and done an act that is not known.

Those of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿"You have certainly done a terrible thing"﴾ — and al-nukr is more severe than al-imr.

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?" (75) [Musa] said, "If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have already received an excuse from me." (76)﴾**

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: the scholar said to Musa, ﴿"Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾, regarding what you see of My actions, which you have not encompassed in knowledge. Musa said to him, ﴿"If I ask you about anything after this"﴾, meaning after this time, ﴿"then do not keep me as a companion"﴾, meaning, part from me, and do not be a companion to me. ﴿"You have already received an excuse from me"﴾, meaning, you have already reached the limit of excuse concerning me.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madina read ﴿مِنْ لَدُنِي عُذْرًا﴾ with a fatha on the lam, a damma on the dal, and a light nun. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it with a fatha on the lam, a damma on the dal, and a doubled nun. Some of the reciters of Kufa read it with ishmam (a faint rounding) of the damma on the lam, a sukun on the dal, and a light nun. It seems that those who doubled the nun sought for the nun in *ladun* to be free of vowel movement, since it was originally sukun, and if it were not doubled it would have to take a vowel. So they doubled it, out of disliking to vowel it, as they did with *min* and *ʿan* when they attached them to the pronoun of the speaker referring to himself, doubling them and saying *minnī* and *ʿannī*. As for those who lightened it, they found that the pronoun of the speaker referring to himself in the genitive case is a yāʾ alone, without a nūn with it, so they treated *ladun* in accordance with how their speech runs with it and with other words besides it.

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that both are eloquent dialects, and scholars among the reciters have recited the Qur'an with each of them. Whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct. However, the more preferable of the two readings to me is the reading with a fatha on the lam, a damma on the dal, and a doubled nun, for two reasons. The first is that it is the more well-known of the two dialects. The second is that Muhammad ibn Nafiʿ al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Umayya ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Jariya al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited ﴿قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِنْ لَدُنِّي عُذْرًا﴾ with the doubled nun.

* Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hamza al-Zayyat, from Abu Ishaq, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, from the Prophet (ﷺ) the same. He also mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse and said: "Musa was shy before Allah."

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have already received an excuse from me﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Musa was shy before Allah at that point."

* Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hamza al-Zayyat, from Abu Ishaq, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned someone and prayed for him, he would begin with himself. One day he said: "The mercy of Allah be upon us and upon Musa. Had he remained with his companion, he would have seen the wonder. But he said: 'If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have already received an excuse from me'" (doubled).
