God subjected to him his hand, his heart, his opinion, his intellect, his sight and his plotting, so he never erred when he planned, and when he undertook a task he perfected it. He set out leading those peoples, and they followed him. When he came to a sea or a ford, he built boats of small planks like sandals, arranged them within an hour, then placed in them all who were with him of those peoples and those armies. When they crossed the rivers and seas, he dismantled them, and then gave each person a plank, so its weight did not distress him. He continued in this manner until he came to Hawil, and he acted there as he had acted with Nasik. When he finished with it, he continued on his way along the right side of the earth until he reached Manasik at the rising of the sun. He acted there, and formed armies from it as he had done with the two peoples before it. Then he turned back heading along the left side of the earth, intending Tawil, the people opposite Hawil; the two are facing each other, with the breadth of the whole earth between them. When he reached it he acted there, and formed an army from it as he had done before. When he finished with it, he turned from it to the peoples in the middle of the earth, from the jinn and all humanity, and Yajuj and Majuj. When he was in part of the route on the side of the end of the Turks towards the east, a righteous human nation said to him: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, between these two mountains there are creatures of God's creation, and many of them resemble humans [[In ʿArāʾis al-Majālis of al-Tha'labi the exegete (Halabi edition, p. 365) it reads: 'there is no resemblance to humans among them,' and that is more fitting to the context.]], and they are like beasts. They eat grass, and they prey on animals and wild beasts as beasts of prey do, and they eat all the crawling things of the earth, such as snakes and scorpions, and every living creature God has created on earth. No creature of God grows as they grow in one year, nor increases as they increase, nor multiplies as they multiply. If they have a term, according to what we see of their growth and increase, there is no doubt that they will fill the earth, expel its inhabitants from it, prevail over it and corrupt it. No year has passed for us since we have been neighbours to them without our anticipating them and expecting that their first ones will appear to us from between these two mountains." [God says:] ﴿So shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you make a barrier between us and them?﴾ He said: ﴿What my Lord has established me in is better, so help me with strength; I will make between you and them a barrier﴾. Bring me the rocks, the iron and the copper, until I survey their lands, learn their state, and measure the distance between their two mountains.

Then he set off, leading them, until he reached them and passed into the midst of their land. He found them all of one measure, males and females alike. The height of each of them was like half of a man of medium stature among us. They had claws in the place of our fingernails, and molars and fangs like the molars and fangs of beasts of prey, and jaws like the jaws of camels, with a strength such that a sound of movement could be heard when they ate, like the chewing of a camel's cud, or like the gnawing of an old stallion or a strong mare. They were hairy: on their bodies was hair sufficient to cover them and to protect them from heat and cold when these befell them. Each one of them had two large ears: one of them was woolly, its back and belly covered with wool, and the other was downy, its back and belly covered with down. They could wrap themselves in them when they wore them: one of them served as a blanket and the other as a mattress, one they used in summer and the other in winter. Among them, no male or female failed to know the appointed time at which they would die and the end of their lifespan. That is because no male among them dies until a thousand children have come forth from his loins, and no female dies until a thousand children have come forth from her womb. When that happens, they become certain of death. They are provided with the tannin (sea-monster/serpent) during the days of spring, and they pray for rain when they seek it, just as we pray for rain at its appointed time; they cast forth from it one each year, and they eat it throughout the year until the following year. It suffices them, despite their numbers and their growth. When they receive rain, become fertile, live, and grow fat, and its effect is seen upon them, the females yield milk and the males become lustful. When it fails them, they become emaciated and suffer drought, the males become weak and the females become barren, and the effect of that becomes evident upon them. They call to one another like doves, howl like dogs, and mate wherever they meet, like beasts.

When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw this from them, he turned back to the area between the two barriers (al-Saddayn). He measured the distance between them, while he was at the farthest edge of the land of the Turks toward the rising of the sun, and found the distance between them to be one hundred farsakh. When he began his work, he dug a foundation for it until he reached water. Then he made its width fifty farsakh, made its filling of rocks, and its mortar of copper, which was melted and then poured over it, so that it became like a vein of a mountain beneath the earth. Then he raised it and crowned it with blocks of iron and molten copper, and placed between them a vein of yellow copper, so that it became like a striped cloth woven with the yellow and red of copper and the black of iron. When he finished it and made it firm, he set off intending for the community of humankind and jinn. As he was traveling, he came upon a righteous community who guide by the truth and act justly by it. He found a equitable, moderate people who divide equally, judge with justice, support one another and show mercy to one another. Their condition was uniform, their word was one, their characters were alike, their way was upright, their hearts were harmonious, their conduct was good, and their graves were by the doors of their houses. Their houses had no doors, they had no rulers, no judges among them, no rich people, no kings, no nobles. They did not differ, did not vie for superiority, did not disagree, did not quarrel, did not curse one another, did not fight, were not struck by drought, did not become irritable, and were not afflicted by the calamities that afflict people. They were the longest-lived of people, and among them there was no needy person, no poor person, no harsh person, and no coarse person. When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw this of their affair, he marveled at it and said: "Tell me, O people, your story, for I have surveyed the whole earth, its land and sea, its east and west, its light and darkness, and I have not found anyone like you. So tell me your story." They said: "Yes, ask us what you wish." He said: "Tell me, why are the graves of your dead by the doors of your houses?" They said: "We did that deliberately, so that we do not forget death and its remembrance does not leave our hearts." He said: "Then why do your houses have no doors?" They said: "There is no one among us who is suspected, and there is none among us but a trustworthy, entrusted person." He said: "Then why do you have no rulers?" They said: "We do not oppress one another." He said: "Then why do you have no judges among you?" They said: "We do not dispute." He said: "Then why do you have no rich people among you?" They said: "We do not compete in accumulation." He said: "Then why do you have no kings among you?" They said: "We do not act arrogantly." He said: "Then why do you not quarrel or disagree?" They said: "Because of the harmony of our hearts and the righteousness of our relations with one another." He said: "Then why do you not curse one another or fight?" They said: "Because we have overcome our natures with resolve, and governed ourselves with forbearance." He said: "Then why is your word one, and your way upright and balanced?" They said: "Because we do not lie, do not deceive, and do not backbite one another." He said: "Then tell me, from where did your hearts become alike, and your conduct become balanced?" They said: "Our breasts are sound, so that rancor and envy have been removed from our hearts." He said: "Then why is there no needy or poor person among you?" They said: "Because we share equally." He said: "Then why is there no harsh or coarse person among you?" They said: "Because of humility and lowliness." He said: "What has made you the longest-lived of people?" They said: "Because we pursue the truth and judge with justice." He said: "Then why are you not struck by drought?" They said: "We do not neglect seeking forgiveness." He said: "Then why are you not irritable?" They said: "Because we have accustomed ourselves to trials since we were, and we loved them and were eager for them, so we were spared from them." He said: "Then why are you not struck by calamities as people are?" They said: "We do not rely on anyone other than God, and we do not act by the stars or the signs of the weather." He said: "Tell me, did you find your fathers acting thus?" They said: "Yes, we found our fathers showing mercy to their needy, comforting their poor, pardoning those who wronged them, doing good to those who harmed them, forbearing toward those who acted ignorantly toward them, asking forgiveness for those who reviled them, keeping their ties of kinship, returning their trusts, guarding their times of prayer, fulfilling their covenants, keeping their promises, not turning away from their equals, and not disdaining their relatives. So God set their affairs right by that, and preserved them while they lived, and it was a right upon God to preserve them in their inheritance."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet of God (ﷺ), who said: "Yajuj and Majuj dig through the barrier every day, until, when they are nearly about to see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Return, and you will dig through it tomorrow.' Then God restores it to its condition on the day they left it. Then, when the time comes, he says: 'If God wills,' and they dig through it and come out upon the people, drinking up the waters, and the people take refuge in their fortresses. They shoot their arrows at the sky, and they return to them stained like blood. They say: 'We have overcome the people of the earth and prevailed over the people of heaven.' Then God sends upon them a worm in their necks, and it kills them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the beasts of the earth will grow fat and be sated with their flesh.'"

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari then al-Zafari, from Mahmud ibn Labid, brother of Bani Abd al-Ashhal, and from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Yajuj and Majuj will be let loose, and they will come out upon the people, as God the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And they will swarm from every hillock﴾. They will overrun the earth, and the Muslims will withdraw from them to their cities and fortresses, and gather their livestock to themselves. They will drink the waters of the earth, until some of them pass by a river and drink what is in it, until they leave it dry. Then one who comes after them passes by that river and says: 'There was water here once.' Until no one among the people remains except one who has retreated to a fortress or a city. One of them says: 'These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them. Only the people of heaven remain.' Then one of them shakes his spear and throws it toward the sky, and it returns to him stained with blood, as a trial and a tribulation. While they are in that state, God sends upon them a worm in their necks, like the nagaf, and it comes out in their necks, and they become dead in the morning, with no sound from them. The Muslims say: 'Is there a man who will sell himself for us, to look into what the enemy has done?' Then a man from among them strips himself for this, seeking reward for himself, having prepared himself to be killed. He descends and finds them dead, some upon others. He calls out: 'O assembly of Muslims, rejoice, for God has sufficed you against your enemy.' They come out from their cities and fortresses, and release their livestock, and the livestock have no pasture but their flesh, and it is sated by it more than it has ever been sated by any plant it has ever found."

⁕ Bahr ibn Nasr narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Abu al-Zahiriyah and Shurayh ibn Ubayd, that Yajuj and Majuj are three kinds: one kind whose height is like the height of the cedar; another kind whose height and breadth are equal; and another kind, one of whom spreads his ear as a mattress and covers himself with the other, so that it covers his entire body.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿They said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, indeed Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the earth﴾. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri used to say: The Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "No man among them dies until there is born to his loins a thousand men." He said: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud used to marvel at their multitude and say: No one of Yajuj and Majuj dies until there is born to him a thousand men from his loins.

So the report we have mentioned from Wahb ibn Munabbih concerning the story of Yajuj and Majuj indicates that those who said to Dhu al-Qarnayn ﴿Indeed Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the earth﴾ were only informing him of their fear of what would occur from them of corruption in the earth, not that they were complaining of corruption that had already come from them among themselves or among others. The reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) state that corruption will come from them in the earth, and there is no indication in them that corruption had come from them before Dhu al-Qarnayn built the barrier that he built between them and the people beyond them.

Since this is so, as we have explained, the correct interpretation of His words ﴿Indeed Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the earth﴾ is: indeed Yajuj and Majuj will corrupt in the earth.

* *

As for His words ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment (kharj)?﴾

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it as ﴿kharj﴾, as if they took it in the manner of the verbal noun from kharj for the head (i.e., a tax levied per head), meaning its imposition. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as ﴿kharaj﴾ with an alif, as if they took it in the manner of a noun, meaning by it a wage for your building a barrier for us between us and these people.

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who recited it as ﴿kharaj﴾ with an alif, because the people, as is reported of them, only offered Dhu al-Qarnayn that they would give him some of their wealth with which he could aid in building the barrier, and this he made clear in his words ﴿So help me with strength, and I will place between you and them a barrier﴾. They did not offer him a poll-tax on their heads. In the Arabs' usage, kharaj means produce/yield.

And the interpreters have said what we have said.

Those who said this: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment?﴾ He said: a wage.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment?﴾ He said: a wage.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment?﴾ He said: a wage.

* *

As for His words: ﴿On condition that you make between us and them a barrier﴾

He means: They said to him: Shall we assign for you a payment on condition that you make between us and Yajuj and Majuj an obstacle that will hold them back from us and prevent them from coming out to us? That is the barrier.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then he followed a course﴾. He means: then he traveled through routes and stages, and took paths, ﴿until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾.

The readers (qurra') differed over the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the Kufans recited ﴿between the two barriers (al-suddayn)﴾ with a ḍamma on the sīn, and so with every instance of it in the Qur'an. Some of the Meccan readers recited it with a fatḥa throughout. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' (a reader and grammarian) used a fatḥa on the sīn in this surah and a ḍamma on the sīn in Yā Sīn, and said: al-saddu with a fatḥa is what stands as a barrier between you and a thing, while al-suddu with a ḍamma is what is a film over the eye. As for the Kufans, most of them recited the sīn with a fatḥa throughout the Qur'an, except for the words al-suddayn in this verse, where they specifically used a ḍamma.

It has been transmitted from 'Ikrima concerning this:

- Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: al-Qasim related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrima, who said: Whatever is the work of the children of Adam is al-sadd, meaning with a fatḥa, and whatever is the work of God is al-sudd.

al-Kisa'i (a reader) used to say: they are two dialects with one meaning.

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that they are two widely transmitted readings among the readings of the regional centers (amṣār), and two dialects agreeing in meaning without difference. So whichever of the two the reader recites is correct. There is no sense in the distinction reported from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' and 'Ikrima between al-suddu and al-saddu, because we have found no evidence to show a difference between them as reported from those two. What confirms this is that all the people of interpretation from whom we have received explanations did not transmit from any of them a distinction between the fatḥa and the ḍamma. Had the two differed in meaning, the distinction would have been transmitted along with the interpretation, God willing. Rather, the meaning of both was not divided in their view, so they explained the letter without distinguishing between them. As for what was mentioned from 'Ikrima on this, the one who transmitted it from Ayyub and Harun is open to question, and we do not know of it from Ayyub through the reliable transmitters of his circle. Both al-sadd and al-sudd mean a barrier between two things. Here, according to what has been mentioned, they are two mountains that closed off what lay between them, and Dhu al-Qarnayn filled in with a barrier between Yajuj and Majuj and those behind them, to cut off their hostility and mischief from people.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said:

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿between the two barriers (al-suddayn)﴾, he said: The two mountains, the rampart between Yajuj and Majuj, two peoples from beyond the rampart of Dhu al-Qarnayn. He said: The two mountains are Armenia and Adharbayjan.
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿between the two barriers﴾, and they are two mountains.
- I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿between the two barriers﴾, meaning between two mountains.
- al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿between the two barriers﴾, he said: They are two mountains.

* * *

And His words ﴿he found beside them a people who could hardly understand speech﴾.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: he found beside the two barriers a people who could hardly understand the speech of anyone other than their own speech.

The readers differed over the recitation of His words ﴿could understand (yafqahūn)﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited ﴿yafaqahūna qawlan﴾ with a fatḥa on the qāf and the yā', from faqiha, yafqahu, fiqhan (to understand). The majority of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿yufqihūna qawlan﴾ with a ḍamma on the yā' and a kasra on the qāf, from afqahtu fulānan kadhā uf-qihuhu ifqāhan (I made someone understand that), meaning: when I made him understand it.

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that they are two widely transmitted readings among the readings of the regional centers, neither of which negates the other. This is because the people about whom God reported this report may be people who could hardly understand speech from others about them, so the recitation with that is correct. And it is possible that they, while being so, could hardly make others understand them, for reasons either in their tongues or in their speech, so the recitation with that is also correct.

* * *

And His words ﴿Indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land﴾.

The readers differed over the recitation of His words ﴿Indeed Gog and Magog (inna Ya'jūja wa Ma'jūja)﴾. The readers of the Hijaz, Iraq and elsewhere recited ﴿inna Yājūja wa Mājūja﴾ without a hamza, in the pattern fā'ūl from yajjtu and majjtu, and they took the two alifs in them to be extra letters. The exception was 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud and al-A'raj, for it has been reported that they recited it with a hamza in both, and they took the hamza in both to be original to the word. It seems they took Ya'jūj to be yaf'ūl from ajjtu, and Ma'jūj to be maf'ūl.

The recitation that is the correct one according to us is Yājūj and Mājūj with an alif and without a hamza, because the authoritative readers are in consensus on it, and because it is the known speech on the tongues of the Arabs. From it is the verse of Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj:

"Even if Yājūj and Mājūj together,
and 'Ād returned and they gathered an army against Tubba'..."

[The verse is by Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj (his Dīwān, Leipzig edition 1903, p. 92). He said: "Yājūj and Mājūj are not diptotes. Some of them add a hamza to their two alifs, and some do not add it. Ru'ba said: 'If Yājūj and Mājūj together...' and did not make them diptotes (in the Arabic sense, without tanwīn). (In Lisān al-'Arab, under ajj.) Yājūj and Mājūj are two tribes of God's creation, and the recitation came with both hamza and without hamza. He said: A ḥadīth has come: 'Creation is ten parts, nine of them are Yājūj and Mājūj.' They are two foreign names, and the derivation of similar words is from Arabic speech: it comes from ajjat al-nār (the fire blazed), and from al-mā' al-ajāj (salt water), which is extremely salty, burning from its saltiness. He said: The estimate for Yājūj would be yafʿūl, and likewise Majūj. He said: This would be their derivation if the two names were Arabic, but a foreign word is not derived from Arabic. Whoever does not add a hamza and takes the two alifs to be extra says: Yājūj is from yajjtu, and Mājūj is from majjtu, and they are not diptotes. Ru'ba said: 'If Yājūj and Mājūj together... and 'Ād returned and they gathered an army against Tubba'.' End of quote.]

They are two peoples beyond the barrier.

* * *

And His words ﴿corrupters in the land﴾.

The people of interpretation differed over the meaning of the corruption with which God described these two peoples. Some of them said: They used to eat people.

Those who said that:

- Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ayyub al-Khuzani related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, saying: I heard Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz say concerning His words ﴿Indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land﴾, he said: They used to eat people.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is that Yajuj and Majuj would corrupt the land in the future, not that they were corrupting it at that time.

Those who said that, and the description of Dhu al-Qarnayn's following of the causes which God mentioned in this verse, and the account of the reason for his building the barrier: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Some of those who narrate the stories of the non-Arabs from the People of the Book, who had become Muslim, related to me, from what they had inherited of the knowledge of Dhu al-Qarnayn, that Dhu al-Qarnayn was a man from the people of Egypt named Marzaba ibn Mardaba al-Yunani, from the descendants of Yawnan ibn Yafith ibn Nuh.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan al-Kala'i, and Khalid was a man who had met people: "The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked about Dhu al-Qarnayn and he said: 'A king who swept the earth from beneath it with the causes (asbāb).'" Khalid said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab heard a man say: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn!" So he said: "O God, forgive us! Are you not content to be named after the prophets, until you name yourselves after the angels? If the Messenger of God said that, then the truth is what he said, and falsehood is what contradicts it."'

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Someone whom I do not suspect related to me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who had knowledge of the earlier narratives, that he used to say: Dhu al-Qarnayn was a man from the Romans, the son of an old woman from among their old women, who had no child other than him. His name was Iskandar (Alexander). He was only called Dhu al-Qarnayn because the two sides of his head were of copper. When he reached maturity, and he was a righteous servant, God, mighty and majestic, said to him: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, I am sending you to the peoples of the earth, and they are peoples of differing tongues, and they are all the people of the earth. Among them are two peoples between whom is the length of the whole earth. Among them are two peoples between whom is the breadth of the whole earth. And a community in the middle of the earth, among them are the jinn, the humans, and Yajuj and Majuj. As for the two peoples between whom is the length of the earth: one people is at the west of the sun, called Nāsik. The other is at its rising, called Manasik. As for the two between whom is the breadth of the earth: one people is in the right side of the earth, called Hawil. The other, which is on the left side of the earth, is a people called Tawil."

When God said that to him, Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "My God, You have appointed me to a great matter, whose measure none but You can grasp. So inform me about these peoples to which You have sent me: with what strength shall I contend with them, with what gathering shall I outnumber them, with what stratagem shall I outwit them, with what patience shall I endure them, with what tongue shall I speak with them, and how can I understand their languages, and with what hearing shall I grasp their speech, and with what sight shall I penetrate them, with what proof shall I dispute with them, with what heart shall I understand them, with what wisdom shall I manage their affairs, with what justice shall I be fair among them, with what forbearance shall I bear with them, with what knowledge shall I distinguish between them, with what skill shall I master their affairs, with what hand shall I overpower them, with what foot shall I trample them, with what power shall I subdue them, with what army shall I fight them, with what gentleness shall I win them over? For I have nothing, O my God, of what I have mentioned that can stand against them, nor that can prevail over them or withstand them. You are the Lord, the Merciful, who does not burden any soul beyond its capacity, nor load it beyond its power, nor distress it nor overwhelm it, but You are gentle with it [[It is said: raʾafa bihi yarʾafu, if he had mercy on him. It is of the pattern faḥa, karuma and faraḥa, and it takes bi, as in Lisān al-'Arab. Perhaps here it implies the meaning of ramiḥa, so it took its object directly, or it is a distortion of tarʾamuhā.]] and merciful to it."

God, mighty and majestic, said: "I shall equip you with what I have burdened you with. I shall expand your breast, so it will embrace everything. I shall expand your understanding, so you will comprehend everything. I shall loosen your tongue, so you will speak everything. I shall open your hearing, so you will grasp everything. I shall extend your sight, so you will penetrate everything. I shall manage your affairs, so you will master everything. I shall count for you, so nothing will escape you. I shall guard over you, so nothing will be hidden from you. I shall strengthen your back, so nothing will break you. I shall strengthen your support, so nothing will overcome you. I shall strengthen your heart, so nothing will frighten you. I shall subject to you light and darkness, and make them soldiers of your army: light will guide you in front of you, and darkness will shelter you from behind you. I shall strengthen your intellect, so nothing will terrify you. I shall extend for you from before your hands, so you will overpower everything. I shall strengthen your tread for you, so you will crush everything. I shall clothe you in awe, so nothing will dare to approach you."

When he was told that, he set out aiming for the people at the west of the sun. When he reached them, he found a multitude and a number that none but God could count, and a strength and might that none but God could withstand, and differing tongues, scattered desires, and divided hearts. When he saw that, he outnumbered them with darkness. He struck around them three of the armies of darkness, which surrounded them from every direction and encircled them until they were gathered in one place. Then he took them with light, and invited them to God and to worship Him. Some of them believed in him, and some turned away. He then targeted those who had turned their backs on him, and brought darkness upon them. It entered their mouths, their noses, their ears and their bellies, and entered their houses and their homes, and covered them from above, from below and from every side. They surged within it and became bewildered. When they feared they would perish in it, they cried out to him with one voice. He lifted it from them and took them forcibly, so they entered his call. He then gathered from the people of the west great nations, and made them one army. Then he set out, leading them, while darkness drove them from behind and guarded them on every side, and light was in front of them, leading and guiding them. He was travelling along the right side of the earth, intending the people on the right side of the earth called Hawil. God subjected to him his hand, his heart, his opinion, his intellect, his sight and his plotting, so he never erred when he planned, and when he undertook a task he perfected it. He set out leading those peoples, and they followed him. When he came to a sea or a ford, he built boats of small planks like sandals, arranged them within an hour, then placed in them all who were with him of those peoples and those armies. When they crossed the rivers and seas, he dismantled them, and then gave each person a plank, so its weight did not distress him. He continued in this manner until he came to Hawil, and he acted there as he had acted with Nasik. When he finished with it, he continued on his way along the right side of the earth until he reached Manasik at the rising of the sun. He acted there, and formed armies from it as he had done with the two peoples before it. Then he turned back heading along the left side of the earth, intending Tawil, the people opposite Hawil; the two are facing each other, with the breadth of the whole earth between them. When he reached it he acted there, and formed an army from it as he had done before. When he finished with it, he turned from it to the peoples in the middle of the earth, from the jinn and all humanity, and Yajuj and Majuj. When he was in part of the route on the side of the end of the Turks towards the east, a righteous human nation said to him: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, between these two mountains there are creatures of God's creation, and many of them resemble humans [[In ʿArāʾis al-Majālis of al-Tha'labi the exegete (Halabi edition, p. 365) it reads: 'there is no resemblance to humans among them,' and that is more fitting to the context.]], and they are like beasts. They eat grass, and they prey on animals and wild beasts as beasts of prey do, and they eat all the crawling things of the earth, such as snakes and scorpions, and every living creature God has created on earth. No creature of God grows as they grow in one year, nor increases as they increase, nor multiplies as they multiply. If they have a term, according to what we see of their growth and increase, there is no doubt that they will fill the earth, expel its inhabitants from it, prevail over it and corrupt it. No year has passed for us since we have been neighbours to them without our anticipating them and expecting that their first ones will appear to us from between these two mountains." [God says:] ﴿So shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you make a barrier between us and them?﴾ He said: ﴿What my Lord has established me in is better, so help me with strength; I will make between you and them a barrier﴾. Bring me the rocks, the iron and the copper, until I survey their lands, learn their state, and measure the distance between their two mountains.

Then he set off, leading them, until he reached them and passed into the midst of their land. He found them all of one measure, males and females alike. The height of each of them was like half of a man of medium stature among us. They had claws in the place of our fingernails, and molars and fangs like the molars and fangs of beasts of prey, and jaws like the jaws of camels, with a strength such that a sound of movement could be heard when they ate, like the chewing of a camel's cud, or like the gnawing of an old stallion or a strong mare. They were hairy: on their bodies was hair sufficient to cover them and to protect them from heat and cold when these befell them. Each one of them had two large ears: one of them was woolly, its back and belly covered with wool, and the other was downy, its back and belly covered with down. They could wrap themselves in them when they wore them: one of them served as a blanket and the other as a mattress, one they used in summer and the other in winter. Among them, no male or female failed to know the appointed time at which they would die and the end of their lifespan. That is because no male among them dies until a thousand children have come forth from his loins, and no female dies until a thousand children have come forth from her womb. When that happens, they become certain of death. They are provided with the tannin (sea-monster/serpent) during the days of spring, and they pray for rain when they seek it, just as we pray for rain at its appointed time; they cast forth from it one each year, and they eat it throughout the year until the following year. It suffices them, despite their numbers and their growth. When they receive rain, become fertile, live, and grow fat, and its effect is seen upon them, the females yield milk and the males become lustful. When it fails them, they become emaciated and suffer drought, the males become weak and the females become barren, and the effect of that becomes evident upon them. They call to one another like doves, howl like dogs, and mate wherever they meet, like beasts.

When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw this from them, he turned back to the area between the two barriers (al-Saddayn). He measured the distance between them, while he was at the farthest edge of the land of the Turks toward the rising of the sun, and found the distance between them to be one hundred farsakh. When he began his work, he dug a foundation for it until he reached water. Then he made its width fifty farsakh, made its filling of rocks, and its mortar of copper, which was melted and then poured over it, so that it became like a vein of a mountain beneath the earth. Then he raised it and crowned it with blocks of iron and molten copper, and placed between them a vein of yellow copper, so that it became like a striped cloth woven with the yellow and red of copper and the black of iron. When he finished it and made it firm, he set off intending for the community of humankind and jinn. As he was traveling, he came upon a righteous community who guide by the truth and act justly by it. He found a equitable, moderate people who divide equally, judge with justice, support one another and show mercy to one another. Their condition was uniform, their word was one, their characters were alike, their way was upright, their hearts were harmonious, their conduct was good, and their graves were by the doors of their houses. Their houses had no doors, they had no rulers, no judges among them, no rich people, no kings, no nobles. They did not differ, did not vie for superiority, did not disagree, did not quarrel, did not curse one another, did not fight, were not struck by drought, did not become irritable, and were not afflicted by the calamities that afflict people. They were the longest-lived of people, and among them there was no needy person, no poor person, no harsh person, and no coarse person. When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw this of their affair, he marveled at it and said: "Tell me, O people, your story, for I have surveyed the whole earth, its land and sea, its east and west, its light and darkness, and I have not found anyone like you. So tell me your story." They said: "Yes, ask us what you wish." He said: "Tell me, why are the graves of your dead by the doors of your houses?" They said: "We did that deliberately, so that we do not forget death and its remembrance does not leave our hearts." He said: "Then why do your houses have no doors?" They said: "There is no one among us who is suspected, and there is none among us but a trustworthy, entrusted person." He said: "Then why do you have no rulers?" They said: "We do not oppress one another." He said: "Then why do you have no judges among you?" They said: "We do not dispute." He said: "Then why do you have no rich people among you?" They said: "We do not compete in accumulation." He said: "Then why do you have no kings among you?" They said: "We do not act arrogantly." He said: "Then why do you not quarrel or disagree?" They said: "Because of the harmony of our hearts and the righteousness of our relations with one another." He said: "Then why do you not curse one another or fight?" They said: "Because we have overcome our natures with resolve, and governed ourselves with forbearance." He said: "Then why is your word one, and your way upright and balanced?" They said: "Because we do not lie, do not deceive, and do not backbite one another." He said: "Then tell me, from where did your hearts become alike, and your conduct become balanced?" They said: "Our breasts are sound, so that rancor and envy have been removed from our hearts." He said: "Then why is there no needy or poor person among you?" They said: "Because we share equally." He said: "Then why is there no harsh or coarse person among you?" They said: "Because of humility and lowliness." He said: "What has made you the longest-lived of people?" They said: "Because we pursue the truth and judge with justice." He said: "Then why are you not struck by drought?" They said: "We do not neglect seeking forgiveness." He said: "Then why are you not irritable?" They said: "Because we have accustomed ourselves to trials since we were, and we loved them and were eager for them, so we were spared from them." He said: "Then why are you not struck by calamities as people are?" They said: "We do not rely on anyone other than God, and we do not act by the stars or the signs of the weather." He said: "Tell me, did you find your fathers acting thus?" They said: "Yes, we found our fathers showing mercy to their needy, comforting their poor, pardoning those who wronged them, doing good to those who harmed them, forbearing toward those who acted ignorantly toward them, asking forgiveness for those who reviled them, keeping their ties of kinship, returning their trusts, guarding their times of prayer, fulfilling their covenants, keeping their promises, not turning away from their equals, and not disdaining their relatives. So God set their affairs right by that, and preserved them while they lived, and it was a right upon God to preserve them in their inheritance."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet of God (ﷺ), who said: "Yajuj and Majuj dig through the barrier every day, until, when they are nearly about to see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Return, and you will dig through it tomorrow.' Then God restores it to its condition on the day they left it. Then, when the time comes, he says: 'If God wills,' and they dig through it and come out upon the people, drinking up the waters, and the people take refuge in their fortresses. They shoot their arrows at the sky, and they return to them stained like blood. They say: 'We have overcome the people of the earth and prevailed over the people of heaven.' Then God sends upon them a worm in their necks, and it kills them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the beasts of the earth will grow fat and be sated with their flesh.'"

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari then al-Zafari, from Mahmud ibn Labid, brother of Bani Abd al-Ashhal, and from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Yajuj and Majuj will be let loose, and they will come out upon the people, as God the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And they will swarm from every hillock﴾. They will overrun the earth, and the Muslims will withdraw from them to their cities and fortresses, and gather their livestock to themselves. They will drink the waters of the earth, until some of them pass by a river and drink what is in it, until they leave it dry. Then one who comes after them passes by that river and says: 'There was water here once.' Until no one among the people remains except one who has retreated to a fortress or a city. One of them says: 'These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them. Only the people of heaven remain.' Then one of them shakes his spear and throws it toward the sky, and it returns to him stained with blood, as a trial and a tribulation. While they are in that state, God sends upon them a worm in their necks, like the nagaf, and it comes out in their necks, and they become dead in the morning, with no sound from them. The Muslims say: 'Is there a man who will sell himself for us, to look into what the enemy has done?' Then a man from among them strips himself for this, seeking reward for himself, having prepared himself to be killed. He descends and finds them dead, some upon others. He calls out: 'O assembly of Muslims, rejoice, for God has sufficed you against your enemy.' They come out from their cities and fortresses, and release their livestock, and the livestock have no pasture but their flesh, and it is sated by it more than it has ever been sated by any plant it has ever found."

⁕ Bahr ibn Nasr narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Abu al-Zahiriyah and Shurayh ibn Ubayd, that Yajuj and Majuj are three kinds: one kind whose height is like the height of the cedar; another kind whose height and breadth are equal; and another kind, one of whom spreads his ear as a mattress and covers himself with the other, so that it covers his entire body.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿They said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, indeed Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the earth﴾. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri used to say: The Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "No man among them dies until there is born to his loins a thousand men." He said: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud used to marvel at their multitude and say: No one of Yajuj and Majuj dies until there is born to him a thousand men from his loins.

So the report we have mentioned from Wahb ibn Munabbih concerning the story of Yajuj and Majuj indicates that those who said to Dhu al-Qarnayn ﴿Indeed Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the earth﴾ were only informing him of their fear of what would occur from them of corruption in the earth, not that they were complaining of corruption that had already come from them among themselves or among others. The reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) state that corruption will come from them in the earth, and there is no indication in them that corruption had come from them before Dhu al-Qarnayn built the barrier that he built between them and the people beyond them.

Since this is so, as we have explained, the correct interpretation of His words ﴿Indeed Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the earth﴾ is: indeed Yajuj and Majuj will corrupt in the earth.

* *

As for His words ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment (kharj)?﴾

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it as ﴿kharj﴾, as if they took it in the manner of the verbal noun from kharj for the head (i.e., a tax levied per head), meaning its imposition. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as ﴿kharaj﴾ with an alif, as if they took it in the manner of a noun, meaning by it a wage for your building a barrier for us between us and these people.

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who recited it as ﴿kharaj﴾ with an alif, because the people, as is reported of them, only offered Dhu al-Qarnayn that they would give him some of their wealth with which he could aid in building the barrier, and this he made clear in his words ﴿So help me with strength, and I will place between you and them a barrier﴾. They did not offer him a poll-tax on their heads. In the Arabs' usage, kharaj means produce/yield.

And the interpreters have said what we have said.

Those who said this: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment?﴾ He said: a wage.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment?﴾ He said: a wage.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment?﴾ He said: a wage.

* *

As for His words: ﴿On condition that you make between us and them a barrier﴾

He means: They said to him: Shall we assign for you a payment on condition that you make between us and Yajuj and Majuj an obstacle that will hold them back from us and prevent them from coming out to us? That is the barrier.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then he followed a course﴾. He means: then he traveled through routes and stages, and took paths, ﴿until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾.

The readers (qurra') differed over the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the Kufans recited ﴿between the two barriers (al-suddayn)﴾ with a ḍamma on the sīn, and so with every instance of it in the Qur'an. Some of the Meccan readers recited it with a fatḥa throughout. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' (a reader and grammarian) used a fatḥa on the sīn in this surah and a ḍamma on the sīn in Yā Sīn, and said: al-saddu with a fatḥa is what stands as a barrier between you and a thing, while al-suddu with a ḍamma is what is a film over the eye. As for the Kufans, most of them recited the sīn with a fatḥa throughout the Qur'an, except for the words al-suddayn in this verse, where they specifically used a ḍamma.

It has been transmitted from 'Ikrima concerning this:

- Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: al-Qasim related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrima, who said: Whatever is the work of the children of Adam is al-sadd, meaning with a fatḥa, and whatever is the work of God is al-sudd.

al-Kisa'i (a reader) used to say: they are two dialects with one meaning.

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that they are two widely transmitted readings among the readings of the regional centers (amṣār), and two dialects agreeing in meaning without difference. So whichever of the two the reader recites is correct. There is no sense in the distinction reported from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' and 'Ikrima between al-suddu and al-saddu, because we have found no evidence to show a difference between them as reported from those two. What confirms this is that all the people of interpretation from whom we have received explanations did not transmit from any of them a distinction between the fatḥa and the ḍamma. Had the two differed in meaning, the distinction would have been transmitted along with the interpretation, God willing. Rather, the meaning of both was not divided in their view, so they explained the letter without distinguishing between them. As for what was mentioned from 'Ikrima on this, the one who transmitted it from Ayyub and Harun is open to question, and we do not know of it from Ayyub through the reliable transmitters of his circle. Both al-sadd and al-sudd mean a barrier between two things. Here, according to what has been mentioned, they are two mountains that closed off what lay between them, and Dhu al-Qarnayn filled in with a barrier between Yajuj and Majuj and those behind them, to cut off their hostility and mischief from people.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said:

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿between the two barriers (al-suddayn)﴾, he said: The two mountains, the rampart between Yajuj and Majuj, two peoples from beyond the rampart of Dhu al-Qarnayn. He said: The two mountains are Armenia and Adharbayjan.
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿between the two barriers﴾, and they are two mountains.
- I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿between the two barriers﴾, meaning between two mountains.
- al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿between the two barriers﴾, he said: They are two mountains.

* * *

And His words ﴿he found beside them a people who could hardly understand speech﴾.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: he found beside the two barriers a people who could hardly understand the speech of anyone other than their own speech.

The readers differed over the recitation of His words ﴿could understand (yafqahūn)﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited ﴿yafaqahūna qawlan﴾ with a fatḥa on the qāf and the yā', from faqiha, yafqahu, fiqhan (to understand). The majority of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿yufqihūna qawlan﴾ with a ḍamma on the yā' and a kasra on the qāf, from afqahtu fulānan kadhā uf-qihuhu ifqāhan (I made someone understand that), meaning: when I made him understand it.

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that they are two widely transmitted readings among the readings of the regional centers, neither of which negates the other. This is because the people about whom God reported this report may be people who could hardly understand speech from others about them, so the recitation with that is correct. And it is possible that they, while being so, could hardly make others understand them, for reasons either in their tongues or in their speech, so the recitation with that is also correct.

* * *

And His words ﴿Indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land﴾.

The readers differed over the recitation of His words ﴿Indeed Gog and Magog (inna Ya'jūja wa Ma'jūja)﴾. The readers of the Hijaz, Iraq and elsewhere recited ﴿inna Yājūja wa Mājūja﴾ without a hamza, in the pattern fā'ūl from yajjtu and majjtu, and they took the two alifs in them to be extra letters. The exception was 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud and al-A'raj, for it has been reported that they recited it with a hamza in both, and they took the hamza in both to be original to the word. It seems they took Ya'jūj to be yaf'ūl from ajjtu, and Ma'jūj to be maf'ūl.

The recitation that is the correct one according to us is Yājūj and Mājūj with an alif and without a hamza, because the authoritative readers are in consensus on it, and because it is the known speech on the tongues of the Arabs. From it is the verse of Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj:

"Even if Yājūj and Mājūj together,
and 'Ād returned and they gathered an army against Tubba'..."

[The verse is by Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj (his Dīwān, Leipzig edition 1903, p. 92). He said: "Yājūj and Mājūj are not diptotes. Some of them add a hamza to their two alifs, and some do not add it. Ru'ba said: 'If Yājūj and Mājūj together...' and did not make them diptotes (in the Arabic sense, without tanwīn). (In Lisān al-'Arab, under ajj.) Yājūj and Mājūj are two tribes of God's creation, and the recitation came with both hamza and without hamza. He said: A ḥadīth has come: 'Creation is ten parts, nine of them are Yājūj and Mājūj.' They are two foreign names, and the derivation of similar words is from Arabic speech: it comes from ajjat al-nār (the fire blazed), and from al-mā' al-ajāj (salt water), which is extremely salty, burning from its saltiness. He said: The estimate for Yājūj would be yafʿūl, and likewise Majūj. He said: This would be their derivation if the two names were Arabic, but a foreign word is not derived from Arabic. Whoever does not add a hamza and takes the two alifs to be extra says: Yājūj is from yajjtu, and Mājūj is from majjtu, and they are not diptotes. Ru'ba said: 'If Yājūj and Mājūj together... and 'Ād returned and they gathered an army against Tubba'.' End of quote.]

They are two peoples beyond the barrier.

* * *

And His words ﴿corrupters in the land﴾.

The people of interpretation differed over the meaning of the corruption with which God described these two peoples. Some of them said: They used to eat people.

Those who said that:

- Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ayyub al-Khuzani related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, saying: I heard Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz say concerning His words ﴿Indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land﴾, he said: They used to eat people.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is that Yajuj and Majuj would corrupt the land in the future, not that they were corrupting it at that time.

Those who said that, and the description of Dhu al-Qarnayn's following of the causes which God mentioned in this verse, and the account of the reason for his building the barrier: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Some of those who narrate the stories of the non-Arabs from the People of the Book, who had become Muslim, related to me, from what they had inherited of the knowledge of Dhu al-Qarnayn, that Dhu al-Qarnayn was a man from the people of Egypt named Marzaba ibn Mardaba al-Yunani, from the descendants of Yawnan ibn Yafith ibn Nuh.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan al-Kala'i, and Khalid was a man who had met people: "The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked about Dhu al-Qarnayn and he said: 'A king who swept the earth from beneath it with the causes (asbāb).'" Khalid said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab heard a man say: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn!" So he said: "O God, forgive us! Are you not content to be named after the prophets, until you name yourselves after the angels? If the Messenger of God said that, then the truth is what he said, and falsehood is what contradicts it."'

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Someone whom I do not suspect related to me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who had knowledge of the earlier narratives, that he used to say: Dhu al-Qarnayn was a man from the Romans, the son of an old woman from among their old women, who had no child other than him. His name was Iskandar (Alexander). He was only called Dhu al-Qarnayn because the two sides of his head were of copper. When he reached maturity, and he was a righteous servant, God, mighty and majestic, said to him: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, I am sending you to the peoples of the earth, and they are peoples of differing tongues, and they are all the people of the earth. Among them are two peoples between whom is the length of the whole earth. Among them are two peoples between whom is the breadth of the whole earth. And a community in the middle of the earth, among them are the jinn, the humans, and Yajuj and Majuj. As for the two peoples between whom is the length of the earth: one people is at the west of the sun, called Nāsik. The other is at its rising, called Manasik. As for the two between whom is the breadth of the earth: one people is in the right side of the earth, called Hawil. The other, which is on the left side of the earth, is a people called Tawil."

When God said that to him, Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "My God, You have appointed me to a great matter, whose measure none but You can grasp. So inform me about these peoples to which You have sent me: with what strength shall I contend with them, with what gathering shall I outnumber them, with what stratagem shall I outwit them, with what patience shall I endure them, with what tongue shall I speak with them, and how can I understand their languages, and with what hearing shall I grasp their speech, and with what sight shall I penetrate them, with what proof shall I dispute with them, with what heart shall I understand them, with what wisdom shall I manage their affairs, with what justice shall I be fair among them, with what forbearance shall I bear with them, with what knowledge shall I distinguish between them, with what skill shall I master their affairs, with what hand shall I overpower them, with what foot shall I trample them, with what power shall I subdue them, with what army shall I fight them, with what gentleness shall I win them over? For I have nothing, O my God, of what I have mentioned that can stand against them, nor that can prevail over them or withstand them. You are the Lord, the Merciful, who does not burden any soul beyond its capacity, nor load it beyond its power, nor distress it nor overwhelm it, but You are gentle with it [[It is said: raʾafa bihi yarʾafu, if he had mercy on him. It is of the pattern faḥa, karuma and faraḥa, and it takes bi, as in Lisān al-'Arab. Perhaps here it implies the meaning of ramiḥa, so it took its object directly, or it is a distortion of tarʾamuhā.]] and merciful to it."

God, mighty and majestic, said: "I shall equip you with what I have burdened you with. I shall expand your breast, so it will embrace everything. I shall expand your understanding, so you will comprehend everything. I shall loosen your tongue, so you will speak everything. I shall open your hearing, so you will grasp everything. I shall extend your sight, so you will penetrate everything. I shall manage your affairs, so you will master everything. I shall count for you, so nothing will escape you. I shall guard over you, so nothing will be hidden from you. I shall strengthen your back, so nothing will break you. I shall strengthen your support, so nothing will overcome you. I shall strengthen your heart, so nothing will frighten you. I shall subject to you light and darkness, and make them soldiers of your army: light will guide you in front of you, and darkness will shelter you from behind you. I shall strengthen your intellect, so nothing will terrify you. I shall extend for you from before your hands, so you will overpower everything. I shall strengthen your tread for you, so you will crush everything. I shall clothe you in awe, so nothing will dare to approach you."

When he was told that, he set out aiming for the people at the west of the sun. When he reached them, he found a multitude and a number that none but God could count, and a strength and might that none but God could withstand, and differing tongues, scattered desires, and divided hearts. When he saw that, he outnumbered them with darkness. He struck around them three of the armies of darkness, which surrounded them from every direction and encircled them until they were gathered in one place. Then he took them with light, and invited them to God and to worship Him. Some of them believed in him, and some turned away. He then targeted those who had turned their backs on him, and brought darkness upon them. It entered their mouths, their noses, their ears and their bellies, and entered their houses and their homes, and covered them from above, from below and from every side. They surged within it and became bewildered. When they feared they would perish in it, they cried out to him with one voice. He lifted it from them and took them forcibly, so they entered his call. He then gathered from the people of the west great nations, and made them one army. Then he set out, leading them, while darkness drove them from behind and guarded them on every side, and light was in front of them, leading and guiding them. He was travelling along the right side of the earth, intending the people on the right side of the earth called Hawil. God subjected to him his hand, his heart, his opinion, his intellect, his sight and his plotting, so he never erred when he planned, and when he undertook a task he perfected it. He set out leading those peoples, and they followed him. When he came to a sea or a ford, he built boats of small planks like sandals, arranged them within an hour, then placed in them all who were with him of those peoples and those armies. When they crossed the rivers and seas, he dismantled them, and then gave each person a plank, so its weight did not distress him. He continued in this manner until he came to Hawil, and he acted there as he had acted with Nasik. When he finished with it, he continued on his way along the right side of the earth until he reached Manasik at the rising of the sun. He acted there, and formed armies from it as he had done with the two peoples before it. Then he turned back heading along the left side of the earth, intending Tawil, the people opposite Hawil; the two are facing each other, with the breadth of the whole earth between them. When he reached it he acted there, and formed an army from it as he had done before. When he finished with it, he turned from it to the peoples in the middle of the earth, from the jinn and all humanity, and Yajuj and Majuj. When he was in part of the route on the side of the end of the Turks towards the east, a righteous human nation said to him: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, between these two mountains there are creatures of God's creation, and many of them resemble humans [[In ʿArāʾis al-Majālis of al-Tha'labi the exegete (Halabi edition, p. 365) it reads: 'there is no resemblance to humans among them,' and that is more fitting to the context.]], and they are like beasts. They eat grass, and they prey on animals and wild beasts as beasts of prey do, and they eat all the crawling things of the earth, such as snakes and scorpions, and every living creature God has created on earth. No creature of God grows as they grow in one year, nor increases as they increase, nor multiplies as they multiply. If they have a term, according to what we see of their growth and increase, there is no doubt that they will fill the earth, expel its inhabitants from it, prevail over it and corrupt it. No year has passed for us since we have been neighbours to them without our anticipating them and expecting that their first ones will appear to us from between these two mountains." [God says:] ﴿So shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you make a barrier between us and them?﴾ He said: ﴿What my Lord has established me in is better, so help me with strength; I will make between you and them a barrier﴾. Bring me the rocks, the iron and the copper, until I survey their lands, learn their state, and measure the distance between their two mountains.

Then he set off, leading them, until he reached them and passed into the midst of their land. He found them all of one measure, males and females alike. The height of each of them was like half of a man of medium stature among us. They had claws in the place of our fingernails, and molars and fangs like the molars and fangs of beasts of prey, and jaws like the jaws of camels, with a strength such that a sound of movement could be heard when they ate, like the chewing of a camel's cud, or like the gnawing of an old stallion or a strong mare. They were hairy: on their bodies was hair sufficient to cover them and to protect them from heat and cold when these befell them. Each one of them had two large ears: one of them was woolly, its back and belly covered with wool, and the other was downy, its back and belly covered with down. They could wrap themselves in them when they wore them: one of them served as a blanket and the other as a mattress, one they used in summer and the other in winter. Among them, no male or female failed to know the appointed time at which they would die and the end of their lifespan. That is because no male among them dies until a thousand children have come forth from his loins, and no female dies until a thousand children have come forth from her womb. When that happens, they become certain of death. They are provided with the tannin (sea-monster/serpent) during the days of spring, and they pray for rain when they seek it, just as we pray for rain at its appointed time; they cast forth from it one each year, and they eat it throughout the year until the following year. It suffices them, despite their numbers and their growth. When they receive rain, become fertile, live, and grow fat, and its effect is seen upon them, the females yield milk and the males become lustful. When it fails them, they become emaciated and suffer drought, the males become weak and the females become barren, and the effect of that becomes evident upon them. They call to one another like doves, howl like dogs, and mate wherever they meet, like beasts.

When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw this from them, he turned back to the area between the two barriers (al-Saddayn). He measured the distance between them, while he was at the farthest edge of the land of the Turks toward the rising of the sun, and found the distance between them to be one hundred farsakh. When he began his work, he dug a foundation for it until he reached water. Then he made its width fifty farsakh, made its filling of rocks, and its mortar of copper, which was melted and then poured over it, so that it became like a vein of a mountain beneath the earth. Then he raised it and crowned it with blocks of iron and molten copper, and placed between them a vein of yellow copper, so that it became like a striped cloth woven with the yellow and red of copper and the black of iron. When he finished it and made it firm, he set off intending for the community of humankind and jinn. As he was traveling, he came upon a righteous community who guide by the truth and act justly by it. He found a equitable, moderate people who divide equally, judge with justice, support one another and show mercy to one another. Their condition was uniform, their word was one, their characters were alike, their way was upright, their hearts were harmonious, their conduct was good, and their graves were by the doors of their houses. Their houses had no doors, they had no rulers, no judges among them, no rich people, no kings, no nobles. They did not differ, did not vie for superiority, did not disagree, did not quarrel, did not curse one another, did not fight, were not struck by drought, did not become irritable, and were not afflicted by the calamities that afflict people. They were the longest-lived of people, and among them there was no needy person, no poor person, no harsh person, and no coarse person. When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw this of their affair, he marveled at it and said: "Tell me, O people, your story, for I have surveyed the whole earth, its land and sea, its east and west, its light and darkness, and I have not found anyone like you. So tell me your story." They said: "Yes, ask us what you wish." He said: "Tell me, why are the graves of your dead by the doors of your houses?" They said: "We did that deliberately, so that we do not forget death and its remembrance does not leave our hearts." He said: "Then why do your houses have no doors?" They said: "There is no one among us who is suspected, and there is none among us but a trustworthy, entrusted person." He said: "Then why do you have no rulers?" They said: "We do not oppress one another." He said: "Then why do you have no judges among you?" They said: "We do not dispute." He said: "Then why do you have no rich people among you?" They said: "We do not compete in accumulation." He said: "Then why do you have no kings among you?" They said: "We do not act arrogantly." He said: "Then why do you not quarrel or disagree?" They said: "Because of the harmony of our hearts and the righteousness of our relations with one another." He said: "Then why do you not curse one another or fight?" They said: "Because we have overcome our natures with resolve, and governed ourselves with forbearance." He said: "Then why is your word one, and your way upright and balanced?" They said: "Because we do not lie, do not deceive, and do not backbite one another." He said: "Then tell me, from where did your hearts become alike, and your conduct become balanced?" They said: "Our breasts are sound, so that rancor and envy have been removed from our hearts." He said: "Then why is there no needy or poor person among you?" They said: "Because we share equally." He said: "Then why is there no harsh or coarse person among you?" They said: "Because of humility and lowliness." He said: "What has made you the longest-lived of people?" They said: "Because we pursue the truth and judge with justice." He said: "Then why are you not struck by drought?" They said: "We do not neglect seeking forgiveness." He said: "Then why are you not irritable?" They said: "Because we have accustomed ourselves to trials since we were, and we loved them and were eager for them, so we were spared from them." He said: "Then why are you not struck by calamities as people are?" They said: "We do not rely on anyone other than God, and we do not act by the stars or the signs of the weather." He said: "Tell me, did you find your fathers acting thus?" They said: "Yes, we found our fathers showing mercy to their needy, comforting their poor, pardoning those who wronged them, doing good to those who harmed them, forbearing toward those who acted ignorantly toward them, asking forgiveness for those who reviled them, keeping their ties of kinship, returning their trusts, guarding their times of prayer, fulfilling their covenants, keeping their promises, not turning away from their equals, and not disdaining their relatives. So God set their affairs right by that, and preserved them while they lived, and it was a right upon God to preserve them in their inheritance."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet of God (ﷺ), who said: "Yajuj and Majuj dig through the barrier every day, until, when they are nearly about to see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Return, and you will dig through it tomorrow.' Then God restores it to its condition on the day they left it. Then, when the time comes, he says: 'If God wills,' and they dig through it and come out upon the people, drinking up the waters, and the people take refuge in their fortresses. They shoot their arrows at the sky, and they return to them stained like blood. They say: 'We have overcome the people of the earth and prevailed over the people of heaven.' Then God sends upon them a worm in their necks, and it kills them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the beasts of the earth will grow fat and be sated with their flesh.'"

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari then al-Zafari, from Mahmud ibn Labid, brother of Bani Abd al-Ashhal, and from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Yajuj and Majuj will be let loose, and they will come out upon the people, as God the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And they will swarm from every hillock﴾. They will overrun the earth, and the Muslims will withdraw from them to their cities and fortresses, and gather their livestock to themselves. They will drink the waters of the earth, until some of them pass by a river and drink what is in it, until they leave it dry. Then one who comes after them passes by that river and says: 'There was water here once.' Until no one among the people remains except one who has retreated to a fortress or a city. One of them says: 'These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them. Only the people of heaven remain.' Then one of them shakes his spear and throws it toward the sky, and it returns to him stained with blood, as a trial and a tribulation. While they are in that state, God sends upon them a worm in their necks, like the nagaf, and it comes out in their necks, and they become dead in the morning, with no sound from them. The Muslims say: 'Is there a man who will sell himself for us, to look into what the enemy has done?' Then a man from among them strips himself for this, seeking reward for himself, having prepared himself to be killed. He descends and finds them dead, some upon others. He calls out: 'O assembly of Muslims, rejoice, for God has sufficed you against your enemy.' They come out from their cities and fortresses, and release their livestock, and the livestock have no pasture but their flesh, and it is sated by it more than it has ever been sated by any plant it has ever found."

⁕ Bahr ibn Nasr narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Abu al-Zahiriyah and Shurayh ibn Ubayd, that Yajuj and Majuj are three kinds: one kind whose height is like the height of the cedar; another kind whose height and breadth are equal; and another kind, one of whom spreads his ear as a mattress and covers himself with the other, so that it covers his entire body.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿They said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, indeed Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the earth﴾. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri used to say: The Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "No man among them dies until there is born to his loins a thousand men." He said: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud used to marvel at their multitude and say: No one of Yajuj and Majuj dies until there is born to him a thousand men from his loins.

So the report we have mentioned from Wahb ibn Munabbih concerning the story of Yajuj and Majuj indicates that those who said to Dhu al-Qarnayn ﴿Indeed Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the earth﴾ were only informing him of their fear of what would occur from them of corruption in the earth, not that they were complaining of corruption that had already come from them among themselves or among others. The reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) state that corruption will come from them in the earth, and there is no indication in them that corruption had come from them before Dhu al-Qarnayn built the barrier that he built between them and the people beyond them.

Since this is so, as we have explained, the correct interpretation of His words ﴿Indeed Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the earth﴾ is: indeed Yajuj and Majuj will corrupt in the earth.

* *

As for His words ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment (kharj)?﴾

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it as ﴿kharj﴾, as if they took it in the manner of the verbal noun from kharj for the head (i.e., a tax levied per head), meaning its imposition. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as ﴿kharaj﴾ with an alif, as if they took it in the manner of a noun, meaning by it a wage for your building a barrier for us between us and these people.

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who recited it as ﴿kharaj﴾ with an alif, because the people, as is reported of them, only offered Dhu al-Qarnayn that they would give him some of their wealth with which he could aid in building the barrier, and this he made clear in his words ﴿So help me with strength, and I will place between you and them a barrier﴾. They did not offer him a poll-tax on their heads. In the Arabs' usage, kharaj means produce/yield.

And the interpreters have said what we have said.

Those who said this: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment?﴾ He said: a wage.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment?﴾ He said: a wage.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So shall we assign for you a payment?﴾ He said: a wage.

* *

As for His words: ﴿On condition that you make between us and them a barrier﴾

He means: They said to him: Shall we assign for you a payment on condition that you make between us and Yajuj and Majuj an obstacle that will hold them back from us and prevent them from coming out to us? That is the barrier.

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿He said: "That in which my Lord has established me is better; so help me with strength. I will set between you and them a barrier"﴾
