Says the Exalted: Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "That in which my Lord has established me, that is, has enabled me to carry out what you have asked of me, the building of a barrier between you and these people, and has made it easy for me and strengthened me to do it, is better than your tribute and the wage you offer me for building it, and more abundant and finer. But help me with your own strength: help me with workmen and craftsmen who are skilled in building and labour."

As narrated:

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿He said: "That in which my Lord has established me is better; so help me with strength"﴾, he said: "with men." ﴿I will set between you and them a barrier﴾. And he said "ma makkanni," so the one of the two nuns was assimilated into the other; it is actually "ma makkanni fihi" (what He has established me in).

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿I will set between you and them a barrier﴾

It means: I will set between you and Gog and Magog a barrier. The radm (barrier) is a wall or dam, except that it is stronger and firmer than that. It is said of it: "So-and-so has barricaded (radama) the place such-and-such, yardimuhu radman and rudaman" [[al-Rudam: the verbal noun of radama, yardimu (with damma in the imperfect) rudaman: flatulence (from Lisan al-Arab).]]. It is also said: "He patched (raddama) his garment, yuraddimuhu, and it is a garment that is muraddam," when it has many patches. From this is the verse of 'Antara:

Have the poets left any patched place (mutaraddam)? Or do you recognise the abode after doubt?

[[The verse is by 'Antara ibn 'Amr ibn Shaddad al-'Absi, from his well-known mu'allaqa (see it in al-Zawzani's commentary on the Seven Mu'allaqat, al-Tabrizi's commentary on the Ten Odes, and Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, p. 369). Its commentator said: mutaraddam: a place that is mended and repaired for its weakness and its flaw, from their saying: "radamtu al-shay'" when I repaired it and strengthened what had become weak in it. It is also narrated as mutarannam, from tarannum, which is the modulation of the voice with grief. He means: have the poets left a patched place without repairing it, or have the poets left anything without echoing its melodies by composing poetry describing it? The meaning: the earlier one left nothing for the later one. Then he turned away from that and asked himself: have you recognised the abode of your beloved, after your doubt about it? In (Lisan al-Arab, radama): "al-mutaraddam is the place that is patched." It is said: "tarraddama al-rajul thawbahu," meaning he patched his garment; it is transitive and intransitive. Ibn Sidah: "thawb mudram, and murtadam, and mutaraddam, and mulawwam: a patched garment." 'Antara said: "Have the poets left any mutaraddam?" ... the verse." Its meaning is: that which is repaired, i.e., from speech that joins its parts together and fits well: they have preceded us to the pen and left no saying for any speaker.]]

Commentators have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿I will set between you and them a barrier﴾, he said: "It is like the strongest barrier."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: "It was related to us that a man said: 'O Prophet of Allah, I have seen the barrier of Gog and Magog.' He said: 'Describe it to me.' He said: 'It is like a striped cloak (al-burd al-muhabbar), one stripe black and one stripe red.' He said: 'You have seen it.'"

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verses 96–97:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron until, when he had leveled [the gap] between the two cliffs, he said, "Blow," until, when he had made it fire, he said, "Bring me molten copper to pour over it."﴾ (96) ﴿So they were not able to scale it, nor could they make a breach in it.﴾ (97)

He, exalted is His mention, says: Dhul-Qarnayn said to those who had asked him to build a barrier between them and Gog and Magog, ﴿Bring me﴾, that is, bring me ﴿blocks of iron﴾, zubar being the plural of zubra, and a zubra is a piece of iron.

As related:

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿blocks of iron﴾, he said: pieces of iron.

* Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾, he said: pieces of iron.

* Ismaʿil ibn Sayf narrated to me, saying: ʿAli ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Ismaʿil, from Abu Salih, regarding His words ﴿blocks of iron﴾, he said: pieces of iron.

* Muhammad ibn ʿUmara al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: ʿUbaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Israʾil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾, he said: pieces of iron.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾, that is, splitting of iron.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾, he said: pieces of iron.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾, he said: pieces of iron.

* * *

As for His words ﴿until, when he had leveled [the gap] between the two cliffs﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: So they brought blocks of iron, and he placed them between the two cliffs until he had leveled the gap between the two mountains with the blocks of iron he had placed between them. It is said: sawwa (he leveled).

Al-Sadafayn (the two cliffs) refers to the area between the two sides of the mountains and their summits, and from it is the verse of the rajaz poet:

"It has taken what lies between the breadth of the two sadafs, their two sides and the heights of the two corners."

[The two verses are among the witnesses cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Quran (1:414), where he says: "bayn al-sadafayn": some pronounce it with a damma, some with a fatha (the sad doubled), with the dal vowelled. Its sense is what lies between the two sides of the mountains. He said: "qad akhadhat… (the two verses)," without attributing them. In Lisan al-ʿArab (s-d-f): al-sadafan (with fatha) and al-sudafan (with damma) are two mountains meeting, between us and Gog and Magog. In the revealed Book: ḥattā idhā sāwā bayn al-sadafayn — it is read al-sadafayn (with fatha), al-sudafayn, and al-sadfayn (with the first letter vowelled and the second with fatha). A marginal note in Lisan says: "A fourth remains: al-saddafayn, like ʿudwayn, as in al-Qamus." Lisan then says: a hadith reads that the Prophet (ﷺ) would hasten his walk when passing a sadaf or hadaf mail (a slope). Ibn al-Athir: it is with two fathas and two dammas. Abu ʿUbayda said: sadaf and hadaf are one, meaning any tall, great structure. Al-Azhari said: it is like the sadaf of a mountain, likened to it, and it is what faces you from its side.]

Those of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿between the two sadafayn﴾, he said: between the two mountains.

* Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾, he said: it was a barrier that was between two sadafs, and the two sadafs are the two mountains.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, [and another chain] al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿al-sadafayn﴾, he said: the summits of the two mountains.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* I was told by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿between the two sadafayn﴾: meaning the two mountains, which are on the side of Armenia and Adharbayjan.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿until, when he had leveled between the two sadafayn﴾: they are the two mountains.

* Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim informed us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, that he read it ﴿between the two sadafayn﴾ with both the sad and the dal in the accusative, and said: between the two mountains. The Arabs have three dialectal forms for al-sadafayn, and a group of reciters has read each of them:

The fatha on the sad and the dal, which is the recitation of the majority of the reciters of Madina and Kufa; the damma on both, which is the recitation of the people of Basra; and the damma on the sad with a sukun on the dal, which is the recitation of some people of Makka and Kufa. The fatha on both the sad and the dal is the most common of these dialects, and reciting with it is more pleasing to me, though I consider it permissible to recite with all of them, since their meanings agree. I chose the fatha on both for the reason I have mentioned.

As for His words ﴿he said, "Blow"﴾, He, exalted is His mention, says: He said to the workers: blow the fire upon these blocks of iron.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿until, when he had made it fire﴾

In the speech there is an omission, which is: so they blew, until, when he had made what lay between the two cliffs of iron into fire, ﴿he said, "Bring me molten copper to pour over it."﴾ The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madina and Basra, and some people of Kufa, read ﴿qala ātūnī﴾ with the alif of ﴿ātūnī﴾ lengthened, meaning: give me copper that I may pour over it. Some reciters of Kufa read ﴿ituni﴾ with the alif linked, meaning: bring me copper that I may pour over it, as one says: akhadhtu al-khiṭam (I took the halter), akhadhtu bil-khiṭam (I took by the halter), ji'tuka Zaydan (I came to you with Zayd), and jiʾtuka bi-Zayd (I brought you Zayd). This meaning may also be understood, when read thus, as the sense of "give me," so that the reader is as if he intended lengthening the alif of ātūnī, leaving out the first hamza of ātūnī, and when the first is dropped, the second is pronounced with a hamza.

As for His words: ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾

He says: I will pour molten copper over it, and al-qitr is copper.

Those of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾, he said: al-qitr is copper.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾: meaning copper.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾, that is copper, so that it would bind it.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾, he said: copper.

Some of the people of learning in Arabic speech from Basra used to say: al-qitr is molten iron, and in support of this claim he cited the verse of the poet:

"A sword like the colour of salt, clear its iron, cutting, from the pieces of the smelted iron."

[This verse is among the witnesses cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Quran (1:415) in explaining His words ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾, where he says: that is, I will pour over it molten iron, and he cited "ḥusāman… (the verse)," the plural of qiṭr, which some have said is refined silver. In Lisan al-ʿArab (q-t-r): al-qiṭr with a kasra is molten copper, and it is said it is a kind of it. In Lisan (j-r-z): a jarraz sword is cutting; it is said a sword is jarraz when it is uprooting. And al-jarraz among swords is the one that is sharp and piercing.]

* * *

As for His words: ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: So Gog and Magog were not able to ascend the barrier that Dhul-Qarnayn had made as a barrier between them and the people beyond them, so that they could get above it and descend from it to the people.

It is said from this: zahara fulan fawqa al-bayt, meaning he ascended above the house, and from the people's saying: zahara fulan ʿala fulan, meaning he overpowered him and rose above him. ﴿And they could not make a breach in it﴾ means: and they were not able to dig through it from its base.

Those of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, from His words ﴿nor could they make a breach in it﴾, that is, from its base.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, he said: they were not able to pull it down.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, he said: to climb it ﴿nor could they make a breach in it﴾.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, he said: to climb it ﴿nor could they make a breach in it﴾.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, he said: to rise above it ﴿nor could they make a breach in it﴾, that is, to breach it from its base.

The people of Arabic grammar differed over the reason the tā' is dropped from His words ﴿So they were not able﴾. Some grammarians of Basra said: it was done this way because the Arabic usage is to say: asṭaʿa yasṭīʿu, meaning istaṭaʿa yastaṭīʿu, but they dropped the tā' when it was combined with the ṭā', as their articulation point is one. He said: some of them said: istāʿa, dropping the ṭā' for this reason. Some said: asṭaʿa yasṭīʿu, making it from the causative form, as though it were aṭaʿa yuṭīʿu, making the sīn a substitute for the omitted vowel of the wāw. [That is, a substitute for the loss of the vowel of the wāw, as in Lisan.] Some grammarians of Kufa said: this is a form that became common until it was elided.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, [and another chain] al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿al-sadafayn﴾, he said: the summits of the two mountains.

* I was told by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿between the two sadafayn﴾: meaning the two mountains, which are on the side of Armenia and Adharbayjan.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿until, when he had leveled between the two sadafayn﴾: they are the two mountains.

* Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim informed us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, that he read it ﴿between the two sadafayn﴾ with both the sad and the dal in the accusative, and said: between the two mountains. The Arabs have three dialectal forms for al-sadafayn, and a group of reciters has read each of them:

The fatha on the sad and the dal, which is the recitation of the majority of the reciters of Madina and Kufa; the damma on both, which is the recitation of the people of Basra; and the damma on the sad with a sukun on the dal, which is the recitation of some people of Makka and Kufa. The fatha on both the sad and the dal is the most common of these dialects, and reciting with it is more pleasing to me, though I consider it permissible to recite with all of them, since their meanings agree. I chose the fatha on both for the reason I have mentioned.

As for His words ﴿he said, "Blow"﴾, He, exalted is His mention, says: He said to the workers: blow the fire upon these blocks of iron.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿until, when he had made it fire﴾

In the speech there is an omission, which is: so they blew, until, when he had made what lay between the two cliffs of iron into fire, ﴿he said, "Bring me molten copper to pour over it."﴾ The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madina and Basra, and some people of Kufa, read ﴿qala ātūnī﴾ with the alif of ﴿ātūnī﴾ lengthened, meaning: give me copper that I may pour over it. Some reciters of Kufa read ﴿ituni﴾ with the alif linked, meaning: bring me copper that I may pour over it, as one says: akhadhtu al-khiṭam (I took the halter), akhadhtu bil-khiṭam (I took by the halter), ji'tuka Zaydan (I came to you with Zayd), and jiʾtuka bi-Zayd (I brought you Zayd). This meaning may also be understood, when read thus, as the sense of "give me," so that the reader is as if he intended lengthening the alif of ātūnī, leaving out the first hamza of ātūnī, and when the first is dropped, the second is pronounced with a hamza.

As for His words: ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾

He says: I will pour molten copper over it, and al-qitr is copper.

Those of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾, he said: al-qitr is copper.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾: meaning copper.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾, that is copper, so that it would bind it.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾, he said: copper.

Some of the people of learning in Arabic speech from Basra used to say: al-qitr is molten iron, and in support of this claim he cited the verse of the poet:

"A sword like the colour of salt, clear its iron, cutting, from the pieces of the smelted iron."

[This verse is among the witnesses cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Quran (1:415) in explaining His words ﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾, where he says: that is, I will pour over it molten iron, and he cited "ḥusāman… (the verse)," the plural of qiṭr, which some have said is refined silver. In Lisan al-ʿArab (q-t-r): al-qiṭr with a kasra is molten copper, and it is said it is a kind of it. In Lisan (j-r-z): a jarraz sword is cutting; it is said a sword is jarraz when it is uprooting. And al-jarraz among swords is the one that is sharp and piercing.]

* * *

As for His words: ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: So Gog and Magog were not able to ascend the barrier that Dhul-Qarnayn had made as a barrier between them and the people beyond them, so that they could get above it and descend from it to the people.

It is said from this: zahara fulan fawqa al-bayt, meaning he ascended above the house, and from the people's saying: zahara fulan ʿala fulan, meaning he overpowered him and rose above him. ﴿And they could not make a breach in it﴾ means: and they were not able to dig through it from its base.

Those of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, from His words ﴿nor could they make a breach in it﴾, that is, from its base.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, he said: they were not able to pull it down.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, he said: to climb it ﴿nor could they make a breach in it﴾.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, he said: to climb it ﴿nor could they make a breach in it﴾.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, ﴿So they were not able to scale it﴾, he said: to rise above it ﴿nor could they make a breach in it﴾, that is, to breach it from its base.

The people of Arabic grammar differed over the reason the tā' is dropped from His words ﴿So they were not able﴾. Some grammarians of Basra said: it was done this way because the Arabic usage is to say: asṭaʿa yasṭīʿu, meaning istaṭaʿa yastaṭīʿu, but they dropped the tā' when it was combined with the ṭā', as their articulation point is one. He said: some of them said: istāʿa, dropping the ṭā' for this reason. Some said: asṭaʿa yasṭīʿu, making it from the causative form, as though it were aṭaʿa yuṭīʿu, making the sīn a substitute for the omitted vowel of the wāw. [That is, a substitute for the loss of the vowel of the wāw, as in Lisan.] Some grammarians of Kufa said: this is a form that became common until it was elided.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 98:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿He said, "This is a mercy from my Lord. But when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true."﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When Dhu al-Qarnayn saw that Ya'juj and Ma'juj could not reach the top of the barrier he had built, nor were able to breach it, he said: "This that I have built and made into a barrier between this nation and them is a mercy from my Lord, who has shown mercy by it to the people beyond the barrier. He aided me with His mercy toward them until I built it and leveled it, so that it would restrain the harm of this nation from them."

* *

As for His words ﴿But when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level﴾

He says: When the promise of my Lord comes, which He has appointed as the appointed time for the emergence of this nation and their coming forth from behind this barrier to them, He will make it level (dakka'), meaning He will make it even with the ground and stick it to it. This is from their saying "a dakka' camel" (naqa dakka'), meaning one whose back is level with no hump. The meaning of the statement is: He will make it crushed (madkukan), and so it was called dakka'.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿When the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level﴾, he said: "I do not know whether it refers to the two mountains or to what lies between them."

It has been mentioned that this will happen after the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, kills the Dajjal.

Report concerning this: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to me, saying: Hushaym ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: al-Awwam informed us, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Mu'thir, who is Ibn 'Affarah al-'Abdi, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the night of the Night Journey I met Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa, and they discussed the matter of the Hour. They referred the matter to Ibrahim, and Ibrahim said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' So they referred the matter to Musa, and Musa said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' So they referred the matter to 'Isa. 'Isa said: 'As for the establishment of the Hour, none knows it but Allah. But my Lord has covenanted with me concerning what will occur before its time: He has covenanted with me that the Dajjal will emerge, and that I will descend to him.' He mentioned that he would have two lances, and when he sees me, Allah will destroy him. He said: 'He will melt as lead melts, until even the stone and the tree will say: O Muslim, this is a disbeliever, so kill him. Allah will destroy them, and the people will return to their lands and homelands. Then Ya'juj and Ma'juj will confront them, swarming from every elevation. They will leave nothing behind without devouring it, and they will not pass by any water without drinking it. The people will come to me and complain of them, and I will supplicate Allah against them, and He will cause them to die, until the earth reeks from the stench of them. Then rain will fall and carry their bodies away and cast them into the sea. Then He will blow away the mountains until the earth becomes like a leveled hide. My Lord has covenanted with me that when that occurs, the Hour will be upon them like a pregnant woman near her term, whose family does not know when she will surprise them with her birth, by night or by day.'"

Ubayd ibn Isma'il narrated to me, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Asbagh ibn Zayd, from al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Mu'thir ibn 'Affarah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, he, Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa, peace be upon them, met. They discussed the matter of the Hour. He then mentioned something similar to the report of Ibrahim al-Dawraqi from Hushaym, and he added in it: al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab said: "I found confirmation of this in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, Allah says: ﴿until, when Ya'juj and Ma'juj are let loose, and they swarm from every elevation, and the true promise draws near, then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾, and He says: ﴿When the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true﴾." He means: the promise of my Lord which He promised to His creation, concerning the leveling of this barrier, the emergence of these people upon the people, their corruption among them, and other of His promises, is true, for He does not break the appointment, so nothing occurs other than what He promised would occur.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a gathering﴾ [18:99]

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We will leave Our servants on the day when the promise We made them comes to them, that We will level the mountains, blow them away from the earth in a blowing, and leave the earth as a level plain without any valleys or heights, ﴿surging over one another﴾, meaning: the jinn and the humans will mix together.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, from Harun ibn Antarah, from a shaykh of the Banu Fazara, concerning His saying ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another﴾, he said: When the jinn and the humans surge, Iblis says: "I know for you the knowledge of this matter." So he sets off toward the east, and finds that the angels have already traversed the earth. Then he sets off toward the west, and finds that the angels have already traversed the earth. Then he climbs right and left to the farthest end of the earth, and finds that the angels have traversed the earth. So he says: "There is no escape." While he is in this state, a path appears to him like a thong (shirak), so he takes it, he and his offspring. While they are on it, they suddenly come upon the Fire. Then God brings forth a guardian from the guardians of the Fire, who says: "O Iblis, did you not have a rank with your Lord? Were you not in the Gardens?" He says: "This is not a day of reproach. If God had imposed upon me an obligation, I would have worshipped Him in it with a worship that none of His creation worshipped like it." The guardian says: "Indeed God has imposed upon you an obligation." He says: "What is it?" The guardian says: "He orders you to enter the Fire." So he hesitates before it, [[yuqal: meaning he pushes it and moves it.]] and then with his two wings he pushes him and his offspring, and casts them into the Fire. The Fire then heaves a roar, and no angel brought near nor prophet sent remains except that he falls to his knees.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another﴾: This is the beginning of the Resurrection. Then the Horn is blown after that, ﴿and We will gather them in a gathering﴾.

﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾ We have already mentioned the difference of opinion among the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) earlier concerning the Ṣūr, what it is, and what is meant by it.

We have chosen the correct view on this matter, with its evidences that make repeating it in this place unnecessary; however, we mention here some of the reports that we did not mention in that place.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, saying: Aslam related to us, from Bishr ibn Shaghaf, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that a Bedouin asked him about the Ṣūr, and he said: "It is a horn in which one blows."

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham related to us, from Sufyan, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from al-Ajli, from Bishr ibn Shaghaf, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording.

Muhammad ibn al-Harith al-Qantari related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr related to us, saying: I was at the funeral of Umar ibn Dharr, and I met Malik ibn Mighwal, and he related to us from Atiyya al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease when the holder of the horn has put it to his mouth, bowed his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded?" This weighed heavily on the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so he said: "Say: Sufficient for us is God, and upon God we rely; and even if the people of Mina gathered to lift that horn, they could not lift it." Thus he said, though it is actually "ma aqallu" (they could not lift).

Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Hafs related to us, from al-Hajjaj, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth, bowed his back, and fixed his eyes?" They said: "What should we say, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Say: Sufficient for us is God; we rely upon God."

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Mutarrif, from Atiyya, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth, bowed his forehead, listening for when he will be commanded to blow into it?" The companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "How then should we say?" He said: "Say: Sufficient for us is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs; upon God we rely."

Abu Kurayb and al-Hasan ibn Arafa related to us, both saying: Asbat related to us, from Mutarrif, from Atiyya, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Shu'ayb ibn Harb related to us, saying: Khalid Abu al-Ala' related to us, saying: Atiyya al-Awfi related to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth and bowed his forehead, inclining his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow? And even if the people of Mina gathered together to lift the horn from the earth, they would not be able to." He said: The companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were dumbfounded, and it weighed on them. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Say: Sufficient for us is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs; upon God we rely."

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi related to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Fulan, from a man of the Ansar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Ṣūr and gave it to Israfil. He placed it at his mouth, his gaze fixed on the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded." Abu Hurayra said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Ṣūr?" He said: "A horn." He said: "And what is it like?" He said: "A great horn into which three blasts will be blown: The first: the blast of terror (fazaʿ); the second: the blast of swooning (ṣaʿq); and the third: the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds."

* *

And His saying ﴿and We gathered them in a gathering﴾

He says: We gathered all creation at that time for the place of reckoning, all together.

* *

And His saying ﴿And We will present Hell that day to the disbelievers, a presentation﴾ [18:100]

He says: We will bring forth Hell on the day the Horn is blown, and We will make it manifest to the disbelievers in God, so that they see it and witness it like a mirage. If the verb were attributed to it, one would say "a'radat" (it appeared) when it becomes clear. As 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

"And al-Yamama appeared and rose high, like swords in the hands of bared men."

[[The verse is from the Mu'allaqa of Amr ibn Kulthum al-Taghlibi (in Jamharat ash'ar al-'Arab, pp. 74–84, and in the commentaries of al-Zawzuni and al-Tabrizi on the Mu'allaqat). "A'radat": appeared; "'aradtu al-shay'": I made the thing appear, and from it the verse "And We presented Hell that day to the disbelievers, a presentation." This is among the rare usages: "'aradtu al-shay' fa-a'rada" (I made the thing appear, so it appeared), like "kabbabtuhu fa-akabba" (I overturned it, so it toppled). "Ashmakharrat": grew tall and rose. The meaning: it appeared extended. The kaf in "ka-asyaf" is in the accusative position, as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun. "Al-musallit" is one who brandishes his sword; one says "asallat al-saif" when he draws it. The meaning: the villages of al-Yamama appeared to us and rose in our eyes like swords in the hands of men drawing their swords, so the simile was made for what we saw of their destination. The evidence is in "a'radat" meaning "appeared."]]

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said in accordance with what we have said.

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Shu'ayb ibn Harb related to us, saying: Khalid Abu al-Ala' related to us, saying: Atiyya al-Awfi related to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth and bowed his forehead, inclining his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow? And even if the people of Mina gathered together to lift the horn from the earth, they would not be able to." He said: The companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were dumbfounded, and it weighed on them. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Say: Sufficient for us is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs; upon God we rely."

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi related to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Fulan, from a man of the Ansar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Ṣūr and gave it to Israfil. He placed it at his mouth, his gaze fixed on the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded." Abu Hurayra said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Ṣūr?" He said: "A horn." He said: "And what is it like?" He said: "A great horn into which three blasts will be blown: The first: the blast of terror (fazaʿ); the second: the blast of swooning (ṣaʿq); and the third: the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds."

* *

And His saying ﴿and We gathered them in a gathering﴾

He says: We gathered all creation at that time for the place of reckoning, all together.

* *

And His saying ﴿And We will present Hell that day to the disbelievers, a presentation﴾ [18:100]

He says: We will bring forth Hell on the day the Horn is blown, and We will make it manifest to the disbelievers in God, so that they see it and witness it like a mirage. If the verb were attributed to it, one would say "a'radat" (it appeared) when it becomes clear. As 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

"And al-Yamama appeared and rose high, like swords in the hands of bared men."

[[The verse is from the Mu'allaqa of Amr ibn Kulthum al-Taghlibi (in Jamharat ash'ar al-'Arab, pp. 74–84, and in the commentaries of al-Zawzuni and al-Tabrizi on the Mu'allaqat). "A'radat": appeared; "'aradtu al-shay'": I made the thing appear, and from it the verse "And We presented Hell that day to the disbelievers, a presentation." This is among the rare usages: "'aradtu al-shay' fa-a'rada" (I made the thing appear, so it appeared), like "kabbabtuhu fa-akabba" (I overturned it, so it toppled). "Ashmakharrat": grew tall and rose. The meaning: it appeared extended. The kaf in "ka-asyaf" is in the accusative position, as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun. "Al-musallit" is one who brandishes his sword; one says "asallat al-saif" when he draws it. The meaning: the villages of al-Yamama appeared to us and rose in our eyes like swords in the hands of men drawing their swords, so the simile was made for what we saw of their destination. The evidence is in "a'radat" meaning "appeared."]]

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said in accordance with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, saying: Abu al-Za'ra' related to us, from Abdullah, who said: "The creation will stand before God when the Horn is blown, standing as one man. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, will manifest Himself to the creation, and no creature that worshipped anything besides God will meet Him without it being raised before him and following him. He will meet the Jews and say: 'Whom do you worship?' They will say: 'We worship 'Uzayr.' He will say: 'Would you like water?' They will say: 'Yes.' So He will show them Hell, which appears like a mirage." Then he recited: ﴿And We will present Hell that day to the disbelievers, a presentation﴾. "Then He will meet the Christians and say: 'Whom do you worship?' They will say: 'We worship the Messiah.' He will say: 'Would you like water?' They will say: 'Yes.' He will show them Hell, which appears like a mirage. Likewise for whoever worshipped anything besides God." Then Abdullah recited: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [37:24].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 101:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those whose eyes were in a covering from My remembrance, and who were not able to hear﴾ (18:101).

He, exalted is He, says: We presented Hell on that Day to the disbelievers who used not to look into the signs of God, so that they would reflect upon them and not contemplate His proofs, whereby they would take heed, be mindful, and turn in repentance to the Oneness of God, and submit to His command and His prohibition. "And who were not able to hear" means: they were unable to bear hearing the remembrance of God with which He reminded them, and His clarification which He made clear to them in the verses of His Book, owing to God's forsaking them, the domination of wretchedness over them, and their preoccupation with disbelief in God and obedience to Satan, so that they would be admonished by it, reflect upon it, and thereby recognize guidance from error and disbelief from faith.

And Mujahid used to say concerning this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying ﴿they were not able to hear﴾: he said, "They do not understand."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid ﴿and who were not able to hear﴾: he said, "They do not know."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿Those whose eyes were in a covering from My remembrance﴾, "the verse," he said: "These are the people of disbelief."

On the words of His Majesty, "Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as protectors besides Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers" (18:102):

He, mighty is His remembrance, says: Do those who disbelieve in Allah, from among the worshippers of the angels and the Messiah, think that they may take My servants, whom they worshipped besides Allah, as protectors? He says: No indeed, rather they are enemies to them.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words "Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as protectors besides Me?" He said: He means those who worship the Messiah son of Mary and the angels, and they are servants of Allah, and they were not protectors for the disbelievers.

With this reading, meaning with the sin of "أفحسب" pronounced with a kasra in the sense of "to think" (zann), the readers of the major cities (qurra' al-amsar) recited this letter. It is also transmitted from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), Ikrimah, and Mujahid that they recited it as "أَفَحَسِبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا" with the sin pronounced sukun (silent) and the letter after it raised (ḥasbu), in the sense: "Is it enough for them that they take My servants besides Me as protectors, from among My worship and My allegiance?"

As:

It was related to me from Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq, from Imran ibn Hudayr, from Ikrimah, "أَفَحَسِبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا" he said: "Is it enough for them that...?" The reading we recite is the reading upon which the readers of the major cities agree, "أَفَحَسِبَ الَّذِينَ" with a kasra on the sin, in the sense of "afazanna" (do they think), due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

As for His words, "Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers" (18:102):

He says: We have prepared Hell as a dwelling (manzil) for those who disbelieve in Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verses 103–104:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"  Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing well in work.﴾

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these people who seek to trouble you and dispute with you in falsehood, and who question you with problems, from the People of the Two Books: the Jews and the Christians, ﴿"Shall We inform you"﴾, O people, ﴿"of the greatest losers in deeds"﴾, meaning: of those who exhausted themselves in work by which they sought profit and bounty, but who gained destruction and ruin thereby and did not attain what they sought, like the buyer of a commodity who hopes through it for gain and profit, but whose hope is disappointed, whose sale is a loss, and who is cheated in what he hoped would bring him gain.

The people of interpretation differed concerning those who were meant by this. Some of them said: It refers to the monks and the priests.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Muqbiri narrated to us, saying: Haywah ibn Shurayh narrated to us, saying: al-Sakan ibn Abi Karima informed me that his mother told him that she heard Abu Khumaysa Abdullah ibn Qays say: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib say concerning this verse, ﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"﴾, "They are the monks who confined themselves in the monasteries."

* Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Haywah say: al-Sakan ibn Abi Karima narrated to me, from his mother, who told him that she heard Abdullah ibn Qays say: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib say, and he mentioned something similar.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Musab ibn Sa'd, who said: I said to my father, concerning ﴿and they think that they are doing well in work﴾: Are they the Haruriyya? He said: They are the people of the monasteries.

* Fadala ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Bazi' said: A man asked al-Dahhak about this verse, ﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"﴾ He said: They are the priests (qissisun) and the monks.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Musab ibn Sa'd, who said: Sa'd said: They are the people of the monasteries.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibn Sa'd, who said: I said to Sa'd: O father, ﴿Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ Are they the Haruriyya? He said: No, but they are the people of the monasteries. As for the Haruriyya, they are a people who deviated, so God caused their hearts to deviate.

Others said: Rather, they are all of the People of the Two Books.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murra, from Musab ibn Sa'd, who said: I asked my father about this verse, ﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world"﴾: Are they the Haruriyya? He said: No, they are the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad. As for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise and said: There is no food or drink in it. But the Haruriyya are ﴿those who break the covenant of God after its ratification, and sever what God has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on the earth; those are the losers﴾. Sa'd used to call them the wicked.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Hurra, from Musab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, concerning His saying, ﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"﴾, he said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Zadhan, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he was asked about His saying, ﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"﴾ He said: They are the disbelievers among the People of the Book. Their early ones were upon the truth, but they associated others with their Lord and innovated in their religion, striving in falsehood while thinking that they were upon the truth, striving in misguidance while thinking that they were upon guidance. ﴿Their effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing well in work.﴾ Then he raised his voice and said: ﴿And they are not far from the Fire.﴾

Others said: Rather, they are the Kharijites.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Salama, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about His saying, ﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"﴾ He said: You, O people of Harura'.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Sakhr, from Abu Mu'awiya al-Bajali, from Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, that Ibn al-Kawwa asked him about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ Ali said: You and your companions.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa stood up before Ali and said: ﴿Who are the greatest losers in deeds, those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think that they are doing well in work?﴾ He said: Woe to you, the people of Harura' are among them.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn 'Ashma [[She is the mother of Muhammad, and Khalid is his father, so the alif must be written.]] narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ya'qub ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Huwayrith narrated to me, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa said to Ali ibn Abi Talib: Who are the greatest losers in deeds, those whose effort is lost in the life of this world? He said: You and your companions.

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that it is said: God, Mighty and Majestic, by His saying ﴿Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ means every doer who performs a deed that he thinks himself correct in, and that by his doing that he is obedient to God, though he is in fact displeasing to Him, and by his doing that he is in deviation from the path of the people of faith in Him, like the monks, the shammasa, and their likes, from among the people of striving in their misguidance. Along with that, by their deeds and striving, they are disbelievers in God, whatever religion they belong to.

The grammarians differed concerning the reason for the accusative case of His saying ﴿a'mālan﴾ (in deeds). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is in the accusative because, when the alif, lam and nun were attached to al-akhsirīn, it could not be put in the genitive construction (idafa), and the deeds are the thing in which they are "greatest losers," so it is accusative for that reason. Another said: This is the category of af'al and fu'lā, like al-afḍal and al-fuḍlā, and al-akhsar and al-khusrā, and the waw does not enter into it, and it does not take an explanatory noun, because it is already separated by "min" (than), as in His saying "al-afḍal" and "al-fuḍlā." When an explanatory noun comes with it, it is for the first and the last. He said: Do you not see that you say: "I passed by a man handsome in face," so that "handsome" applies to the man and the face? Likewise "great in intellect" and what resembles it. He said: It was permissible with al-akhsirīn only because he returned it to af'al and af'ala (the pattern of the plural). He said: I heard the Arabs say: "al-awwalāt dukhūlan wa-l-ākhirāt khurūjan" (the first in entering and the last in leaving), so it became for the first and the second like the rest of the category. He said: And on this one analogizes.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world﴾

It means: they are those whose work which they did in their worldly life was not upon guidance and uprightness, but upon injustice and misguidance; this is because they worked other than what God had commanded them, indeed upon disbelief in Him. ﴿And they think that they are doing well in work﴾: that is, they suppose that by that deed they are obedient to God, and striving in what He urged His servants toward. This is one of the clearest proofs against the error of the one who claims that no one disbelieves in God except one who intends disbelief knowingly after knowledge of His oneness. For God, the Exalted, informed concerning these people described in this verse that their effort which they exerted in the world went astray, and that they had been thinking they were doing well in that work; and He informed that they are those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord. If the matter were as those who claim that no one disbelieves in God except knowingly said, it would necessarily follow that these people, in the deed about which God informed that they thought they were doing well, would be rewarded and recompensed for it. But the matter is contrary to what they said; so He, whose praise is great, informed concerning them that they are disbelievers in God, and that their deeds are void.

By His saying ﴿that they are doing well in work﴾, He means "deed." Al-sun', al-sani'a and al-sana' are one and the same; it is said: a "sanī'" horse, meaning "mas'nū'" (made, crafted).

For God, the Exalted, informed concerning these people described in this verse that their effort which they exerted in the world went astray, and that they had been thinking they were doing well in that work; and He informed that they are those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord. If the matter were as those who claim that no one disbelieves in God except knowingly said, it would necessarily follow that these people, in the deed about which God informed that they thought they were doing well, would be rewarded and recompensed for it. But the matter is contrary to what they said; so He, whose praise is great, informed concerning them that they are disbelievers in God, and that their deeds are void.

By His saying ﴿that they are doing well in work﴾, He means "deed." Al-sun', al-sani'a and al-sana' are one and the same; it is said: a "sanī'" horse, meaning "mas'nū'" (made, crafted).

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds have become worthless, and We will not assign them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (18:105).

He, exalted is His mention, says: Those whose description We have given, the greatest losers in deeds, are those who disbelieved in the proofs (ḥujaj) and evidences of their Lord and denied meeting Him. ﴿So their deeds have become worthless﴾ means: their deeds have been nullified, so there is no reward for them that benefits their doers in the Hereafter; rather, for them there is punishment and lasting disgrace from them. ﴿So We will not assign them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — He, exalted is His mention, says: We will not give them any weight. What is meant by this is that their scales will not be made heavy by them, because the scales are made heavy only by righteous deeds, and these people have none of the righteous deeds by which their scales would be made heavy.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Recite: ﴿So We will not assign them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Sallat narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from Salih, mawla of al-Tawama, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A great eater and drinker will be brought, and he will be weighed, and he will not weigh the wing of a gnat." **The explanation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise (al-Firdaws) as their lodging. They will abide therein forever; they will not desire any removal from them.﴾ [18:107-108]**

His statement, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger, acknowledged the Oneness of Allah and what He sent down in His Books, and acted in obedience to Him, will have the gardens of al-Firdaws. Al-Firdaws is the main part of Paradise, as Umayya said:

*"Their dwellings were then clearly visible, / in them were al-faradis, al-fuwman and onions."* [[The verse is by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi (al-Lisan, root f-w-m). He said: Umayya said, using the plural of fum: "There was for them a garden then, clearly visible..." the verse. He said: It is also narrated as "al-fararis." Abu al-Asba' said: al-fararis is onion. Al-Zajjaj said: al-fum is wheat, and it is also said grains in general. There is no disagreement among the lexicographers that fum means wheat and all grains that are baked, which take the name fum. He said: Whoever says that fum here means garlic, this is not known. Abu Mansur said: If Ibn Mas'ud read it with the letter thaʾ, its meaning is fum, which is wheat. In (al-Lisan, root f-r-d-s): al-firdaws is an orchard. Al-Farra' said: It is Arabic. Ibn Sayyida said: al-firdaws is a fertile valley according to the Arabs, an orchard; in the language of the Romans it is an orchard. Al-Firdaws is a meadow, according to al-Sirafi. Al-Firdaws is the greenness of grapevines. Al-Zajjaj said: Its reality is that it is the orchard that gathers what is found in orchards, and so it is in the language of every people. Al-Firdaws is a garden in Paradise. Al-Firdaws originally is a Roman word that became Arabized, and it means orchard.]]

The scholars of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., explanation of meaning) differed regarding the meaning of al-Firdaws. Some of them said: It refers to the best and the central part of Paradise.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abbas ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, who said: Al-Firdaws is the elevated part of Paradise, its middle and its best.

- Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj al-Razi narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham Abu Bishr narrated to us, saying: al-Faraj ibn Fudala informed us, from Luqman, from ʿAmir, who said: Abu Usama was asked about al-Firdaws, and he said: It is the navel of Paradise.

- Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn ʿAmr al-Nasibi narrated to us, from Abu ʿAli, from Kaʿb, who said: There is no garden higher than the Garden of al-Firdaws among the gardens, and in it are those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.

Others said: It is the orchard in Roman (Byzantine) language.

Those who said this:

- ʿAli ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, who said: Al-Firdaws is an orchard in the Roman language.

- al-ʿAbbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, who said: Ibn Jurayj informed me, from ʿAbd Allah, from Mujahid, similarly.

Others said: It is the orchard in which there are grapevines.

- ʿAbbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Kaʿb, who said: The gardens of al-Firdaws are those in which there are grapevines.

The correct view on this matter is that which is supported by the reports transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

That is what:

- Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us with it, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Paradise has one hundred levels; between every two levels is a distance of a year's journey. Al-Firdaws is the highest of them in level, and from it issue the four rivers, and al-Firdaws is above them. So when you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws."

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Fulayh narrated to us, from Hilal, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi ʿAmra, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly, except that he said: "the middle of Paradise," and he also said: "and from it gush forth, or it gushes forth."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 109:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.﴾ (18:109)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad: ﴿If the sea were ink﴾ for the pen with which one writes ﴿for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely be exhausted, [the water of the sea], before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.﴾ He means: even if We supplied the sea with the like of the water that is in it as a supplement, from the saying of the speaker, "I came to you as a supplement (madadan) for you," and that is from the meaning of increase.

It has been reported from some of them: "even if We brought the like of it as a supplement (madadan)", as if the reader of it in this way intended: the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We added the like of what is in it of ink with which to write, as ink (midadan).

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, (ḥ) and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿the sea as ink for the words of my Lord﴾: "for the pen."

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn al-Barqi related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Ibn al-Darawardi informed us, both saying: Zayd ibn Aslam related to us, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Paradise has one hundred levels, each level of which is like the distance between the heaven and the earth; the highest level of it is al-Firdaws."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Ta'i related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samura ibn Jundab, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Al-Firdaws is from the elevated part of Paradise; it is its middle and its best."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Muslim informed us, from al-Hasan, from Samura ibn Jundab, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed us: "Indeed al-Firdaws is the highest part of Paradise, its best and its loftiest."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Marzuq related to me, saying: Rawh ibn Ubadah related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said to al-Rabi' daughter of al-Nadr: "O Umm Harithah, indeed it is gardens, and indeed your son has attained al-Firdaws al-A'la." And al-Firdaws: the elevated part of Paradise, its middle and its most excellent.

* *

And His saying: ﴿nuzulan﴾ (a lodging)

He says: dwellings and residences. The manzil (dwelling) is from nuzul (descent/lodging), which is from the lodging of some people with others.

As for the nuzl (provision/hospitality): it is the feast (rif'), as one says: "What is this food of yours a nuzl?" meaning a feast; and "We did not find with you any nuzl," i.e., any lodging.

* *

And His saying: ﴿abiding therein﴾ (khalidina)

He says: remaining in them forever, ﴿they shall not desire any removal therefrom﴾ (la yabghuna 'anha hiwalan): He says: they do not wish to transfer from them. It is a verbal noun of tahawwala (to change/transfer), returned to its original root, as one says: sagira yasgaru sagaran, and 'aja ya'uju 'awajan.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿they shall not desire any removal therefrom﴾: "seeking any change (mutahawwilan)."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord﴾: he says: then the water of the sea would be exhausted before the words and decrees of Allah were exhausted.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 110:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your god is but one God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord."﴾ (18:110)

His saying, exalted is He mention: Say to these polytheists, O Muhammad: "I am only a human being like you, from the children of Adam. I have no knowledge except what Allah has taught me, and Allah reveals to me that your deity, whom you must worship and not associate anything with Him, is one God with no second and no partner." ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾ means: whoever fears his Lord on the Day of meeting Him, watches over himself regarding His disobedience, and hopes for His reward for obedience to Him. ﴿Let him do righteous deeds﴾ means: let him make his worship sincerely for Him and single Him out in lordship.

And the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said similarly to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Abi Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾, he said: "The reward of his Lord."

* *

And His saying ﴿and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾

means: and let him not make a partner for Him in his worship of Him. He only becomes one who makes a partner for Him in worship when he shows off with his deed, which outwardly is for Allah, while he intends by it other than Him.

And the people of ta'wil have said similarly to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: (and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord) [[As in manuscript no. 100 Tafsir, Dar al-Kutub al-Misriyya; and in al-Durr, from Sa'id: "Not associate": not show off in the worship of his Lord to anyone.]]

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us: ﴿and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾, he said: "He does not show off."

al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Tawus, who said: A man came and said: "O Prophet of Allah, I love to fight in the way of Allah, and I love that my standing place and my position be seen," so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.﴾"

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid and Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji, from Sadaqa ibn Yasar, who said: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned something similar, and added in it: 'I perform deeds and give charity, and I love that people see it.' And the rest of the hadith is similar."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from al-A'mash, who said: Hamza Abu 'Amara, client of the Banu Hashim, narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: "A man came to 'Ubada ibn al-Samit and asked him, saying: 'Inform me about what I ask you: Do you see a man who prays seeking the face of Allah, and loves to be praised, and fasts seeking the face of Allah, and loves to be praised?' 'Ubada said: 'He has nothing. Allah, mighty and majestic, says: I am the best partner. Whoever has a partner with Me, it is all for that partner; I have no need of it.'"

Abu 'Amir Isma'il ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays al-Kindi narrated to us, that he heard Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan recite this verse: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾, and said: "It is the last verse revealed of the Qur'an."

End of the commentary on Surah al-Kahf.
